lines.st: ...As much as we value the young, youth is never an excuse for crime and depravity.
In Ursus, children younger than them are already contributing to the empire in their respective ways; in the armies, in the factories, in the mines.
It is only the rich, spoiled students who cry foul at those who tell them to rein in their babbling mouths, as though Ursus would fall if they stopped talking for a moment.

They have never seen battle nor borne the weight of their comrades on their shoulders, yet they read their newspapers and play with their sandboxes and maps, dreaming of encirclements and flanking maneuvers, of 'victory at any cost'.

They have never spent a moment working the factories, or watching the desperate workers when a production line is halted in the middle of the night, yet they fool themselves with slogans like 'double the pay, double the production'.
They flock into the birch forests, writing sorry poems that would have you believe their lives were more pathetic than the miners of the Far North.

Their views are based on their shallow understanding of the land around them. They appropriate the words of their forebears to support their fallacies, repeating themselves over and over to convince those foolish enough to hold such views.
The only mistake of this council is its continued indulgence and restraint. It has gained nothing but their scorn and hatred, and birthed these outcomes.
I maintain that this hearing is completely redundant, because the nature of the incident at issue is clear.
The students are attempting to undermine Ursine order. They have taken up arms and broken down the walls of the containment zone. This is no less than premediated insurrection.

lines.x:
As for their 'leader', this so-called 'The General'—
—This Sonya Mikhailivna.
She is a traitor to Ursus, plain and simple.
Your opinion is respected, Count Yusupov, but we cannot make a determination as to these students until the hearing is concluded.
I will once again remind all present that the outcome of this hearing will define the Katorga Incident.
This atrocity that took place in our magnificent Grypherburg must be judged fairly and solemnly.
And we must ensure a fair outcome for the future of Ursus, these students living in Grypherburg.
Your Honor, I must remind you before we begin...
The actions of these students that currently stand outside the council building have tarnished the dignity of Ursus.
The emblem of our empire hangs above your head. It reminds us all from whence the glory of Ursus arises, the glory in which all her people bathe.
As the Grypherburg of old belongs likewise to the emperors of old, the present and future belong to His Reigning Majesty, and to all of us who execute Ursus's will on his behalf.
If we fail to try Sonya Mykhailivna and her accomplices for treason, we are handing the future over to the lazy, unproductive dregs of society.
How, then, could Ursus hold her head high upon this land? How could His Imperial Majesty's justice be upheld?
Justice? How dare you speak of His Majesty's justice?
No lawyers, no prosecutors, no juries... the motion to establish a statute has been on the agenda for more than a decade. The old guard like you are the only reason it hasn't been passed!
And what have the new blood like you done for the empire? You've bought your titles with chervontsy, yet you consort with traitors...
How dare you adorn your chest with the medals conferred upon you by His Imperial Majesty, when you step up from those protesting students outside to wax lyrical here. Have you no shame?
Meanwhile, outside the council building.
Damned kids...
He was supposed to be off-duty today.
That is, until he got an urgent call while sleeping in his room, and was told that students from all over Grypherburg are on the streets, blocking every route to the council building.
He and his colleagues mobilized for war, yet when they came on the scene...
They found no flags, no shouting, only students standing on the streets quietly.
They give way when police or officials show up, allowing them to enter the 'siege'.
...Huh?
Stop right there! What are you doing?
Remain calm, sir. We mean no disrespect. We're only here to support our fellow students.
But some dignitaries have promised to speak at the hearing, and now they are nowhere to be seen.
May I ask if the police have them in custody? We can't allow the hearing to begin without them—
I don't know what you're talking about! This is none of your business!
Now, get back!
Where are our people? Why are there so many absences?
Have the old fools detained our witnesses to give themselves an advantage?
Order!
The police have been mobilized to maintain order in Grypherburg, given the circumstances. Traffic disruption may cause delays.
However, this matter can permit no further delay. While you were arguing, our first witnessed arrived.
The bickering belligerents turn to the door, their anger replaced with curiosity as they watch the Ursus woman enter the hall.
Please take your seats. Let the proceedings commence, in the name of His Imperial Majesty's justice...
Witness, proceed to the stand.
This is a friend of Sonya Mykhailivna?
Yes. They say the new nobility vouched for her. As long as she plays her part and testifies as agreed, her friend will get off easy.
But that's not the outcome we want to see...
Relax. I want to see how much weight these commoners' words carry.
Thank you for testifying, Young Zoya.
I'm sure you have noticed the police equipment that Zoya carries.
Her father was a respected Ursine policeman, who gave his life at Chernobog to protect the empire's order. I am sure she carries on her father's loyalty to the land.
As an eyewitness to the Katorga Incident, she was questioned several days ago, and submitted a report regarding the matter.
The committee will now read the report and cross-examine the witness. I believe this report will give all of us a better understanding of the Katorga Incident.
Young Zoya, do you attest to the truthfulness of this document, and to the statements that you will give at this hearing?
I do, Your Honor.
Your Honor, we request the hearing be postponed.
Young Zoya's guarantor, Baron Kamshalov, has not yet arrived. The baron's honor is at stake when she testifies. She must not be allowed to do so in his absence.
Hah, everyone knows Baron Kamshalov likes to sleep in. Are we to postpone the hearing permanently, when he never wakes up?
I am unaware that he has any such habit.
You think his casinos operate in the daylight? He does his business late at night.
You may both be barons now, but he had already made more money than you will in two lifetimes by the time you were just a private in the army.
But he wasn't there last night—

Someone beside him grabs him, and he stops himself mid-sentence, sweating profusely from his forehead. He can hardly admit in public that he and other friends in high places spent last night in an illegal casino.
Oh?
If he wasn't at the casino last night, maybe you should ask your wife—
Say that again, mudak!
The furious noble jumps across a few rows of seats to get at the other.
Police! Separate them!
The arbiter's shouting ignites a council hall that was already on the brink of inferno, with several who were already arguing joining the fray.
The few policemen in the room walk up and motion to try to separate them, but stop short of touching anyone. All the belligerents are too important for them to risk angering.

Absinthe closes her eyes and touches the back of her neck. For a moment there, she thinks it might be the air stirred by the swinging of fists that is making her feel cold, not the behavior of the nobles once again going beyond the pale.
In her mind, she seems to hear the words that every person in Ursus has heard a thousand times.

lines.st: You want to destroy Ursus?
I say...
You're the reason Ursus is what it is!

lines.x: ...You're the reason Ursus is what it is!
So much the better! Do we dare to imagine the empire if you were guiding her?
They grab each other by the collar, while the onlooking students seem to have no intention of stopping then, instead cheering them on in eager anticipation of a good show.
Several students sit quietly in the rear, away from the crowd.
*Sigh*...
Is Sonya not here yet?
Reviewing the correspondence, Sonya should be here this afternoon, and Instructor Dur-nar tomorrow.
But the discussion has meandered onto a tangent. Should we intervene before things get out of hand?
We're participating in a student gathering under the banner of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group, with Sonya as our leader. I doubt anyone will listen to us without her present.
Besides, the issues being discussed here are important. We need her to make decisions.
But I recall that Sonya did not part on the best of terms with Olga's group—
That's the last honey drop, Leto!
You're the kindest and sweetest, Gummy. Maybe there's another hidden somewhere in your pocket?
Don't pick on Gummy over a piece of candy, Leto.
It's because you wouldn't let me drink honey... I haven't had a sip since I got back to Ursus.
I should've stayed in Kjerag.
We're not here on vacation... you can have all the honey you want once we complete our mission from the Grypherburg office, or when you stop getting honey drunk.
Boooooring...
You sure you don't want to watch them fight, Leto? I thought you of all people would be excited.
I like fighting, but I don't care about two dunces slugging it out. They talk about helping people, but the first thing they do is punch the people who are supposed to help them.
Hm? Looks like the one in charge has finally had enough.
People... people! That's enough!
The golden-haired Ursus screams at the top of her lungs, but her anxious, trembling voice sounds thin and weak amidst the cheers and angry shouts.
People... let's set these pointless arguments aside. Don't forget why we're here today.
Rania is a Grypherburg student. He's one of us, our friend, and he has been treated unjustly because of an act of justice.
I am only so strong alone, but there must be something that the combined strength of the Student Assembly can do, to make the capital hear our voices.
Let's calm down, and work out a plan to free our friend from prison.
No point in discussing the big picture with a bunch of meat heads.
Rania's actions were reckless. Did he not think through the consequences when he vandalized the council hall?
You hear them, Olga? The Symposium doesn't want to help Rania. They are defeatists who keep using the 'big picture' as an excuse to shirk their responsibilities.
Rania is your friend and a member of the Petrachevsky Group, but the Vanguards have always been on your side.
Meanwhile, this coward's grandfather might have been an honorary captain in the old Emperor's Imperial Guard, but he has none of the spirit of an Ursus soldier!
The Symposium is of one mind with you, Olga. We have never opposed rescuing Rania and the other detained students, and we do not even oppose the use of force when necessary.
Meanwhile, what do these Vanguards think their crude, barbaric actions would actually serve to achieve when it comes to changing our country?
The Revitalization of Ursus makes it clear that the empire is not an old jacket you can simply swap out for a new one.
That damnable Nikola Ilyinsky again...
I would be happy to hear the Symposium out, if you have any better ideas.
We must print more newspapers, highlighting the injustices Rania and his comrades have suffered.
Not just in the academies; we have to mobilize the citizenry as well. Rania was arrested for speaking up for the miners of the Far North. The workers will stand on our side.
We will attract sympathizers by publicizing the plight of the arrested students, we will teach them why we struggle, and how to struggle. We will target the legacy of Hippogryphs.
The old nobles of Ursus gladly accepted the brutal traditions of the Hippogryph Kingdom. Many of them have Hippogryph blood in their veins.
Only by excising these centuries-old tumors can Ursus truly belong to the Ursus.
What a joke. Do these 'old nobles' include the House of Treplev? Are you going to excise Olga like a tumor?
That is another matter entirely. As long as they support a new Ursus—
Then you tell the burghers and workers that Nikola Ilyinsky never proposed overthrowing the regime, only how to sell himself for a good price afterwards.
And then you tell the Liberi and Felines among them that Ursus belongs to the Ursus, and all other races are either our servants or spies.
You're taking things out of context! He never said anything of the sort.
The only thing the old tsar did right was hang this madman who kept babbling about a 'new Ursine identity'!
A student beneath the podium throws a metal water can at the Vanguards member, but it misses and hits the stage instead.
Other Vanguards immediately grab him and start beating him up, once again engulfing the scene in chaos.
Hey, these guys don't call themselves Vanguards for nothing. They fight a little better, relatively speaking.
The ruckus is making it impossible for Absinthe to respond to Leto's joke. She glances at Olga, who is supposed to be in charge.
Olga stands quietly with hesitation on her face, looking at the members of the Self-Government Group, the only ones who have not involved themselves in the clash.
...We have new problems.
Punches freeze in mid-air and the shouting ceases. The brawling students let go of each other.
General!
You're late again, Sonya.
...Sorry.
But it looks like I'm here just in time.
You were late for the last general meeting. Need I remind you that a general meeting of the Student Assembly represents—
A major event that will determine the future of Grypherburg's students. I remember. Go on, keep 'talking'.
Why so quiet, Faddey? I thought you liked greeting people with your fists, including me.
Not like that'd achieve anything.
No, but talking with your fists always guarantees a result better than talking with your mouth.
It's true that today's agenda has not advanced smoothly. But that doesn't excuse the Self-Government Group's repeated contempt for the Student Assembly.
Excuse me, Chairman Trepleva, but what exactly do you mean by 'contempt'?
The Self-Government Group has followed the Assembly's rules to the letter and participated in all activities since we joined.
Everyone turns to look at Zima.

This general meeting is being held on short notice, while many of the Self-Government Group's members have missions abroad. I find it unfair that you are accusing us of contempt simply for being late.
Most importantly, the Self-Government Group has never been party to the Assembly's internal conflicts.
If I may be blunt, it seems the Self-Government Group has respected the Assembly to a greater extent than any of the student organizations arguing and fighting in this room.
If I may be blunt, Anna, you were never supposed to be part of the Assembly.
Your organization and its members are from Chernobog, while we are all Grypherburgers.
I remind you that it was Olga who extended an invitation to the Self-Government Group to join the Assembly.
Olga wanted the Assembly to unite as many students as possible. That's why she took you in, and provided assistance for you to establish a base in Grypherburg.
In turn, you are expected to demonstrate an eagerness to contribute to the Assembly, or at the very least, to respect it.
We have not forgotten the help that we received, and we express our gratitude for it, Leonid.
The Self-Government Group has always been supportive of the Assembly's activities. We have never backed down, nor compromised your plans.
What did you do when the assembly instructed you to burn the tsar's portrait?
We upgraded the portrait to a scrawling of the tsar's family. Something wrong with that?
Whose scrawling was it?
Mine, hehe.
It was my first time. Everyone loved it!
That's the problem!
How do you expect to provoke anti-tsarist sentiment when you draw the tsar's family so cute?
So the problem is she draws too good? You couldn't catch her if you practiced three years!
Suka! You're just looking for trouble!
That's enough! Stop—
...Order! This is a hearing, a solemn occasion. We will tolerate no disruptions.
Absinthe wakes from her reverie. The nobles have reached a truce, though they continue to glare at each other, their fine outfits not looking so fine anymore.
Very well. Let us return to your background, Young Zoya.
You mentioned the Student Assembly, an organization that I'm sure most of us are familiar with.
It is an alliance of student organizations from various schools, often publishing commentary under pseudonyms inspired by famous traitors, such as the wicked Ivan Tulin
Hey... who is this Ivan Tulin
Younger brother of the great traitor Yakov Petrov, who wrote several seditious volumes while in exile in Leithanien.
The council has investigated, but he hasn't been seen in public for a while, and he hasn't published anything new in some time, so he's probably dead.
Why use the name of a dead man?
All these conspiracies and outlandish claims need a representative opposed to His Imperial Majesty, preferably someone who cannot personally rebuke them.
They all want Ivan dead more than we do, so that they might claim the name.
You said you personally witnessed the meeting of this Student Assembly as a spectator before the incident?
Yes.
I should make it clear that I was not a member of any student organization; I attended as a friend of Sonya's, and others.
I do not have full knowledge of the outcome of their discussions, and I never supported their actions.
Hmm...
Parliamentarian, pass me the document to your left.
This transcript indicates that the Student Assembly was planning some kind of action against the Grypherburg Winter Ball.
That's enough... we've wasted too much time already. We must get back to the agenda at hand—how to rescue Rania and his comrades.
Faddey, you are the Vanguards' representative. What is your final proposal?
We’ve deliberated fully. A raid on the prison.
While Rania's arrest was a high-profile one, we have learned that his prison is not heavily guarded.
Besides, the annual ball presents a waning of Grypherburg's security. It's the perfect opportunity.
You're out of your mind!
(Whisper) Wouldn't the police be extra careful with all the nobles gathered during the ball?
(Whisper) Father said the Grypherburg police are not selected by the law, but appointed by the powerful.

(Whisper) Both the armies and the police are part of the Ursus Guard. Minor nobles who don't have the influence to send their children into the Army as officers take the second-best option of sending them into the police to 'gain experience'.
(Whisper) The Winter Ball is more than just a social event; it's also the stage of politics and intrigue for all the assembled nobility.
(Whisper) Personnel moves in the police normally take place before and after the ball, which will keep the officials busy.
(Whisper) And so, Faddey is not necessarily wrong.
You're proposing an act of war, Faddey, while I'm not sure you can even wield a weapon, nor have I seen any preparation from your party.
Of course we're prepared.
This is for present company only, but I will tell you that I know some free traders who can get us used weapons from the Londinium war, enough to arm us all.
Free traders? Those foreigners?
Is that enough to face down heavily-armed prison guards?
Of course! If you've seen them with your own eyes, you know that they're decades ahead of Ursine technology.
We're falling behind. Survival of the fittest is the law of nature. This is our last chance to catch up.
We must not allow the old, corrupt aristocrats to drag the empire into its grave. We will be the vanguard that makes Ursus strong again.
And you think these 'free traders' do it out of the goodness of their hearts? Have you forgotten that we are Ursines first and foremost?
You would have us take up foreign weapons and follow the corrupt institutions of Victoria and Columbia! I will not stand idly by while people like you—
He steps forward as he shouts, trying to prove the Symposium are just as physically capable.
Someone grabs his right arm. He tries to shake off the hand, only to find that it does not budge in the slightest.
Leonid turns around to curse the interloper, only for his gaze to meet Zima's.
Are you done?
Faddey, your plan is just sending people to die. No intel, no tactics, no info on whether the weapons are any good.
The police will be a little mixed up, but the prison is defended by trained gendarmes that we can't handle.
I know you can fight, Sonya. Many of us Vanguards have great respect for you.
But your talk of 'ready' is no different from the Symposium's 'big picture', both excuses for inaction.
Do not interfere with the Assembly's decision, if you don't have a better way to get Rania and his comrades out.
Do not presume to represent the Assembly's decision without a general vote, Faddey.
The Symposium is clearly not on your side, and the Self-Government Group will not support a suicide mission. We can take a vote now, if you really think your words are enough to sway the majority.
All eyes are on Olga, filled with hope and expectation.
Olga, if there are no objections, the Petrachevsky Group can count the votes as usual—
No.
Olga?
I agree with Leonid and Sonya. The Assembly cannot risk a failed violent struggle.
But I also agree that simply sitting around will only make matters worse, sapping our will to resist while giving the police the chance to do as they please with Rania.
Therefore, I have a plan that will satisfy everyone and rescue Rania. We will encircle the Winter Ball.
What is she talking about? Instead of raiding the prison, we go straight for the nobles?
No, this is not an act of violence.
We will go unarmed. We will protest with signs in our hands and tell the nobles about the people who are undermining our nation's future behind our backs.
I don't see the point in it.
Your father may be a good man, Olga, but that doesn't mean all the nobility are willing to sit and talk with us.
Even setting aside everything they've done over the years, they have arrested Rania and his comrades, and they're talking about making a public example of them.
You would simply yell at them, empty-handed and defenseless...? This is like putting a plate of fresh meat out for a mangler, cut to bite-sized pieces for the beast's convenience.
No, Anna, you don't understand. The nobles at the ball have no reason to harm us.
I've organized similar events in the past. As long as we exercise restraint, neither the nobles nor the police will lay hands on us.
In the name of my father, I promise that this is simply an action to make our voices heard. No one will get hurt.
I agree with Olga. Many of our number come from the local aristocracy. In effect, we will be holding ourselves hostage against the aristocratic class as a whole.
It's one of the few chips that we truly hold in our own hands. With enough of us, it's very possible that we can sway the council's decision.
A compromise, but better than inaction... the Vanguards assent.
Let us take the vote.

It is hereby proposed that all the constituent organizations of Student Assembly march upon the venue and protest before the nobility at seven o'clock in the evening, three days from now, during the Winter Ball.
Hands raise into the air... before long, there are a few outsiders at the meeting, just as there were during the brawl.
The students with their hands raised look so tall, their calm giving them strength.
Absinthe is short of breath. She scans their faces, but finds no reassurance in them.
Some desire action, their eyes filled with anger, their hands trembling with guilt towards their fellow students and hatred for the establishment.
Some fear violence, embracing this alternative, believing that someone will back them up as long as they do not raise steel, relieved smiles on their faces.
Others are worried. They wish to be accepted, fearing rejection by an organization that represents passion and progress. They have raised their palms above their ears, docile and obedient...
...Get away from Sonya!
The outcome is clear, Sonya. The vast majority agree with the proposal.
I hope the Self-Government Group will join in this action. The Assembly needs everyone.
The votes in favor don't change the fact that this is an ill-considered... ill-advised proposal.
You think you're smarter than us, Anna? We know the SSG has been paying lip service to the Assembly, we simply chose not to say it out loud!
The SSG needs to prove its loyalty to the Assembly. Enough of your arrogance, Chernobogian.
You want a fight, I'll give you one!
Leto! No!
The Self-Government Group has been utterly committed to finding the best way for all students.
Our doctrine is flexibility, as we have explained to you many times. It is most unfair to criticize the SSG's position now.
Natalya of House Rostov, you may not be a soldier, but you are Ursine nobility, and you should know that obedience is the foundation of our nation's battlefield dominance.
But—
I'll go.
Sonya...?
I'm glad you accept the Assembly's ideals, Sonya.
I'll go, and I'll join your action, Olga, on one condition.
Any student who refuses to participate is free to pull out without compromising their future status in the Assembly.
Phew... glad that's over.
Dealing with those noble kids is such a headache... brr, Grypherburg nights are awfully cold.
I'll block the wind for you, Leto!
Thanks, Gummy!
Aha! Got it! C'mere, honey drop!
Hey! That wasn't nice!
YOU were the one who lied to me about running out of honey drops!
Sonya...?
Sorry I made that call for you all, without asking.
That's not what I meant...
Why apologize, Sonya? You didn't decide anything for us. We chose to join you.
Besides, falling out with the Assembly back there would only make things more difficult for our subsequent operations.
You're always trying to do the right thing. We trust you.
Natalya is right... but did you agree to Olga's proposal to get the SSG out of a tight spot, or do you genuinely support her action?
They're rushing into this without planning anything. I'm worried it's gonna get out of hand.
We're Rhodes Island-trained. If anything unexpected happens, we can help.
I support you too, Sonya.
I'm just thinking...
Why did we come back to Ursus?
Because Rhodes Island doesn't have an office in Ursus, and they need the Self-Government Group to establish an information network here.
But we could've helped Rhodes Island in other ways. It's not like we've done anything but a little support work since we got to Grypherburg.
We talked about this before we left Rhodes Island. We agreed that the SSG should fight for an office in Ursus.
The Doctor was a little iffy on it, but eventually said yes...
I guess the Doctor wants us to go back to a normal life.
But... this isn't the normal life I imagined...
Everyone's fighting all the time. I don't get hungry, but I'm never happy.
That much is true. Everyone we've met is the same. They keep blather on with big words and concepts, without actually understanding anything.
Is it because we don't know Grypherburg well enough, or because of our unwillingness to reach out to others?
Maybe we've just been away from Ursus for too long. We need time...
We never truly left Chernobog, did we?
Their faces reflect faintly in the shop windows by the roadside under the dim street lamps. Winter nights in Deity Grypherburg are long and quiet.
They walk old stone-paved streets, trampling chunks of snow into the dirt-filled gaps.
We should have gone back to say goodbye to that old, lifeless place.
If we keep running from it, the Ursus we remember is just gonna stay charred dirt under broken rubble... And I can't call that home.
It is the empire's past. It will be the empire's future, if we do nothing.
The Self-Government Group has seen the fire, while the rest of Ursus has not. We should find the best way forward, however slim the chance may be.
We need friends to get ourselves set up in Grypherburg. That's why we joined the Assembly in the first place.
I wanna help our new friends!
Hah. Besides, the SSG never backs down.
Damn straight!
Are you alright, Zoya?
...Young Zoya? Young Zoya!
Are you listening?
I'm sorry, Your Honor.
I find myself fighting my emotions as I relive the events of the general meeting. It was a difficult time for me.
Entirely understandable.
I'm sure that all present know the background of the Katorga Incident, but I would like you to describe again the circumstances surrounding the Winter Ball at the start of the incident.
Yes, Your Honor.
I spoke to attendees at the ball, and some students who participated in the action shortly after the end of the ball.
I learned that certain unexpected events took place on the day of the ball—
Only candles lighting the corridors. Is the palace cutting back power usage too?
His Imperial Majesty wishes to share the conserved energy with the people.
Rest assured, this is simply a pragmatic measure of frugality. Life in the palace has not been affected, nor has this year's Winter Ball.
Here we are. May I take your coat, Miss Rostova?
That's very kind of you.
It is my duty.
So bright...
I will take my leave, then.
One moment. I have some questions—
—Natashenka?
Countess Vorontsova?
Gosudar-batyushka... it's really you, poor girl!
The noblewoman hurriedly approaches Rosa, so excited she can hardly maintain her aristocratic demeanor.
She grabs Rosa's arm tightly, as though confirming she has not seen a ghost.
Natashenka... oh, I'm so glad to see you... alive and well...
It broke my heart to hear what happened in Chernobog. Why would fate be so cruel to such a kind family?
Thank you for your sympathy. We lost some property, but it's nothing compared to the safety of the family... and anyway, it's all in the past.
Yes, yes, let us leave all the painful memories in the past... you have no idea how glad I was to read your letter that you were coming to Deity Grypherburg.
I wish you could enjoy a peaceful time here, but the capital is hardly a peaceful place these days.
Malcontents and ingrates everywhere—as though the troubles stirred by those insolent military brutes were not enough, now unruly commoners want to turn Deity Grypherburg upside-down.

Oh, look at me, this is no way to talk to the daughter of an old friend that I haven't seen in years. You've only just gotten back, of course you have no idea! I'm afraid I'm always on edge these days, I hardly get any sleep at night.
Not at all. I'm glad you're sharing the news with me.
You're a good girl, but this is not a good time to talk of such things.
Is your mother well, Natashenka? What about your father, Andrey?
If he's in the capital without saying a word, sending you alone to the Winter Ball...
I suppose I've been a poor friend, and allowed our families to drift apart.
Countess, that's not it at all. Father asked me to send you his regards if I saw you, and to beg your pardon for falling out of touch.
And of course, I do not need to tell you that you are Mother's best friend, but the House of Rostov is focusing our full attention on what assets we have left in the Central Governorate.
'We must not lose any more prestige,' and I regret to say... they are fully occupied, for the time being.
I understand, but you should say, 'Therefore, I am here.'
Look at you, a proper young lady all grown up. You are a perfect representative of the House of Rostov!
I must say, you show better manners and dignity than many native Grypherburgers... I'm sure the Rostov name will be known throughout the capital before long.
No... I still have much to learn.
Speaking of which, I would very much like to ask about the present situation...
Have patience, young Natashenka. I understand your unease, but this is not something that can be explained in a few words.
Learn to observe with your own eyes. There is no better opportunity than this. What you should do now, is go enjoy the Winter Ball.
Until His Majesty arrives, set aside all the troubling questions, all the answers you eagerly seek, and all the wild theories about what the future holds. Enjoy the present.
Dance, laugh, do as youth ought to.
And if a young officer catches your eye, I will stake my reputation to be your matchmaker, for the sake of your mother, even if it's stubborn old Bolkonsky's—
Enjoy the peace of His Majesty's protection. It is a privilege for those of us who live here in the capital, those of us who are loyal.
You must learn this in order to fully integrate yourself, Natashenka.

lines.st: '...You must learn this in order to fully integrate yourself.'

lines.x: ...The miners are still hungry. Even in Grypherburg, the residents of Odoyev Raion can no longer afford heating, while Katorga Raion has seen power and heat cut completely upon work stoppage.
But for them, the show must go on.
I don't understand... didn't that person say His Majesty is reducing the palace's electricity use? What happened to the energy conserved? Why—
This is all such nonsense. Dealing with big shots is such a hassle.
Is Rosa gonna be okay in there?
Natalya spoke to us a few days before the Student Assembly general meeting about going into the ball as the scion of House Rostov to gather information.
Certain things are known only to the aristocracy, after all. And more information never hurts, regardless of where it comes from.
Sonya believes she can do it, and I have no reason to object. The contents of these conversations are as expected. Things seem to be going smoothly so far, and the audio feed is clear.
We have to thank that student they call Botani for this. Her equipment has worked out even better than I hoped.
All we need to do is to cooperate with the protestors and follow the plan.
Zima's waving at us! We should go to her.
I think she's talked things over with the others. We'll pack up and head over.
Leto, are you staying here or...?
Shh, gimme a sec.
Something's happening.
I thought this year's Winter Ball would be cancelled...
Those insolent traitors are attempting to coerce His Imperial Majesty by force of arms. But I'm not sure how the tsar intends to deal with them...
All the more important that we hold our heads high and continue doing what we must. His Imperial Majesty has both courage and vision.
This is the strongest possible response. It proves that there is nothing to be feared from the chaos, that we will not be beaten by traitors who have already failed once.
As for those who do not see clearly, and choose to stand with the traitors... we will place flowers on their graves, this time next year.
Look out!
—I'm sorry—
You have ruined not only the young lady's dress, but also a cup of fine wine... sudar'.
I'm so sorry! Please forgive the offense, Duchess Volkina—
You did not offend me, but you should apologize to the young lady whose dress you have soiled.
Erm, I apologize, baryshnya...
It's alright.
Who let this buffoon in?
He could hardly be a nameless commoner if the servants let him in. What is your name?
Ah! Please call me Pavlovich, a humble deputy of the Duma. I was recently appointed magistrate by His Imperial Majesty, serving as special representative for recent matters in Katorga Raion—
A representative of Katorga Raion? Ah, I remember now.
You know me? I'm honored!

Of course, of course. I heard the State Council was having difficulty finding someone to deal with the Katorga problem. I'm sure you must be a remarkable talent, if the responsibility has fallen upon your shoulders.
I would have sent someone to congratulate you, if I was not busy arranging winter supplies for the Second Army.
You flatter me, Your Grace... I have been serving in Katorga for two months now.
In fact, I do not know why I was given such an important responsibility, but I certainly would not dream of disappointing His Imperial Majesty.
As you may know, Katorga Raion is not as worthless as people think. All this old industrial district needs is an opportunity to revitalize itself...
(Whisper) Why have I never heard of him?

Perhaps you've been spending too much time on your luxurious estate and grown out of touch with the personnel movements of the central government. At least read a few newspapers while you sit on your rocking chair in your garden.
All the news does is make one more troubled.
Of course, I am unworthy of Your Serenity's attention, Count Golitsyn—I understand that this has been an exemplary year for your winery, and you must be very busy...
Enough flattery. I believe you still owe this young lady a formal apology.
What is your name, baryshnya?
I am Natalya Rostova, Your Grace.
Rostova? I am not familiar with the name...
Neither am I.
Ah! Your father must be Count Andrey Rostov of Chernobog!
You know of my father?
Of course! His Serenity demonstrated such foresight when he pulled out from Chernobog just in time, narrowly avoiding complete ruin!
...That's all in the past now.
I see you are surprisingly... knowledgeable, Gospodin Pavlovich.
But you ought to get changed, young lady. Even the best wine was not made to be tasted by silk.
Yes, spasibo...
Rosa hurries away from the embarrassing scene. She can still hear the excited conversation going on behind her as she leaves.
Duchess Volkina! I hear that you oppose the motion to decommission Katorga Raion. I am naturally of the same mind...
...The factories are still...
...Perhaps we can work together...
...Watch your words, Melnikov. Not even His Imperial Majesty has made an official statement on the events of the Far North.
You misunderstand. I am not leveling an accusation towards you or the Grand Duchess.

However, I have long expressed concerns about Breskenoy, long before Yelizaveta's transgressions in the Far North, yet your camp unanimously swore to His Imperial Majesty that her loyalty should not be questioned.
You, and every single member of the old guard, have betrayed the trust of the State Council and His Imperial Majesty.
Then I look forward to your speech at the hearing. You would do well not to change a single word, that everyone might hear how you slander the foundations of our empire.
There is no need to wait until then.
I will expose your crimes to His Imperial Majesty when he attends tonight's ball!
The angry shouting has drawn the attention of the crowd. Several servants hurry to the scene, trying to placate the angry aristocrat.
Rosa pulls on her sleeves to ward off the cold, though the fireplaces in the ballroom burn hotter than anywhere else in Ursus, and the heat is always on.
A servant is replacing the fragrance. The smell of citron and neroli cover up the stinging scent of evaporating alcohol. Rosa lets out a long sigh.
Are you alright, Natashenka? Have you not yet found an appropriate conversation partner?
Oh dear, what happened to your dress? Did someone insult you? Give me a name, and I will teach them a lesson!
Please, Countess, there is no need to be angry. It's a mark of honor for assisting a noble lady.
You have a heart of gold, my child, but please, take care of your own safety first next time. Who knows what those sycophants might do?
I appreciate your concern, but that was the most interesting thing to happen to me tonight.
Most of what I've heard has to do with the Grand Duchess. I tried to understand and ask questions, but I lack the necessary knowledge to continue the conversation.
This is why your parents sent you to Grypherburg, my dear Natashenka.
I have seen many young ladies give their souls to cooks, tailors, and doctors, but not the great people who write laws, quell rebellions, and set taxes...
Even if they are always caring about us.
I understand, but today I'm simply the heir of a humble count with naught but a few small holdings in the Central Governorate. How might I catch a gaze that these busy lords only occasionally cast?
...I should make myself clearer, since you're my old friend's only daughter.
Politics is a part of all our lives. No one is immune, especially not those upon whom a title of nobility has conferred a heavy responsibility.
Are these responsibilities carried out by engaging in small talk in a place like this?
Natashenka...
You misunderstand the reason we talk here. These words are not necessarily announcements of measures certain to be implemented, nor do they necessarily represent our true views.
Then... why?
To fit in. To know which people to avoid, and which to befriend.
One signature may be all it takes to rebuild your parents' fortune, to keep your children out of the trenches, to allow your friends to sleep soundly on a grand estate.
Do not think you can avoid their gazes by indulging in pleasure. It will only cause those gazes to harden, and permit no question.
That is how a highly effective social scene operates, Natashenka.
...Looks like I still have much to learn.
And time is the one thing that young people have aplenty.
(Whisper) It's the Chairman—
And Vice Chairman Vasily Gorchikov! This is a rare sight. They are hardly ever seen together outside of the State Council...
The Chairman is rarely seen at the balls, but His Imperial Majesty has not yet arrived... is this a sign?
Perhaps they are trying to present a picture of calm.
It may be too late for that.
Those two...?
All eyes are on the two men who just entered. The crowd parts to allow them to proceed to the middle of the hall.
The greetings from the crowd are loud, though their sincerity is uncertain.

lines.st: 'Salutations, Chairman.'
'Health to you, Vice Chairman.'

lines.x: Rosa carefully observes the pair from the crowd.
The black-haired man walks through the crowd in silence, not the slightest emotion on his face. His gaze is firm, but clearly fatigued, fixed on the empty space in front of him.
The man whom they call Vice Chairman walks behind the black-haired man who is a head shorter than he is, respectfully keeping a short distance while nodding and smiling in response to the crowd.
...The blonde one is Duke Vasily Gorshkov, colonel-in-chief of the Imperial Guard, and executive Vice Chairman of the State Council.
(Whisper) And the black-haired one in front of him is—
Chairman Islam Witte.
Yes... everyone in Grypherburg should recognize him.
Actually, I watched the Speech at the Inauguration Ceremony of the Tulskaya Special Technical School on the intercity net. It was an impressive speech, concise and sincere.
Ah, the intercity net... I will never understand such newfangled things.
Go before them, Natashenka. Listen to what these people talk about. This is a learning opportunity.
Yes, Countess, I will—
The sharp sound of glass cracking interrupts the cheerful conversations around the hall, as everyone looks around for its source.
Count Osadchy, are you feeling unwell?
...No, no! It's them! They're downstairs!
What? Who turned off the lights—power outage?
The palace wouldn't lose power just like this! It must be the mob—
Are the duty officers of the palace so incompetent they can't even maintain an electrical switch—
...Look outside!
There's a mob right outside the window!
Free Rania! Free all political prisoners!
Release the reserves! Share the energy! Heat for all the people!
Excuse me, pardon me, let me pass...
Zima! Istina! Where are you...?
Liberty for the people! Bread for the people!
Today's silence is tomorrow's slavery! Make our voices heard!
Show yourselves! We demand parley!
I believe those present know the rest better than I do.
The ballroom was in chaos. In their panic, some attendees removed their gowns, snatched women's hats out of the servants' hands and ran outside...
Preposterous! You weren't even at the ball! Who told you these rumors?
They're all over the police force, and it's hard to tell where they come from. I offer you my apologies, if the rumors are unsubstantiated—
Not me!
N-Not to me! Apologize to everyone who was at the ball!
Order!
This hearing is not interested in street rumors. It is what happened with the students that we wish to know.
For example, who spoke those foul words of sedition?
Which words?
Which else? The foulest, most treacherous ones.
People were saying all sorts of things. I'm not sure what you're referring to—
The most treasonous, blasphemous, sacrilegious words... the ones that no one in this room may utter!
Oh, I get it.

Death to the mudak Emperor!
Death to the mudak Emperor!
Death to the mudak Emperor!
Death to the mudak Emperor!
Death to the Hippogryph-blooded filth! Ursus belongs to the Ursus!
Bring out the bloodsucker Witte! Bring out the imbecile Fyodor!
You mean to say every student blasphemed against His Imperial Majesty that night.
Maybe, other than the few who kept cool heads. The young can be hot-blooded, and become incited to speak with a voice that does not belong to them.
Or perhaps you are exaggerating in order to cover up for a few of their number.
I am only telling the truth. You're jumping to some shocking conclusions.
Let us go back to the previous statement. You explained why Baryshnya Rostova failed to notice His Imperial Majesty's absence. Do you know where he was?
I learned a few things through my police contacts, but they are vague and uncertain.
You know of his whereabouts?
I know he was in the palace, but not why he did not appear at the ball as scheduled.
No, you know.
I'm sorry?
My evidence indicates that the Deity Grypherburg Police Night's Watch was the first to learn of His Imperial Majesty's disappearance, which means that you, too, were in a position to know.
Answer, Young Zoya. Why are you hiding the truth about the attempt on the Emperor's life, and his subsequent disappearance during the protests in question?
Well...
If you knew, your friend, Sonya Mykhailivna, knew too.
Was the violence that she incited in the quarantine zone aimed at finishing what the assassin attempt began?
(Murmurs) So the Emperor went missing that night. That explains everything.
...What?

Natalya mentioned something in particular. Before the protests began, she was heading to where the chairman and vice chairman were, but her attention, like the others, was drawn to the light outside the window.
Both of them had left by the time she looked back.
Day of the hearing, a Tsarevgrad Office
If you don't want to appear at the hearing, I can go in your place, at least minimize the impact of the Emperor's disappearance by influencing the direction of the hearing.
There is no longer a need to hide, Vasha.
Virtually every major noble in Grypherburg has learned about His Imperial Majesty's 'act of whimsy'. No number of gag orders will wipe away the shock that the event has caused.

Right now, I don't give two hoots about the hearing or the public opinion. The only thing on my mind is His Majesty's safety. You must find out what happened that day, before we move to eliminate the issues that put the Emperor in danger.
It was more than just Grypherburg's guards that went out of control that day. It was a warning sign, and a lesson to learn from.

Forgive my imprudence, Chairman Witte, but I understand that you had an argument with His Imperial Majesty prior to the ball, where he expressed his displeasure with the State Council's handling of the Katorga matter.

If that is what you are referring to, people on the outside would not be surprised, for His Imperial Majesty is ever caring of all who walk upon this land, even if his kindness is often mistaken for weakness.
No, not that.
His Majesty was indeed in a bad mood, but he agreed to attend the ball, until I received a tip prior to the event—
Someone was attempting to place an Originium bomb in the ballroom. He was caught by a maintenance worker.
Attempting to assassinate His Imperial Majesty?

It is not so simple. I thought the same as you did, so I followed emergency protocols and instructed the Royal Guard to go to His Majesty's chambers and escort him through the underground tunnel, while I interrogated the assassin personally.
He claimed he was here to assassinate Baron Kamshalov, at the behest of the baroness.
It would be a captivating family drama, if circumstances were different...
As the interrogation continued, however, he mentioned something even more unsettling—
Damn... come on, Geil, keep it together, you can do it...
Crouched on the floor, he wipes the sweat from his eyes, while haphazard parts are scattered across the red carpet.
A round 'alarm clock', three sticks of explosives bundled together like sausages, and numerous wires. A simple bomb that even a novice could assemble by following the instructions.
But the sweat has soaked through the paper he is holding, blurring the writing to illegibility.
Okay, I can still read this... connect the blue wire, then the green one, then a funt of... a funt of...
A funt of canned stew?
Blyat! Ivan! The baroness paid so much, and you're passing off a recipe as bombmaking instructions?!
Alright, calm down, it's up to me now... maybe this green one goes into this connector.
Wrong, the green one goes below the blue one.
Let's give that a try...
It worked! Thank you, kind-hearted—
Who the khuy are you?
(Hushed) Calm down and don't yell! Do you want to bring the whole police force down on our heads?
I had to stop you. If you really put that wire in, we'd have one more, no, two more 'canned stews' here in this room.
Don't worry, we're fellow travelers, I'm not gonna sell you out.
We're what?
Are you in a noblewoman's pocket too?
What are you talking about? We're both assassins, aren't we?
Sorry, I... it's my first time. I'm not really familiar with this stuff.
Hey, everybody's gotta start somewhere. Who's your debut job? Is it a big one?
I don't know if he's big or not. All I know is that he's a baron with a casino.
Well, that's not a bad one to pop your cherry. You'll get jobs for bigger fins with some practice under your belt.
What about you?
Heh, cover your mouth first. Don't want you freaking out and drawing unwanted attention.
(Hushed) I'm here to kill Duchess Volkina.
Who's that?
...What?
You don't know her?!
Quiet, quiet—
She's one of the few hereditary dukes in Ursus, a thorn in the side of the old guard nobility, and blood relative to the Emperor himself!
Okay, okay, don't shout, I'm sorry...
My employer searched across all of Ursus for an assassin who could take the job, and I was the only one who would do it! How could you—
...You—
Shh—
...Shh?
The surprise visitor shakes his head and gestures to the table on the other side. The nervous assassin hesitates, then walks over slowly.
Give it to me.
You want this bread?
The man shakes his head.
Don't tell me you want the table knife?
The man nods.
Wait, tell us what you're gonna do with it first. Giving a knife to a stranger is not exactly becoming of a professional assassin.
Give it to me, and I'll tell you.
The nervous assassin dares not approach. He tosses the knife to the man, who picks it up silently, then makes a sign with two fingers.
Go out the door, go through the kitchen, climb the ladder to the roof, and get into the room on the west side via the sunroof.
Shh—
...Shh.
The edge of the visitor's mouth twitches. He nods and departs, leaving behind the two stunned assassins.
What were you talking about? I didn't understand a word.
He's here to kill... the Emperor.
So you mean palace security allowed all these myriad assassins into the ballroom, and it took a maintenance worker to discover them.
How many more surprises do the Grypherburg's guards have in store for us?
The capital-wide power outage happened soon after.
While not entirely unexpected, given the recent energy shortage, it coincided with the matter of the assassins, which led to an overreaction.
That is why, after we left the scene of the ball, I instructed you to head to police headquarters and search for suspicious persons amongst the protestors.
You saw their crude, ineffective methods.
It's a good thing that your daughter is hardworking and motivated. If she was unambitious and went into the Guard by pulling strings, you would be the one with the constant headaches.
I am glad for Eloysius that you are willing to mentor her. Our entire family is very proud.
But how could these absurdly incompetent assassins have affected His Imperial Majesty?
Do you remember who I sent to find him, according to emergency procedures?
The Royal Guard?
That's what I don't understand. Why would the Emperor need to flee, if he was protected by the Royal Guard?
(Hushed) Because the loyalty of the Royal Guard is to Ursus, not the Emperor.
What?
Why are you still here?
You're late, Witte.
...Where is His Imperial Majesty? Did you not go with him?
Your orders were to go to his room and guard against assassins.
I ordered you to protect the Emperor! This is a plan that's long been in place. In the event of any emergency, you are to personally escort him through the secret passage.
Unfortunately, your best intentions do not seem to be appreciated.
Do you mean...?
Have you not realized, Chairman?
The one you're sworn to protect has been thoroughly disappointed by all that has happened here for years, decades even.
Of course, given your unreserved loyalty over such a long period of time, he would trust you, even if he sees all the other nobles as traitors.
But he will not put the same trust in me.
What happened to His Majesty?
He left by way of the secret passage, as planned, but he steadfastly refused my escort.
Didn't you stop him?
Why would I stop him?
You may not understand how I think, but you should try to understand how he thinks, 'Caretaker'.
Let him go out and see for himself what Ursus is truly like, beyond the window.
Which means that His Imperial Majesty has disappeared from under the watch of the Royal Guard.
Even if it was of his own volition.
The air itself seems thinner in the tightly packed formation of students, but they make room for their leader, Olga, giving a small but isolated space.
Fellow students! Unite and bring down the establishment!
The young noble lady stands proudly upon a battered oak casket, a faded family emblem faintly visible upon it.
Her shouting is drowned out by even more radical chants, but she squints as if to take in this Grypherburg night that belongs to them, until someone makes it to her side.
Time to put this to bed, Olga!
Sonya?
No marching, not even unified slogans... I see booze in the crowd. This is too risky.
Don't pour cold water when morale is at its highest—
Listen to me! These streets are lined with noble townhouses. Look how narrow the path is, it'd make any retreat really bad.
More than that, I haven't seen a single cop.
There's more to this than we know. Let's march south, shout our chants that way. It'll be easier to respond to any surprises.
I know what you're trying to say, but all this is normal. Faddey already explained that police operations are disrupted during the Winter Ball due to the personnel changes.
Besides, given our background, activism for our friends' rights, within reason, is seen as a sort of youthful experience, not rebellion.
Set your heart at ease and stand with us, Sonya.
Right... given your background.
If you're gonna be stubborn about this, I'll have to take the SSG and go.
This is not like you, Sonya. I thought you would be the bravest and firmest at a time like this.
We have caught their attention and left an impression. All that is left is to negotiate for Rania's release, and enjoy the fruits of victory.
If victory is so close, you can enjoy it yourself! No need to save any for me.
No sooner has she said these words than the ballroom's lights turn off, plunging the scene into darkness. Several screams can be heard from inside, then hushed conversations and sobbing.
The students fall silent, looking at each other in bewilderment. This is the quietest moment of this Grypherburg evening.
Did your group do this, Sonya?
No, we didn't do anyth—
Beautifully done!
I'll pretend I didn't hear what you said before. The Self-Government Group has done a great service to our protest!
She pats Zima's shoulder excitedly. Zima hears a soft, indistinct sound coming from the end of the street, so quiet that it is almost drowned out by Olga's patting.
...Look out!
She pulls Olga and runs. A few black cans fall to the ground, leaving light tracks on the snow, before emanating a white smoke.
The nearest student screams, his voice rasping, before it is interrupted by violent coughing as sulfuric smoke attacks his eyes, nose and mouth like tiny gravel.
Then another, and another, as more students find their sight and breath stolen, screaming and twitching as they clutch at their faces. The others cry out in terror and disperse.
Many have fallen to the ground, calling for their friends in vain. They press their faces to the stone and hear the sound of approaching footsteps.
Tear gas deployed! Take the injured, leave the rest!
The late-arriving guardsmen raise their flashlights, casting powerful beams of light upon the young, frightened faces of the students.
The students that can still move run to the end of the street, crying and screaming, half-stumbling and half-crawling, their clothes soiled with muddy snow, footsteps, even blood.
General! We're here!
Let's go! It's a mess back there!
Wait, where's Gummy?
She went to look for you! Didn't you see her?
Blyat!
Zima turns and charges into the chaotic crowd without a second thought, ignoring the calls of Istina and Leto behind her.
It takes some time for her to get back to where Olga was, a scene of bedlam with guardsmen clubbing the remaining resisters with nightsticks.
Gummy is standing in front of Zima, slowly walking to a policeman, staring at his stick-wielding hand.
Why is Papa's watch here...?
What did you do to him?!
—Freeze! Get on your knees!
A nightstick swings for Gummy. She dodges instinctively and sees the man before her tackled to the ground by a black shadow, causing a slushy splash.
Zima?!
Run!
Guardsman down! I need backup!

A dozen guardsmen rush in from every direction, grabbing Zima's shoulders and trying to separate her from their colleague on the ground, but she does not budge in the slightest. They begin striking her in the back with their nightsticks.
Gotcha, Gummy!
What are you doing? Get away from her!
Chase them off. We're pulling out.
Sonya!
Have you lost your mind, Leto?!
Get out of here! That's an order!
Hmph... not gonna happen!
Zima! No, I'm helping you—
Don't try to be a hero, Sonya! Take our hands!
You're out of your mind too? There's more of them back there, and they've got crossbows.
Retreat! That's an order!
Don't try to pull rank with me! It won't work!
I need you to take them away, and the students out there need you! Help them!
That's not an order then. It's a favor, from a friend!
Listen to me, just this once! Go—
...And that's all that happened that night.
Some here may find it hard to accept, but Sonya should be considered a victim in this incident, regardless of which angle you take.
The parliamentarian has noted the witness's account, which will be used in conjunction with the statement Zoya previously submitted to compile an official report.
Any further questions for the witness?
Your Honor, Young Zoya, perhaps some of us have misunderstood the purpose of the hearing.
The reason that many have called for the student groups' actions to recognized as treason is not the protest alone, but also their disruptive behavior in the quarantine zone.
Of foremost concern to us is this: Where was His Imperial Majesty Fyodor in the course of these events?
There have been various rumors running through the people, some claiming that His Majesty mobilized the students against the nobility.
I am therefore quite curious; for example, on the night of the protests, why did His Imperial Majesty—
Forgive the interruption, Count Troyan.
I must emphasize that the Chairman will not be present today, in order to reduce the pressure on the committee, nor has he made any implicit suggestion.

The reason I questioned the witness concerning His Imperial Majesty's whereabouts was only to understand the relationship between the attempted assassination, the Emperor's subsequent disappearance, and the actions of the student leader Sonya Mykhailivna.
If the committee still has doubts, we can clarify them here and now.
Please answer, Young Zoya.
Do you think Sonya Mykhailivna's actions during the protest had anything to do with the assassination attempt on His Imperial Majesty or his disappearance?
The decision of the Royal Guard...
The part that is most important, yet one that no one can know. It will not be part of the hearing's findings.
Did His Majesty say anything to you upon his return?
No, Vasha, no...
We can all see how taciturn he has become since.
Order! Order!
Answer the question, Young Zoya!
I already have, Your Honor.
I can't describe what I didn't see. I do not know if Sonya had anything to do with the assassination attempt on the Emperor.
The committee has heard that you are regularly seen together.
No, Your Honor.
I have already stated that I did not support them so strongly, and I am no member of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group. As you can see—
I know. They did not even give you a badge.
And, may I ask if the cross-examination proceedings have already begun?
According to the bylaws of the 87th Provisional Inquiry Hearing Committee, cross-examination proceedings can only begin once the relevance of all witnesses and evidence has been properly established.
Prior to this, the witness may decline to answer questions.
I have no further questions.
Arbiter...?
...Young Zoya, I have read your file, and certain things are very plain. For example—
You could choose to be a good girl.
Summon the next witness!
Summoning Witness No. 2. Witness No. 1, return to your seat.
Thank you.
You...? Why are you here?
Hmph.
What is your name, Witness No. 2?
Ukusik.
A strange name.
(Whisper) Here are the reference files, Councilor Artyom.

(Whisper) Orphaned vagrant who grew up on the streets, owing her survival to the protection of the older homeless. They say her de facto guardian died at the hands of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group.
(Whisper) She is no friend to the students... I instructed her on what she should and should not say.
Very well. You may speak, Ukusik. No need to be frightened.
There's nothing to be frightened of... ahem. 'Honored members of the hearing committee.' Did I get that right?
This is what happened—
I was selling newspapers on the street corner that night, waiting for Antosha to send someone to take over for me.
Antosha's my boss. I'll talk about him again later—anyway, I saw a bunch of people running to the ballroom, and I was thinking, did something happen to Antosha?
Then a bunch of cops showed up and blocked all the streets. That was when I realized I should have gotten out of there at the first sign of trouble.
I saw one of my pals just standing there blankly while the crowd pushed him around. He yelled something when he saw me—
But I couldn't hear what he said before the cop's bashed his head in with a nightstick, and then he disappeared...
Wait, wait!
Skip the extraneous details, child... no one knows what you're talking about.
What am I supposed to say, then? I don't even know how to read, did you think I would talk like a salesman?
How about you just tell me what to say, and I'll say it?
No!
The arbiter glares at the noble next to him, who avoids his stare while wiping the sweat from his own forehead.
Let's start from the beginning. What kind of organization do you belong to? Who's this boss you were talking about?
Why were you there that night? Tell us everything that you know. Conceal nothing.
Everything?
Yes, everything.
That's gonna take a while. Can I sit down?
No!

lines.st: Start at the beginning, the beginning... where's the beginning?
From when I was born? Nothing to talk about there. My mom gave birth to me, then she died because she couldn't afford medicine.
The dad who abandoned me? There's even less to talk about. I barely remember him.
Getting drafted into the pipe cleaners, watching other three or four year-old kids like me die in the energy pipelines...
Oh, I can't talk about that? I thought it was legal.
Fine, fine, I guess I'll start with the day I met Antosha...

lines.x: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, can I go home now? You've kept me locked up for so long, my parents are gonna be worried. They can tell you that I've always been a good girl!
But today is Monday.
What's Monday got to do with it?
Good kids are in school on Mondays, not stealing on the streets.
Let me see... three hours until school's done. Your parents won't be worried. No rush.
Let me out, you svoloch!
Hah, look at 'em.
Who are you laughing at?
Me? I'm not laughing...
Get lost, I'm not talking about you! You over there, kid, what are you laughing at?
I'm laughing at him. Look—
I followed the student's gaze and saw the lazy cop looking down at a pie, like he wasn't sure what to do.
It was almost teatime. If he filled his belly now, he wouldn't be able to enjoy the cookies fresh out of the oven at the crossroads.
But the pie filled with fruit and cream looked really good. My mouth was watering just seeing it. I didn't understand—
What's so funny about that?
Come closer and I'll tell you—
He won't get to enjoy his pie at all, if he hesitates any longer.
What do you mean?
Wanna bet? You're shaking your head? Don't have the guts? Hah, just you wait...
I didn't believe him at all. I don't make bets unless I've got a sure thing.
I saw the cop look check the time—the head cop would be back soon, and then he wouldn't get to enjoy his pie at all.
So he opened his mouth...
Antosha! I'm here!
Antosha nodded at the student, then took out the cop clean and easy. He found the keys on the cop and gave it to the student.
Hurry. They'll be here soon to check the noise.
How was I to know that you would use a micro-Originium bomb? Aren't those supposed to be really expensive? How did you get Matvey to agree?
I don't need him to agree to do anything... besides, nothing is more worth more than human life.
I thought nothing was more valuable than liberty.
The student's chains dropped to the ground, and he walked out of his cell before punching Antosha in the shoulder. I learned later that's how they show trust and say thank you to each other.
Hey—wait for me! Take me with you!
Do you know this kid?
The student shook his head. I knew I had to seize the chance, or else those cops would take it out on the rest of us when they came back.
Those men... they're mean to me! I don't have anywhere else to go!
Not buying that one, huh? Well, you can't just leave me here to die!
I can do lots of things. I can help—I can tell you're not honest folk, and neither am I!
I heard the sound of a police whistle. It wasn't far. There was no change in Antosha's expression. Normally, that means my words didn't work.
You're right... we're not 'honest folk'.
Where's home? Maybe I can take you back—
Home? You mean the sewers of Odoyev? I don't need you to take me there.
Here, the keys. Catch—you know how to open a lock, don't you?
'Course I do.

lines.st: Before running from the police station after Antosha, I picked up the pie from the ground. It was mostly clean.
I stuffed it in my mouth as I ran for my life. It was good, really sweet. The cop should've eaten it sooner.
We were going to Katorga.

lines.x: We can't afford another failure. There are a hundred invalids here, plus the families taking care of them.
Pavlovich's forces keep growing by the day, and their equipment's getting better too. We blast open a way out, they block it again. And our explosives... we've got maybe two shots left.
Only by taking out Pavlovich as soon as possible do we stand a chance of turning this around.
Uh-huh.
Did you get a good look at him, Yura? How much security does Pavlovich have?
Two bodyguards in close company at all times. Anything else is unclear.
We've been planning based on your idea, and—
I'm done. Gone any more?
Give her the bread basket—look here, remember this face, and find him in Tsarevgrad Raion tomorrow, he'll help you—
You got water? I can't get this down...
Bottle's in the pantry, get it yourself—look at me, not her! The ball's a few weeks away. Do your job and don't get caught. You understand me?
I'll be fine. It's not the first time I've worked as a waiter at a ball.
This is the Winter Ball. You might be the nimblest amongst us, but you need to cut that absent-mindedness out if you want to get things done.
Who are you calling absent-minded? Besides, we pick the pockets of the rich and sell unattended bicycles every day.
Do you write your three or four daily love letters to the same person?
Come on, Antosha, you're no fun. The redistribution of wealth is serious work, but that doesn't mean everyone has to go around as stone-faced as you all the time.
I'm just reminding you that what we're doing is considered a crime by the ruling class, and we're doing it for—
For vengeance.
Yes, vengeance. But far more than that.
The professor was willing to die for us because he believed we can liberate Ursus and usher in a future of freedom... true freedom.
Creak—
I was standing by the wall and gulping from the bottle when the door suddenly opened.
It was a young man, much taller than I am. He looked really tired, but his back was perfectly straight, like it got a bar of steel in it.
He cocked his head questioningly when he saw me drinking from the bottle, but said nothing.

You're back, Matvey. We left some bread for you—
Hey, there's only half a piece left! Who ate the rest?
I said nothing and quietly put the bottle back.
Ahem. I brought the kid back from the police station. I thought...
What were you talking about?
Something failed because you underestimated the nobles, but you've learned your lesson for next time. Did I get all that right?
...You were talking about killing in front of a little girl?
Killing? Oh, so that's what you were talking about.
We unanimously agreed that we must assassinate the nobles on the list.
A list that keeps getting longer. I'm not sure which version you're talking about.
...I'll stop when Ursus is cleansed of all scum.
Matvey stared silently at Antosha for a long time, then tossed him the bottle that I put back.
Ahem. I don't really mind if you talk about it. People are either alive or dead. Why avoid talking about that?
Oh, for heaven's sake, just shut up!
We don't have any spare beds.
What?
Didn't you think about where she was going to sleep before you brought her back?
I can sleep on the floor.
You heard her. She can sleep on the floor.
Alright, I'll think of something! I should have thought about it before I brought her back!
You can sleep in his bed until he figures out something. He can make do with a corner of the workshop.
Fine, whatever you say. Couldn't have built this house without you anyway.
We can get you something to eat, girl, then we'll take you home once you've rested.
Home? Where?
Matvey, she's—
I'm sorry...
Still, you shouldn't be with us.
Why? Because you're all nobles who get to go to school? I never went to school, but there's lots that I can do!
We're not the kind of students you're thinking of...
(Whisper) Antosha, you know these are dangerous times. We shouldn't—
I know! You pick pockets too, don't you? I can help, I'm good at it! Well, I did screw up that last time, but still...
Please, I can help, all I ask is a bit of bread, I don't eat much anyway...
I have nowhere else to go.
...You heard her, Matvey. She's another one without a home.
With her size, she is less likely to be noticed. We could use a backup plan for communicating with the topside.
Alright, listen up. We're sharing our bread with you, but this is not charity, just extending a hand to someone in need—you don't need to live off anyone's charity.
Everyone has a right to live with their heads held high. If someone is unable to live decently through honest labor, the fault does not lie with that person.
Now, let me ask you something.
Do you believe that there will come a day when we bring down the privileged class, when all of us share equal rights in everything?
Honestly, I didn't really understand what he was saying, but he was pretty excited and all I could do was nod.
You mean... we'll all get to eat bread? Even cake?
If I get to eat every day, that's great.
Good.
Welcome to the Unbound—
It looked like he just remembered he never asked me my name.
What's your name?
I don't have a name. 'Kid' isn't a name, right? Or 'Girl'? Well, I'll know you're talking to me, if you call me that.
You talk like you're always trying to bite.
Ukusik—'little thing that bites'. That's your name!
What? I don't—
Come, Ukusik, let's get you a clean pillow.
I said I don't wanna be called that!
I will—never—answer to that!

lines.st: Of course, I ended up answering to it. What a strange name.
Maybe it meant they accepted me as one of them.
For the first time, I found a place that wouldn't kick me out.

lines.loc: One month later5:30 P.M. 1 hour before the Winter Ball

lines.x: Is Yura ready?
Yes. I gave him the knife and poison. When the ball begins, he will approach the target with a tray of champagne.
Killing is easy. The hard part is getting away afterwards... knife or poison. Which will he choose?
The one that draws more attention.
That's what I would do.
The professor said that simply carrying out justice is not enough...
It must be seen by all.
This is a dangerous mission, but also our best opportunity, given that guests are not permitted to bring their own security into the Winter Ball. Yura... never mind. I trust him.
Have more faith, Antosha. We didn't follow you to watch you hang your head.
You don't follow me. We all chose to be here of our own accord.
I know. You're not our leader, of course.
But ideals must have direction. It was your idea to come to Katorga to continue the struggle.
When Pavlovich is dead, we can leave this place together, and our long struggle will be over.
Antosha.
I saw several people walk in. They were the same age as the students, but wearing worker clothes. They were Antosha's friends, gathered here to do something important.
Important things come together to make great things. That's what Antosha told me.
I saw the crowd gather around Antosha, waiting for him to speak. Antosha took a deep breath. The light shined through the window and fell on his chest.
I see you. My fellow students, my brothers, my comrades.

lines.st: I see you as I did the first time we met.
We were gathered around a great man, listening to his teachings.
I see you thinking of the same questions that you did at the time—
How did Ursus come to this?
Where will Ursus go?
What can we do?
I can see it in your eyes that you have lost all hope for this country, and I am the same!
We tried. We are not like those incompetent successors who only dream and talk! We tried!
Peaceful means did not work. We paid the price.
Words were too weak to move an empire steeped in rot and decay.
The professor lost his life because of the 'peace' that we chose, giving his life in exchange for ours.
I see you as I saw our comrades through prison bars, as I fought back tears, witnessing his blood on the execution ground—
Blood that flowed for us!
Blood that has long run dry. None of us fear punishment or death.

lines.x: We want...
Liberty.
We need...
To destroy.
We betray the laws that bind us, for they betrayed the people!
Destroy all the rotten and pointless systems and institutions, for they are beyond repair!
Burn them and hang them, and tear it all down for bread and liberty! Only on the ruins of everything that came before can Ursus finally find—
Rebirth!
We are the Unbound. We shall be bound no more.
Their voices were stacked one on top of the other, making me dizzy. I stood next to Matvey, the only one who remained quiet throughout.
I didn't really understand the meaning of those words, but I noticed that Antosha looked this way every so often.
He wasn't look at me, of course... it looked like he was after Matvey's approval.
I don't know what kind of agreement they had, but I knew Matvey would tell Antosha if he went wrong.
And then...
We saw the one we were meeting with—Yura. He was standing in the crowd, looking confused and lost...
He didn't manage to kill his target. The plan got interrupted.
Maybe he was thinking, why were there so many students and police outside the ballroom?

lines.st: 'What were they fighting for?'

lines.x: Stop your futile resistance right now!
Your actions this night are unlawful! Admit your wrongdoing!
We don't want to hurt you! Cooperate—
Blyat! You hit me!
Filthy beasts! Lunatics!
All streets surrounding the ballroom are under control. We have the suspects in custody here.
Madness... utter madness.
Students out of school, Armies out of their regions... is anyone in Ursus where they should be?
Should we take them in for questioning?
You can't say you don't recognize their uniforms! How many commoners do you think there could be in those schools?
You want to take all these noble sons and daughters back to the station, and wait for the counts and dukes to show up to claim them?
So... do we just let them go?
Use your brain, mudak! There might be assassins among them. Who am I supposed to hand over to the council if they come looking, you?
Gosudar... one more year and I'll be in the Duma and out of this hellhole...
Why did it have to be now? Damn it all!
How much room do we have in the prisons?
Well, if we clear out everyone who's about to lose their head, we might have room for—
...Think carefully. Can our prisons really take so many?
Uh... maybe not?
Of course, of course.
But I know the perfect place to hold these lawless lunatics...
Gosudar-batyushka... can someone tell me how I come back to this trash heap to find a dozen trucks filled with kids waiting for me?
Oh, the police say they're out of space in the jails and needed to borrow Katorga for these prisoners who were causing trouble at the ball.
Never seen the cops so polite! And they left you a letter.
'Honorable'... 'Katorga'... 'useless things'...
Give it to me. I'll read it myself.

lines.st: Honorable Gospodin Pavlovich,
Katorga is already holding plenty of useless things. A few more will hardly make a difference.
My regards on behalf of Duke Treplev.

lines.x: 'Useless things'? That fool of a superintendent has no idea how valuable this opportunity is.
Bring me Gromov. I will be making numerous visits to important people starting tomorrow. He's in charge while I'm away.
Boss got drunk last night, he's not up yet—there must be something in that backstreet bar's drinks!
Mudak, how much am I paying you scum to keep the peace?
Dump a bucket of ice water on his head NOW, and tell him to take good care of our guests.
Not one musbeast gets out of Katorga without my say-so.
You want us to 'take care' of them? You want them alive, or?
My dear Khvoin, I know your little brain can't handle complex instructions, so I'm trying to use language that even YOU will understand.
Do NOT engage in your usual habits. Do NOT touch a single hair on these people's heads... you understand who 'these people' are, don't you?
Tch.
Do not forget who pays you the money that you waste in those dirty little bars. And don't you dare forget my words.
Their lives have been worth more than yours since the day they were born into their noble names.

lines.st: My luck had been really good ever since I ran into Antosha's guys.
I got separated from the others in the crowd that night. Maybe I was just too small, but the cops didn't notice me, and I got out of there on my own.
I didn't know if I would ever see Antosha's crew again. Katorga was completely locked down after that night, and there was no way in.
I thought maybe I was meant to be back on the streets...
It didn't take long for me to decide.
I would go look for them.
Energy pipelines can never be completely blocked off, no matter where you are.
I make a good sewer musbeast.

lines.x: Phew... almost there.
