Good... didn't see anyone on the way... don't seem to be any guards around...
Hmm... is there somebody behind me?
Hello?
You scared me!
Who are you? Why are you in the energy pipes—I mean, I'm here too, but you gotta explain!
Oh, I can explain later, but right now, I could really use some help...
I think I might have misjudged the width of this pipeline before I squeezed in.
Could you maybe give me a push?
Fine... not like I can get out if I don't.
You push too. Hrgh—
Phew... thanks.
I didn't think there'd be somebody else sneaking in with me. Are you looking for someone too?
You too?!
My friends got arrested a couple of days ago. I heard they might be inside, so I came to check it out.
I'm Rosalind, but my friends call me Leto. What about you?
Ukusik... stupid name that my friends gave me.
Ukusik! That's easy to remember.
Is your friend with the Student Assembly?
Student Assembly? Never heard of it. We've got our own name, the Unbound!
Cool name! But I've never heard it either.
I figure they must be good people, if you're crawling through energy pipes to help them.
They're... really good people. And my home is here.
...Home?
Excuse me! Have you seen any other students around here?
Good heavens, did you just crawl out of the sewers or something?
Well, yeah actually.
Alright, that's close enough. We can talk at this distance. Gosudar...
Wait, you're from the Self-Government Group... I almost mistook you for those Unbound tramps.
Unbound...
Rude, uncouth ruffians... their leader is the worst of the lot. Who does he think he is, acting like he's in charge? What titles do his parents hold?
You saw Antosha? Where are they?!
Just go east from here, and you'll find them behind those filthy factory buildings.
Don't thank me, just... keep moving.
Naum... why don't we go back?
We don't know the situation, and those thugs don't look like they can be reasoned with... besides, I heard there are already students who have gone missing.
Enough, 'Pencil Stub'. You want to hang out with those peasants, you go back on your own. I will not stay and listen to another uncouth word they say.
Hey! Why are you talking about them like that?
What's going on? Who locked you up? What's up with this factory?
We have no idea. The cops grabbed us the night before last outside the ballroom. We're not sure why they took us here.
No cops in this place, but it's patrolled by some street thugs. I overheard them say that the man in charge is named Pavlovich...
I'll remember that. There will be hell to pay when I get out of here.
We must be here by some mistake. I don't know how the misunderstanding happened, but I don't plan on accepting his apology so easily.
Did you sneak in from outside? Is there a way out?
You could get out through the energy pipes, but I'm not sure if big guys like you will fit.
Maybe we, er...
What? You want to crawl through these pipes that can barely fit a musbeast?
I guarantee somebody will be here to pick us up soon.
Shh—someone's coming!
I swear I saw something go past!
You swear? Hah, mochi perkhoti, just fart next time, at least you'll make a sound!
What a waste of time! Even tuskbeasts know to look for a dry slope to dig a hole in on a day like this, and we gotta watch this stupid hole on this ugly wall!
You still got booze?
Blyat, stop drinking! We only need to watch this hole for another day, then someone will be here to fill it up. You give me that look again, and I'll smash your skull with this bottle!
Oh, you wanna see whose skull is harder? Go on, try. You better kill me in one hit, because if you don't, I'm gonna kill you and sell your skin to Gromov for booze.
(Seething) Alright, you want a fight, you'll get one! Chort, I love your crazy. Say, you wanna try some wine made from blood?
Human blood? You can make wine from human blood?
Tuskbeast blood, dura. Whose blood did you think it was, mine? I'm not as crazy as you.
Say... how far do we have to haul this?
Beats me. Hide it where nobody goes. Pavlovich won't let us do this stuff.
I hate taking orders from that mudak.
What can you say, he pays the bills.
I'm tired. What do these students eat? How did they get so fat?
Hey, I've got an idea.
There's a hole here, and we've got a thing. We put the thing in the hole—
And we'll be free to go drink.
You're a damned genius!
Come, I'll take you to my vodka stash.
Oh, how sweet. Come, lemme give you a big, warm hug...
What are they doing...?
What's in that sack?
They watch from the shadows as the thugs stuff a filled sack into the pipeline.

The sack gets stuck, and the woman irritably pulls it open, revealing black pants and shoes covered in mud and dirt—looking suspiciously like a school uniform. She tries to stuff the leg deeper into the sack.
(Whispers) Shh! Shut up!
I told you, I saw something.
Sure, sure, smart guy.
Pavlovich says we can't kill them.
He was talking about the nobles, mudak... besides, there must be hundreds of them. He wouldn't know if a few went missing.
You... you're going to...
No... no...
I'll hold them off! Go on without me—
Don't be a hero! Look at their weapons!
Run—!
Did you see how many there were?
We would have been screwed if we fought them!
Are these the people watching over this turf?
Who are they? Why do they have military-grade weapons, if they're not cops?
No idea. Here, they're the same as the police... all meanies.
Didn't you say Antosha's guys were here? I didn't see them.
Looks like this one's scared stupid.
Hey, Leto, we gotta find a way to get around this corner. Do you see those two—
Block 7 clear. You can come out and clean now.
Antosha! Found you!
Ukusik?
What are you doing here? I thought you got away that night—
You're alive! Some people said you're dead, some people said you got locked up, I didn't know what to do.
Where's Matvey? Are you alright? Are you listening to me?
We're fine. We'll be even finer if you raise your voice any louder and draw the attention of those thugs.
Hey! Stop making fun of me!
We're fine. Matvey, Yura... everyone's here.
Ukusik!
Uwah...
Well... glad you're alright.
You... you killed people...
You're barbarians... murderers...
Where are you going? Come back!
Forget him... where did you find this fool?
Picked him up over there.
This is not a shelter. We don't have time for people like these.
So we chase them away? Is it okay if those thugs kill them?
Antosha, you need to be careful. You may not care whether he lives or dies, but allowing him to run around may draw unwanted attention.
Antosha! Someone's coming!
She's armed, and there's blood on her weapon. She looks dangerous.
Just one? I'll deal with her.
Wait, she's not a threat—
General!
I thought those bastards had rounded up all the students in the area. Looks like you've protected a good bunch.
Your name's Antosha? I'm Sonya.
You're a student at University of Deity Grypherburg too?
Not exactly... but I'm working with them, for now.
I heard your people surrounded the ballroom that night just to shout a few slogans.
Yeah, it wasn't the best idea.
I don't know Grypherburg so well... what can you tell me about what's going on? What is this place?
This is Katorga Raion, a former penal industrial plate. It's been derelict for a long time, and even the power supply has been cut.
I heard the city was planning to abandon the place entirely and discard it in the wilderness.
But there are so many people here now, including us...
I'm guessing it's because of the aristocratic students on your side.
The police didn't want to have to deal with them, so they sent you here... Katorga is nominally a place for the government to hold criminals, after all.
Alright. I guess it's not that complicated.
The problem is, Katorga is now being run by a bunch of lunatics.

Armed with weapons that no one knows how they got, killing for the sheer fun of it... something seems to be holding them back, for now, but no one knows what will happen if things continue on like this.
Maybe we can work together.
How many people do you have?
Well... they're not exactly my people, but there are around two hundred students trapped here with me.
Spoiled nobles aren't good for much, no matter how many there are.
I'm in no position to protect you.
General Zima doesn't need your protection!
At least we want the same thing, for now. And if you can trust what you just saw me do, you can believe that we'll fight those thugs and get out of here together.
Sonya is silent for a long time, then takes a big step forward, and Antosha follows at almost the same time.
Antosha extends his hand first.
Sonya takes it. They shake hands briefly, then quickly break apart.
Sorry for attacking you.
It's all good. Fists can talk, and yours told me you're an okay guy. Where did you learn your moves?
Plenty of opportunities on the streets.
Let me make this clear: just because we're working together doesn't make us allies. Our camps will remain separate, but we can spare you some supplies.
Much appreciated. We will do as you say, and make these supplies count. We can discuss joint operations when the time comes.
Deal. See you around, Sonya.
And take your friends... minus one now, I suppose.
(Shivers)
...Thank you for protecting them.
Thanks for the help, little Ukusik.
Don't call me that—
Ugh, never mind. You be careful. See ya.
You look terrible, General! Are you alright?
I'm fine... how's everyone? Anybody hurt?
Zoya's got a scratch, but nothing serious.
Good.
I didn't think you would come in here on your own... did Istina plan this?
Couldn't wait for a plan. I was afraid it might be too late, so I left a note and came.
Sorry for acting without permission. If you're mad—
No...
Thank you, Leto.
Hey, not so tight! That's maybe a little too much... Sonya?
Are you...
Are you scared?
Don't be stupid.
It's alright! I'm here now. Put us together, and we can take down anything.
If two fists won't do it, add two more!
Besides, there are so many people out there, and so many more fists!
Good point, Leto.
I won't be scared anymore.
'Sonya.' The name is unfamiliar to us. She was not one of them.
I know. I won't take it out on her.
...I'm just reminded of the professor.
Same here, Antosha.
Do you remember why I was the first person you thought of when you formed the Unbound?
You were one of the few in the old gang who came from commoner stock. You knew hardship, knew how to produce, and how to survive in Ursus.
Yes, survive. Only through survival can we achieve our ideals. We have to get out of this alive.
The others need your command now. You must pull yourself together.
Yura, why does Antosha look so terrible?
That one's wearing a Student Assembly badge. That was our design, from back when we were all in the Petrachevsky Group.
The Petrachevsky Group? What's that?
No one told you? Antosha was the first leader of the Petrachevsky Group. After the death of our professor, we were reported by the other students and expelled.
But others escaped punishment because of their upbringing, and they continue to do stupid, despicable things under the group's old name.
Especially their leader, Olga! We will never forgive her!
This Petrachevsky Group... several dukes had children in it, and a group went to His Imperial Majesty to beg for amnesty.
Wait a second.
Who's this Petrachevsky?
Professor of Literature at the University of Deity Grypherburg, and one of those traitors who printed pamphlets slandering the tsar. How could you not know the name?
There are more traitors in the universities than papers they've published! How am I supposed to remember them all?
Order!
(Whisper) Your Honor, the next two witnesses are of the nobility. They may need more time to prepare...
...Very well.
While some of this information has already been made public, we will now once again review Sonya's deeds in Katorga Raion...
Say that again!
The Vanguards will not be retrieving Leonid's corpse. Did you get it this time?
His corpse? He's warming himself up by the fireplace right now, laughing at idiots like you!
You just want to wait here your whole life, fighting over scraps of food and firewood!
I knew you Vanguards were useless imbeciles the moment you started yelling about rescuing Lavrya by force!
Go ahead then, go kneel before those thugs. I want to see if you really can get out, or if you'll be sent back like Shorty.
We're off—
Hold it!
Where are you going? You think those assholes will listen to you?
You guys really are still stuck in the same rut, huh...
Rosalind? What are you doing here?
I came to help Sonya, and to stop you dumbasses from throwing your lives away while I'm at it!
Hmph. Why worry about what they're doing...?
Yesterday, when that guy named Fedya carried Shorty's body back, they were still making snide remarks.
...Listen, it is dangerous out there. Those thugs will not let you walk away, no matter how much you pay them.
You think it's true just because you said so? Who the hell do you think you are? You saw Shorty bribe them with your own eyes, did you?
I—
His pockets were so clean, not even lice would live in them. How could he ever come up with the idea of bribing someone? He must have been killed when trying to break out.
That's just a guess, but those guys who call themselves the 'Council of Sixteen' aren't the kind of people you can bargain with.
Sonya... When you were away, someone sent us a letter. It's from Naum, from the Symposium.
He writes: 'The leader of the Council of Sixteen, Gromov, is a reasonable man. So long as you have enough money, we can walk free.'
Where's the letter?
Here.
Is that all? Are we done? Just let us leave this damned place already.
Wait.
You've got no grounds to stop us, Sonya! Not even you!
Out of our way!
He rashly pushes his way through the crowd, reaching out to grab hold of Zima's sleeve.
Blam! A loud slap slams into his face.
It is almost as if the slap has pushed some button, when everyone grinds to a halt.
Wake up already! Don't you understand what this letter means?

You Symposium people are writing day in, day out. Would any of you have handwriting this sloppy? It's practically going off the page. The best possible outcome here is that he's trading your lives for a meal.
That's not true—
You seriously haven't figured it out? Or do you like keeping your head stuck in the sand? Still stubbornly believing in a way out of here that doesn't involve fighting back?
Then... What should we do?
Save lives.
This letter and Shorty should be enough proof that the Council of Sixteen is dangerous. We can't just sit by and watch as Leonid drags a bunch of people to their deaths.
If only one of them still lives, I'll bring them back. If they're all still alive, I'll bring them all back.
Do you have a death wish too, Sonya?
If they got caught, that's just proof they were stupid and weak. They deserve to die—
Shut up, Faddey.
I'm sick of you always insulting the other students. We need unity, if we want to keep everyone alive.
Unity? Hah! This empire was built by throwing weaklings like these Symposians into the river, one by one!
So, when Ursus finally got thrown into the river, you got pulled along with it, huh?
There's no Vanguard or Symposium here. No nobles or commoners.
There's only one thing we are in the eyes of that 'Council of Sixteen': fresh meat ready for butchering.

Yesterday, they killed Shorty. Tomorrow, they'll squish each and every one of our heads like helpless bugs. And right now, we're bickering our asses off. They don't need to split us up, we're doing it for them.
Even so, those slowing us down—
What about you, Faddey?
When have you ever contributed a damn thing? Or is your 'greatness' just an empty shell, only able to be filled by watching the weak fall apart?
Keep your stupid superiority complex, it'll keep you company while you wait to turn into a corpse!
As for everyone else... If you don't feel like dying a miserable death in a place like this, grab something you can crack a few skulls with.
I'm not asking you all to like the Symposium or anyone else, not even for a second... but right now, you gotta keep up with me if you want everyone to live!
The air seems to have frozen as she finishes her speech. Nobody dares to break the silence.
Until Leto spots a hand. A student cautiously raises his hand, the hesitance still clear on his face. But he is the first of his peers to answer her.
'Pencil Stub'! 'Pencil Stub', right? Whaddya feel like saying?
I... support Sonya's idea.
Those who left are our peers, our friends. We can't abandon them.
But if possible, call me by my real name. I'm—
I support her too! Whether they're dead or alive, I just want to see how they really are!
I'm with her—
Several students stand up, then more, and even more. They gather by Sonya's side.
Good. Ten or so of you should be enough to make a scouting party.
I know a lot of you are still skeptical, but don't worry. I'll bring an answer back to you.
...Count me in.
Are you thinking of—
Don't overthink it. I just want to prove I'm right, so I can slap those Symposium cowards in the face.
So, what do we do? Just give us the order, Sonya.
First, we need to find a route we can use to flank the Council of Sixteen—
Err, Antosha told me to send you guys some supplies.
Have I come at a bad time?
Perfect timing, actually. I was just thinking of going to your camp to get a guide, Matvey.
If a fight breaks out, I'll make sure you're safe.
Don't underestimate me, Sonya.
Antosha wants to kill Gromov, but we were never able to find his lair.
But luckily, our attempts to scout it out have led us to several of the thugs' active bases. We've got their details down—
Trouble up ahead, Sonya!
Suka! They're getting closer!
What do we do, Nika? You always have ideas.
Don't panic, Yeremey, in just a moment—
The door bolt won't hold much longer!
What about the window, Nika? If we can't hold here, can we—
No go. There's two of them outside the window, and they've got steel pipes.
Come here and help me brace against this table. It's our last line of defense.
Her voice wavers as she thrusts a shiny kitchen knife into her friend's hands, pressing both hands down on the table corner like her life depends on it.
Yeremey takes a deep breath, pushing against the table's edge with his entire body. Though his forehead is covered in cold sweat, his face does not show a hint of cowardice.
Hey there, honored 'guests'.
Don't bother trying to resist. We just wanna talk 'business'.
Yeah, it's below twenty out here. Let us in already, we're freezing. Is this how kids these days treat visitors?
If you don't open up, our 'service charge' is gonna go up to... say, an arm.
Get lost!
There's a ton of Originium-tipped bolts in this room pointed right at the door! Come any closer and you die!
Pfft. Originium-tipped bolts? You hear that, Pacient? She's got Originium-tipped bolts!
Oooh, I'm so scared! Hahahaha—

I'd believe you if you said you managed to rustle up some borscht in this cesspit, but Originium-tipped bolts? Pull the other one. I've already taken the Originium out of every contraption in the area.
Well, if you kids don't want to play nice, then don't blame us for what's next.
Remember, keep them alive, otherwise we can't answer to the boss. You're up first, Pacient!
It feels as if every swing of the axe is hacking at the students' minds. A crack opens up in the door, and a filthy, tattooed hand forces its way in, trying to unlatch the bolt.
(Quietly) Now.
Here's a one-way trip back to the hospital, Pacient!
He bellows as he lunges at the trespassing hand, stabbing it with his knife.
Argh! My hand! That punk actually stabbed me!
Smash the door down! Skin those little bastards alive!
The axe blows intensify, the wooden door now riddled with cracks. Snow-laden wind pours into the room as several tall shadows gather around the door, forming a wall of despair.
...Listen, Yeremey.
If they catch us, they'll take us back and torture us... so don't hesitate, whether you have to do it to me, or to yourself.
Got it.
Nika, if we live through this, I—
Save it for after we live through it! They're coming! Aim for the throat!
The thugs grin wickedly as they pass through the doorframe, brandishing their steel pipes. Yeremey closes his eyes in desperation, readying his crude weapon for one last strike—
But the pain never comes. The Ursus who was oh-so arrogant earlier flies through the air like a burlap sack, slamming into the snow-covered ground outside. There is no further movement from him.
Who dares—ARGKH!
I do. Got that?
The tall figure blocking the doorway does not even have time to turn his head before a hand bashes it against the frame.
Zima steps over his collapsed body, flicking the blood off her hands.
Y-You're...
Hey hey, General Zima's here to save you.
Finally—
She cannot stop the tears from flowing, her tense shoulders collapsing from relief.
Don't worry, just take your time telling us what happened. We're here to help.
Were you with Leonid?
Leonid?
He's dead...
Those bastards came up with something: an 'auction'.
Their boss Gromov cheated us. He said we'd be able to buy our freedom as long as we had enough money.
But it was all a lie. It turned into a slaughterhouse.
Gromov had his people grade everyone like meatbeasts. The nobles with money were led to a building, and the commoners... I don't know what happened to them.
Thankfully, Yeremey was suspicious, and he didn't go straight in. We had to run for our lives to escape their pursuit.
As for Leonid, he was full of confidence when he tried to 'discuss' things with Gromov...
He's buried here?
Da, behind the building.
Nika and I both saw it. One of the bastards dragged him over and was looting him for his clothes and watch.
At the time, we thought we had managed to escape their base. Seeing that made me feel faint.
Nika grabbed a crowbar and gave that scumbag a surprise attack when he wasn't looking.
We hid in his house, and we made it through the night, but we never expected his friends to show up at the door on the second day.
I killed a man... but this was the only way we could avenge Leonid.
Something's off.
We're still some distance away from the gang's base. They might come here on occasion to loot things, but they'd never actually live here, but you said this was one of their houses...
But he took a spade and some rations from this house. I thought—
No need to be so tense. Where did you bury him? I want to confirm his identity.
Why... are there corpses by the door?
...What did you people do to my house?
Your house, gospozha?
Where... Where's my husband? Have you seen him? He's just an ordinary worker, wearing a gray jacket. It's the last bit of warm clothing we have...
All the color drains out of Nika and Yeremey's faces in an instant. They give a subconscious glance towards the mound of dirt.
Y-You don't mean—
...Dig him up.
The first thing to be unearthed is the deceased's patchwork gray jacket, followed by his cheeks, his head... and the dark red crack across his temple.
The woman crouches by her husband, her body shaking like a rusty machine as she strokes his face. It is the coldest thing she has touched in her entire life.
I-I didn't know, I really didn't.
We thought he was with that Council of Sixteen because he was taking Leonid's clothes!
Council? Clothes?
Why can't we take things off the dead people Gromov kills?
We've been doing this for two whole months since they stopped all work here! What's wrong with making a living?! What do you know?!
You... You students, you murderers—
We're not—
We're very sorry, gospozha.
Forgive me, madam... Here, this watch is pure gold! And these silver coins... Take them! Please don't cry!
I'm so, so sorry! There's also these things we took from those thugs.
Without a word, Sonya pulled out her rations and essentials, placing them before the woman.
The other students were stunned for a moment, then silently began offering up whatever supplies they had managed to find.
...Ma'am. We were locked in here not long ago and had no idea what it was really like. Those atrocities... everyone has been on edge.
But regardless... we made mistakes, and we will take responsibility for them.
We will accept whatever punishment you deem fit.
Please, take this as a token of our regret... Our camp is just nearby. We will do everything we can to help you and your child get through this.
I am truly sorry. I was the one who acted. It had nothing to do with Yeremey, Sonya, or the others. If you must punish someone, punish—
The woman lifts her head. There is no desire in her eyes, merely an empty hate.
She grabs the coins and the watch, throwing them at Nika's face.
GET OUT!
Take your blood money with you! You think you can buy Ivan's life with these pieces of metal? You think it will bring back the father of my children?!
You can do anything, can't you? You dare to kill, yes? Then why didn't you dare to kill the man who did all of this? You can all go to hell!
If we weren't forced to live like this... Why would my husband become a robber and rob the dead of their clothes? Why would we have to become such wretched things...?
Alright then.
If it'll bring you some peace or closure, we'll do it.
Both for you, and for our friends... I swear to you, Gromov, who caused all of this, will die this winter.
Please, take care of yourself... When we smash open the gate to the quarantine zone, we will all get out of here together.
If that's the case...
Have Nika and Yeremey show you the way, Sonya. I'll head back and get help from Antosha.
Sure.
Everyone else, with me. This is our new mission.
She pulls up Nika, slumped against the ground. She leads the students into the snowstorm, where they fade from sight.
(Sobs)...
Wh-Why are you still here? To laugh at me?!
Not long after I was born, my mother had to bury my father on her own. He was killed by bandits.
You—
Your husband was no criminal, and he never hurt anyone. He fought for you and your children, until the very end.
Don't let his sacrifice be in vain. Take everything he fought so hard for... and live.
He takes the gold watch she threw away, forcing it into the icy palm of her hand, and folds her fingers around it.
Glug. Glug.
I watch the bubbles in the water cooler. They rise up in an unending stream, and then they pop.
Many people are walking out of the dour hall, taking advantage of the arbiter calling a recess to stretch their legs, and voice their opinions on the matter while they are at it.

In my moment of distraction, the water overflows, spilling onto the floor. The noblewoman behind me languidly moves away from the puddle, afraid the 'pure snowmelt from Sami' would damage her worn leather boots.
Bozhe moy, I once had the exact same pair...
I quickly spin my wheelchair, attempting to flee.
Varvara? Is that you?
I can hardly believe it. You look...
Help me carry these books, they're too heavy!
I need to save my strength for tonight's script reading—No, you can't come! This is a student group internal event.
...Are you surprised?
No, Varvara. That's not what I mean.
We were childhood friends. The bond between nobles is not so easily broken.
Do you still think of me as a noble when you see me like this?
What do you—
Did you not hear what Zoya and that other girl said?
Why would that Arbiter twist everything we have endured?
Ha, haha. Looking at my trousers?
It's fine, look as much as you like. It's not going to bring my shins back.
Bozhe moi...
Varvara... This is... O, bozhe moi!
The votes been tallied yet?
Yeah.
The boss decided that, from now on, we're the 'Sixteen Warriors'.
But why?! I read in an old book that the first sixteen to follow Igor Velikiy got a title that meant 'councilmember', so 'Council' is the only choice!
Shut up about your stupid theories... Besides, if we're a 'Council', then we gotta respect a vote, right? Right now everyone thinks 'Warriors' sounds better.
Blyat. I get less and less happy making this money.
It's not just the name change. Now we suddenly need to keep track of our results, see who can handle the most kids...
Enough whining. Saw you slacking off yesterday, you want the boss to scream his head off at you?
Shut up. I sent one of them off last night.
Who?
The one who said he was 'pure Grypherburger stock', Leonid Gelashvili or something.
I checked some Grypherburg copies of the Almanac of Nobility, didn't see the family there. Then I decided to check some chronicles. Turns out, they're just an ordinary family from the south.
The boss only wanted real nobles, so I handled him.
*sigh* Why bother going to all that trouble? Could've just listened to his accent. Did he sound like a Grypherburger?
Accent? I've been shut in this damn place for too long, almost forgot what the locals are supposed to sound like.
Hey, you, you a Grypherburger?
He gives his seat a pat, and he gets a yelp of fear in return. A student kneels on the ground underneath his buttocks, serving as his chair.
I-I-I-I'm a Grypherburger!
I've got the accent, I've got family! Please, let me go, gospodin!
If I remember right... You're not supposed to speak while you're being a chair. The boss is gonna get real mad at me if he sees this.
So shut your mouth, alright? If you stay nice and quiet for an hour, I won't see you off today.
Alright, enough. These kids don't have it easy, what with you terrorizing them all day.
You, lecturing me?
You're the guy who's happy to sit on a stiff corpse.
Upon hearing her comrade's words, the thug pulls her knife out of her 'cushion', warm blood dripping off its blade.
I like sitting cross-legged, doesn't matter to me if they're dead.
...Hey, that little countess there? She's dragging some other girl along with her, think she's a noble too—
Save your strength, dearie. There's nowhere for you to run with all of us here.
No, I beg you—
I gave Gromov all my money. He said I'm a noble, and that I'll leave here alive.
You gave it to him, but not to me. Besides, I don't care about the money.
I only care about order, understand? I'll say it clearly, no fighting in the dorm. Who said you could hit that Symposithingy boy?
I didn't hit anyone! I just gave him a push—
Excuses! I told you kids a thousand times, fighting is wrong! When will you kids actually listen?
You need to be punished.
...Punished... what?
Hey, Warriors! Beat the life outta this spoiled little princess. I'll think of what to say to Gromov.
You got it!
Varvara closes her eyes tight. A gust of wind sweeps by her cheek, and a few drops of warm liquid splash across her forehead.
She shudders as she opens her eyes. The raised stick is gone, along with its master.
Who's next?!
Zima stands before Varvara, waving about a bloodstained steel pipe as she bellows out her challenge.
There are more footsteps and angry shouts, but they are soon replaced by cries of pain.
Hey! Don't even think about running!
Aren't you guys the Warriors now? How come even an Originium slug can take more punches than you?
I've got them!
We've cut off their escape route too, Sonya! They're not going to get away!
Before long, the nearby Warriors are sprawled out across the ground. Leto pats the dust off her hands, giving one of their heads a good kick before moving back to Sonya's side.
All taken care of, General.
Great! Time for a break.
Zima crouches down, stretching out a hand to Varvara.
Though Zima's face is still stained with blood, it is the face that has brought her the most relief these past few days.
You're... Varvara? There are our people here?
Chyort... Just how many Vanguards were captured...?
Not important. Focus on saving people.
Can you still stand, Varvara?
Sonya!
*sob*... Sonya, Faddey, I thought I was going to die...
Do I remember that you're the daughter of a soldier? Dry your tears.
It's fine, seriously.
Mm... Right.
Listen, we're here to get everyone back.
Is it just you here? Where are the other students being held?
They're... They're in the building on the north side.
Gromov said the 'VIP Lounge' and 'Common Waiting Area' were there. There's still lots of students trapped in there, but I know the way, at least.
Lead the way.
Varvara tugs on Zima's hand, using her strength to stand. Though she still trembles, the light has returned to her eyes.

It is the light of a drowning girl who has grabbed onto a buoy. Though she does not know what exactly lies behind that door, she believes that as long as Sonya is with her, it is an exit out of this forsaken place.
We've gotten everyone out, General.
Those thugs were pretty much all bark. Most of the people who were captured are still alive, but... they've been through a lot.
Speaking of the thugs, been a while since we saw them. Almost feels like something's off, haha.
Shut up. You're the only one who likes those bastards.
This building's too close to the exit. It'll be easy to spot us. We can't wait for everyone to calm down before we act.
Pencil Stub, get everyone organized, then lead the way. Rosalind, hold the rear with me.
Got it, General.
Hah. You see? Nicknames are easier to work with, da?
The rescued students, several dozen in all, are huddled along the road like canned fins. Some of them had their jackets taken away, their faces streaked with tears.
But with Pencil Stub and his team's coaxing, they slowly stand up and follow their lead, heading towards their camp.
Finally. We're saved.
The sun is out. Let's go, quickly. I'd rather die than go back to that blasted place.
Wait. What's that sound?
Someone's coming. Hide in the buildings, and don't do anything stupid!
Before anyone can react, the Sixteen Warriors appear at the very back of the group, escorting a burly Ursus.
Shrieks break out at the sight of them, and everything immediately devolves into chaos. A few people shout, trying to maintain order, but to no avail.
Stay calm! I'll handle them!
Oh? You must be the Sonya they were talking about.
You're pretty small, aren't you? But you sure can fight.
You Gromov? What're you doing here?
Haha. Your fellow students were too hasty, forgot a few important things.
Seeing as some people came to the auction, but want to leave without buying a ticket... I've got no choice but to teach them a lesson. Personally.
There's one part you got wrong. I'm the only one you'll be facing.
Just you?
What, scared?
That weapon you've got looks like a hammer and an axe had a baby. Fearsome.
Didn't think its master would be a spineless coward.
...Pfft. Hahahaha—
You're the third one to get a laugh out of me today, little bear. The other two, I already dumped in the snow. They're wishing they had never been born.
Come, take a good look at my weapon!
What the—
It is an ebon maw, a voracious abyss.
Are they pushing a... cannon?
Ready—
Get to cover!

The pitch-black muzzle slowly rises, the grinding of gears piercing the silence. Panic breaks out as people scramble to hide themselves where they can, holding their breath as they wait for the cannon's roar.
Run! To the buildings by the road!
Fire!
For a moment, all sound is driven out of Katorga. All that remains is a keen ringing in the ears.
Zima pokes her head out of a snowbank, her sight blurred by blood. Though she leapt out of the center of the blast, shrapnel has left a gash across her forehead.
Under a layer of dust, a scorched, black pit mars what was once level ground. Flames climb their way up the wooden doors. Around her, there are the bleeding, the injured, the fallen.
Wh... Why?! Most of us are noble!
Because you pissed me off, you snot-nosed little intellectual.
There's only one real rule among the Sixteen Warriors: have your last words ready if you ever make me angry!
Ready the second round—
Get everyone out of here, Rosalind! I'll draw their fire! That's an order!
Dammit!

Gromov's laughter can still be heard through the artillery barrage. He does not bother aiming, wantonly raining down fire across the area. Watching pathetic insects scurry about is his greatest joy, after all.
The ramshackle buildings sway. Varvara had been through too much today. She stands by a stone pillar, her eyes blank...
Move!
AHH!
M-My legs, I—
Oh, no no no no NO, I can't feel my legs!
...Save it. You're still alive.
Faddey! You're bleeding! I need to—
...No. Don't you get it? Just run.
Take that Varvara girl with you, and run. All of you. Don't bother about me...
I said, RUN!
Take care, Faddey...
Grab onto my shoulders, Varvara. You're still alive, so just hang on—
As the girls fade into the distance, Faddey lets out a deep breath. The last vestige of his consciousness is beginning to scatter.
...So that's what it feels like... to get something done... to be a hero...
The perfect time... for graduation day...
Ahh... Feels good to let out all that pent-up frustration that's been building up these past few days.
Keep going, don't give them any time to breathe.
Alright, I'm on—ARGH!
Gromov leaps aside as a crossbow bolt sprouts out of his lackey's chest. He looks towards its source: a high-rise, from which more bolts are coming.
The Unbound? It's that Antosha again!
C'mon, keep loading more shells! I'll bury him along with the students!
Gromov! Stop!
Your reckless actions have alarmed Gospodin Pavlovich, and he demands that you cease firing at once. If you dare hurt another noble, he'll have your hide!
Hey, Boss... Do we retreat?
Retreat? Forgotten how to fight without a cannon, have we?
Go catch Antosha! If you don't deal with him, it'll be your hides on the line!
Now get lost!
You got it!
People covered in bandages throng around tonight's bonfires, repeating their experiences today to anyone within earshot, relishing in the joy of the survivor.
Leto still has energy to burn, so she and a few students with medical knowledge run around the camp, making themselves useful.
As for Nika, Yeremey and Pencil Stub, they sit together in silence, fidgeting with the firewood.
Varvara lies in a deep sleep after receiving treatment. She dreams of the parts of her body she has lost forever... as well as her peers, also gone for good.
The noble girl's alright now. Matvey has brought people to look after her and the other wounded.
Thank you. No amount of thanks could express what we feel. Matvey and the others are professionals when it comes to treating wounds. The Unbound has done so much for us.
Heh. Those non-producing nobles will never understand that workers are far more capable than they are. Even if you start with no skills, as long as you want to survive, Ursus will always 'teach' you.
That's why I can't understand why you'd waste medicine and energy on these people. They're not worth the effort.
I was the one who took them with me, and I promised them I'd bring everyone back. I saved a few people, but others... They believed in me, but they couldn't come back with us.
Either way, you did all you could. The camp here is much more crowded. You brought back most of them. Mission accomplished.
But I still have to warn you. Don't expect anything from those spoiled princelings and princesses. There might come a day when you regret saving their sorry hides.
Don't try and deny it, Sonya. You and I both know how few nobles there are who recognize the need to fight for themselves. You should rely on people with more determination.
You're wrong, Antosha.
Look at the faces around the bonfire. Doesn't matter if they're noble or common, there's always someone with their fists clenched tight.
As long as they haven't given up on resisting, as long as the fire still burns inside them... I won't turn my back on anyone.
I need them. They can become fighters.
You're delusional.
There's only ever a small subsection of the people who are actually decisive. You should pick a team of smart, hard-working, ordinary students, and come with me.
Once we get rid of the two in charge, we'll be out of here quick.
Thanks, Antosha, but I've already made my decision.
When the crisis hits, no one can stay out of it. I will turn them into a real unit. No one gets left behind.
Doesn't matter if it's Gromov, Pavlovich, or those assholes pushing the cannon while they look down on us—
We'll knock them all to the ground!
Today's operation might've given you prestige, but it's also given you blind faith.
I don't understand how those soft-handed weaklings who can't even hold a weapon tight are meant to take down those madmen, and that cannon.
As long as they can walk and make a fist, they can do it. I'll start by teaching them how to march.
Past experience tells me that, with the right tactics, even a weakling can be worth ten men.
As for the cannon, all we can do is wait for the right opportunity. We can't take it head-on, for now at least.
Maybe... My friends can bring us some opportunities.
Your friends? The ones outside Katorga?
Yeah.
How can you be so sure they're working on helping you?
I've got absolutely zero doubt they are.
You can't imagine the things we've been through together.
There is one thing I must reiterate, my dear.
If you are only here to return the book, and are still unwilling to consider my prior suggestion, then leave it by the fireplace, and off you go.
Do you really mean that if I don't agree with your method, you won't even say another word to me?
Were this any other time, I would be happy to entertain your adorable follies of youth and talk with you into the wee hours of the night.
I have missed much, after all. About you, your parents, and what you experienced in Chernobog...
I can just as well tell you all of this now.
But I am in no position to listen.

Even when faced with a choice between life or death, I was unable to persuade you to accept my arrangements: to leave Grypherburg and lie low, or at least submit a testimony that brings you only benefit.
I could not protect you, which leaves me ashamed to face your parents. How could I have the right to learn anything about them from you?
It's not like that, Countess—
Have you read the book?
I have, cover to cover. I now understand why you lent it to me.
What does it say on the title page?
'There is no cause worth sacrificing a beautiful life.'
Indeed, indeed. Yakov Petrov's Confessions, published posthumously by his family. A discussion about a traitor's experiences, bought with his life. So, I simply do not understand...
If you already know that people have paid the ultimate price for these experiences, and you still have the freedom to choose another path, then why must you repeat the mistakes of the past?
Surely you do not have to be on your deathbed, perhaps even choking on blood in prison like he did, to know what you believe in is doomed to be a flash in the pan, forgotten by history?
Countess, I...
Tell me, child. Tell me why.
...To be honest, I have asked myself the same question. But if...
Forgive my shamelessness, but I have a request of you.
If I write my testimony as you say and save myself, can you promise me that the other members of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group will be treated equally as well?
Of course! So long as you do as those people want, and list out some specific names in your testimony—
Very well. I will do as you say.
I will submit a testimony like this one to the hearing...
A 'confession'.
Countess?
Ah, yes, I'm listening. What did you say?
Pardon me. I simply wished to notify you that the arbiter has just mentioned Baryshnya Rostova. He will require you to hand over her testimony in a moment.
Our next witness is Baryshnya Natalya Rostova. Due to special circumstances, she is unable to attend in person today.
However, she has requested that her testimony be read by someone else, on her behalf.
Your Honor—
Baryshnya Rostova sent me a letter yesterday. I'd like to request the committee to look over said letter, and permit me to read it aloud.
As the parliamentarian accepts the letter in Absinthe's hand, the whispers in the gallery grow and grow. Countess Vorontsova senses countless gazes upon her. She shakes her head.
Very well. The hearing asks Young Zoya to recite what knowledge Baryshnya Rostova offers about this incident on her behalf.
'To the honorable and esteemed ladies and gentlemen of the committee, this is a confession...'
'Due to my remorse, and the sensitive nature of the contents of this letter, I will not mention the specific names of any nobles, save for Pavlovich, who must be discussed.'
(Quietly) Countess, what we said was to—
Hear her out.
'...I hope this will be sufficient to win your trust.'

lines.st: 'Not long after the incident at the ball, due to a deep worry over Sonya's safety, I begged a person of influence for aid, successfully contacting the parents of most of the students who were arrested that day.'
'I then learned that all the 'criminals' who trespassed on Tsarevgrad had been locked away in Katorga, the place the people now call the 'quarantine zone'.'

'What surprised me was that, despite there being no small number of illustrious lords and ladies among the parents, they too found it difficult to obtain concrete information on the goings-on in the quarantine zone.'

'Included among them are some who consider themselves of sensitive identity, which rendered it inappropriate for them to visit Katorga. And so, they entrusted me to be the parents' delegate, and bade me visit the arrested students.'
'They recommended I call upon the administrator of Katorga, one Magistrate Pavlovich. To visit him, I climbed the wall that divided the zone from the rest of Terra the following day.'

lines.x: ...Haha, I met with a friend of your father's, Baron Shuvalov. He borrowed heavily, then ran off to Chernobog to invest it all, only to return to Grypherburg with absolutely nothing to his name.

But when I met him the day before yesterday, his hands were shackled, and he was being escorted by two police officers out of the city, to be sent east. My curiosity had me asking him what great crime he had committed to be sentenced to exile.
He had quite the air of mystery as he whispered in my ear that during a banquet, he shouted: 'Long live the miners'.
I was absolutely flabbergasted, so I asked him why. Can you guess what he said?
Forgive me, but nothing comes to mind.
He laughed as he turned to look at the officers with him, saying: 'If I'm exiled, my creditors can't find me, hahahaha.'
What a... unique anecdote. If I didn't have more pressing matters at hand, I would be happy to listen to them all day.
Oh, look at me, such a windbag. Most deserving of your mockery.
Come, my dear Baryshnya Rostova. Let's talk business.
My good magistrate, I am here for—
The shrill whine of a power drill interrupts the conversation. Pavlovich gives Rosa an apologetic wave of the hand before walking to the door.
What's going on? Who's in charge today? Send them to me this instant!
Thousand pardons, sir, we brought in quite a few people last night—
What do I care how many people you have? Don't you know I'm entertaining a guest right now?
I'll have them stop right away.
Terribly sorry about that. What were you going to say?
Pardon my curiosity, but...

Each raion of Deity Grypherburg has its own guard unit, but they are given standardized equipment. I noticed the man you spoke to just now held a weapon, but was wearing plainclothes. Is there something special about Katorga?
Special? Haha, you jest, Baryshnya Rostova, unless you believe a garbage dump to be special.
Ever since Grypherburg's factories received an upgrade, the old industrial zones lay idle. Some councilors suggested they could be refurbished and put to other uses.
Like, for example, having a place to lock up criminals and the poor folk who refuse to move, while also performing some light manufacturing. Two fowls with one stone.
Things started off rather well. If it were not for the shortage of resources these past few months, these factories would not have all shut down.
*Sigh* Ursus has never been one to pay useless places any heed. Proper guards are limited in manpower, and what funds have been given to me are only enough to hire idiots to help manage things.
It's a miracle that these fools haven't caused an accident yet.
That drill earlier did not sound like it was for putting up renovations—
Ah, my humblest apologies if it startled you. Just the dentist at work. I rather wish he would not disturb my guests.
A dentist? Here?
Yes, they drill away cavities, after all. They scrape away the rot, and fill the hole with new materials... No matter if they work with enamel, or thoughts.
Now, I believe your curiosity has been sated. Shall we return to business?
...My apologies for taking us off-track.
You saw my list of names when I first arrived. Their parents have entrusted me to check on their well-being. I hope you can tell me how they are doing.
Especially considering that among these names, there are many heirs of great and powerful nobles. I hope you can be accommodating.
Naturally, naturally. It appears this batch of arrestees really are all students. Oh, pity the hearts of parents everywhere. I know just how worried people of such renown must be about their heirs.
If these children had the least bit of empathy for their parents, why would they display such disgraceful, heartbreaking behavior?
But you must understand just how concerned I am for the future of Katorga.
Before we proceed to the next step of our discussions, I must reiterate that the parents who have entrusted me with this task wish to confirm the condition of their children.
Yes, yes, there'll be plenty of time for you to see how they're doing in a moment.
There happen to be two names on this list that I would like to discuss further with you, Baryshnya Rostova.
By all means.
The first is Naum. As far as I'm aware, he was released yesterday. Most likely already arrived home as you were making your way here.
Thank you for informing me. I shall check with his parents as soon as possible.
Ahem. Next is this girl, Sonya.
She's managed to make quite the name for herself these past few days. I heard about many things involving her from my underlings.
How is she?
Natalya gets the sudden sensation that something has changed in the ever-present smile plastered on Pavlovich's face.
No need to be so tense. I am simply curious myself. She is no noble, nor the daughter of a rich household. Just an ordinary student. So why exactly is she on the list of names?
I had no intention of hiding it from you. It is simple: Sonya is one of my friends, and she is no black-hearted thug, which is why I added her to the list. I beg you, let me check on her.
O, bozhe moi. When the scion of the House of Rostov asks me for aid, how could I ever refuse?

However, you must agree to two things: first, talk to Sonya and get her to sit still without fidgeting about for a few days. I guarantee that she'll be out of the quarantine zone in several days' time.
Secondly, go to the parents you represent, have them pressure the State Council into repealing their proposal and retaining the quarantine zone, by all means available.
'Retaining' the quarantine zone? Do you mean the quarantine will soon be revoked?
Oh my, did our dear Countess Vorontsova not tell you? This is no simple revocation, but rather... pure renunciation.
The exhaustion of the empire's resources is no secret. Ursus is desperate enough to abandon one of the capital's industrial plates, all for the sake of economization.

A week ago, the State Council proposed to cast off the quarantine zone, leaving it to the wilds. This proposal was permitted to move forward by the Chairman, which means His Imperial Majesty must tacitly approve of it.
Fortunately, with the help of some old nobles who support me, this plan has been delayed. But we cannot stave it off forever.

I noticed many renowned industrial nobles on your list. If those nobles can drum up support from their friends and stand as a united front in opposition, I'm sure His Imperial Majesty and the State Council will reconsider.
This is all for the sake of their children's lives. They would not dare be lax. If I receive an edict saying the quarantine zone shall be retained, then I release everyone.
...Do you believe I can do this?
I have hope, at the very least. With only a list of names in hand, you fearlessly strode into this place that all other souls shun, even seeking to save your friend.
And so, everyone's lives are in your hands, Baryshnya Natalya Rostova. Including Sonya's.
I will pass on your requests. But first, I must see her.
Naturally.
Come, Khvoin.
Take this young lady to Sonya. And remember to announce her as Natalya.
We're not far from that sterva—I mean, Sonya's camp. You wait here, I'll go give her a heads-up.
She's already set up a camp here? And do you really need to give her a 'heads-up'?
You're her friend, which means you know you don't mess with her.
The corners of Rosa's mouth curl up into a subtle smile, unbidden. As a gust of wind blows over from the depths of the gloomy street, she turns her head, holding onto her hat.

Suddenly, a gray shadow jumps out of some ruins. Merely a skinny cloudbeast, its skin mange-marked. It stops in the middle of the road, vigilantly watching Rosa as it clamps down on something between its teeth.
Rosa's pupils contract. It is a human finger, pale, stiff, black mud and dried blood staining its cracked nail, the fractured end like a chewed-up branch.
Blyat! Stupid beast!
Are you alright, Natalya?
I... Nothing, it just... No, it's nothing.
It's terribly cold out here. I must trouble you to ask Sonya to come out as quickly as possible.
Right away.
As she watches the man fade from view, a wave of cold seeps down from Rosa's head to her toes. Under its assault, her upright bearing slackens.
She staggers, leaning against a frigid brick wall as she covers her mouth. She forces the bile back down her throat, but she cannot stop the tears streaming from her eyes.
A finger. A shriek from some poor, humiliated soul. A turbid memory of Chernobog. They all flail wildly through her mind.
This is not her first time experiencing this. She can face this alone—
No, you cannot be like this, Natalya. This is unseemly, impermissible, surmountable.
Rosa huddles on the ground, the metallic taste of cold air invading her mouth as she takes deep breaths, trying to stop her arms from shaking—
Natalya?
(Ragged breathing)

You're hyperventilating—
Chyort! Can you hear me, Natalya?
I-I—
Where are you right now?
I'm... I'm... in the quarantine zone...
Yeah, the quarantine zone—Blyat! Why do you all keep coming here one after another? You want to die or something?
Now's not the time for that talk. Listen to me, Natalya. I'm here with you. You are not alone.
Natalya!
Sonya...?
Yeah, it's me. You okay?
Sonya... No, I'm fine. I'm so happy to see you...
And to see that you're fine too.
You're still babbling. How many fingers?
Zima extends three of her fingers, shoving them into Rosa's face.
Three.
Phew. Your brain's in one piece, at least.
I'm fine, really. It was just the wind making me cough, and my heart felt a little uncomfortable because of that. I'm feeling much better now, thank you.
Enough, don't put on an act when you're with me. Did the guy who was looking for me cause you trouble?
I'm really not... *sigh* Forget it.
Listen, Sonya, I can only be here for a short time, so I must catch you up on everything as quickly as possible.
Rosa looks around, hinting to Zima that she should lean in closer.
I know you were sent by the guy in charge.
Let me tell you something first, Leto's already here. Anything else you need to know from me?
Rosalind... She's been insisting on finding you. She left only a note at the branch office before running off.
Don't be too hard on her, she just wanted to come and help me ASAP... I-I wanted to ask, how's everyone doing?
Is Gummy okay? Is Istina mad at me? And Zoya and Instructor Dur-nar...
Everyone's fine, but they're all worried about you.
I myself came to make sure you're safe, as well as this quarantine zone...
I don't know what you've seen so far, but the stuff that's happened here is probably way worse than that.
No food, no fuel, not even clean water. People are forming gangs and fighting everywhere over territory and resources.
Every day, people die.
Pavlovich said he will release everyone, as long as some conditions are met—
Do you really trust a guy like that?
Of course not...
I know there's nothing else you could do. Otherwise you wouldn't have had to ask all over the place for help getting in, just to see how I was doing and tell me the news.
Gotta say, even though everything I said earlier felt scary as hell, and it feels like everyone might just die tomorrow, it's nothing we haven't seen before.
A locked-off city that nobody cares about, even if it explodes, a group of students almost running on instinct, crushing each other to survive...
It's got a familiar ring to it, doesn't it?
Tell me, what do you need right now? I can leave this place, and once I meet up with everyone outside, we'll think of a way—
I need to know how many people are on those fortress-like raion walls. Excluding the thugs.
Not very many. Pavlovich has a few bodyguards. Shouldn't be more than ten, if we include those wearing old army uniforms.
...Not too bad.
Zima leans even closer to Rosa, lowering her voice as low as it will go.
(Whispers) If you can, come up with a laundry list of ideas to cut off their supply of weapons.
(Whispers) Weapons? But the 'security' I saw were hardly professionals.
(Whispers) There's a lot you don't know.
(Whispers) They've been bringing in ammo and heavy weapons every day for the past few days. If every guard on the walls has that kind of firepower, we don't stand a chance.
You mean...
I mean exactly what I said.
...I see. Once we get out, I will talk to the others, and we will figure something out.
Sonya, you and Rosalind need to take care of yourselves. You must.
Don't worry. I'll get out of here, and I'm bringing everybody with me.
Just like before.
'...After that, I went down the list, meeting with each of the students in succession.'
'Unlike Sonya, they were sent to an office by the raion walls to meet with me. Most of them were deeply afraid, too afraid to say anything to me.'
I've had enough! Your Honor, how can an imperial hearing tolerate such absurd, vile slander against an innocent noble?
His Imperial Majesty personally granted him the title of magistrate for this work. If the truth really is as Natalya described, how could he have earned such distinction?
Anyone with ears can tell this 'confession' is actually a denunciation. We cannot be led astray by rumors.
As far as I know, the zone still has a—
No matter how much you admire Pavlovich's 'managerial skills', my lord, please do not dismiss the suffering in Natalya's testimony as rumor.
Just because we're talking inside a warm hall doesn't mean you can deny that there are people outside who are cold and hungry.
If we followed your logic, how could Ursus have enjoyed prosperity for the past several centuries while there is so much suffering on Terra?

Mind your tongue, Young Zoya. The hearing respects you as the daughter of a martyr, and it is because of this trust and our pursuit of justice that we have asked you here to testify, not to besmirch the nobility!
The committee knows I'm protecting a true noble. I won't let anyone casually slander her by dismissing it as a rumor.
Preposterous—
Order!
Young Zoya, your duty is to read the testimony on behalf of Baryshnya Rostova. Only the hearing committee can determine the truth.
...I apologize, Your Honor.
If the committee only cares about the 'confession', that's the next part.
May I continue?
Remember, if you again attempt to pass judgment on any noble's views, I will no longer allow you to speak.
Proceed.

lines.st: 'When I returned to the city and reported what had happened to the parents, some of them asked me to stay longer, wanting to understand more about their children's circumstances.'
'I had to determine who could offer the most aid, for the chance to relieve the suffering of those within the quarantine zone.'
'And so, I chose a few parents to meet with privately, intentionally embellishing the misery of the students' situation.'
'In the end, I found a noble whose only child had been detained, and he eagerly introduced me to his superior.'

lines.x: ...And that is what I witnessed in the quarantine zone, Councilor. All of it.
If we just stand by and watch Pavlovich continue to do as he pleases, especially if we let them keep using heavy weaponry, it won't be long before this turns into an irreversible catastrophe.
Baryshnya Rostova, based on what you have said, you seem to hope the legislature will publicize Pavlovich's crimes, strip him of authority, and perhaps even sack him.
My only wish is to stop him.
Please forgive my directness. I have no intention of casting aspersions on the State Council, nor can I exert any influence upon it, but I can imagine how much resistance such an act will face.
Perhaps we should agree to his demands and postpone the discarding of the quarantined plate, at which point he will release the students as promised.
Do you believe him a man of his word?
No. I have absolutely zero trust in him.
And I can see that the reason you are asking me such a question is because you cannot trust him either.
Haha, very clever, very clever. Perhaps you and my daughter would get along.
My subordinates also tell me you have not done as he asked since you left the quarantine zone. His request to pressure us parents into retaining Katorga, that is.
Instead, you looked through the list of parents, and after considering our stations, situations, and temperaments, you chose me.
You believe me to be the most politically influential figure you can contact at the moment, one able to grease the right wheels.
Your assessment is correct. I figured you would see through such under-baked schemes with a glance.
However, it is only because I cannot stop thinking about my friends. They are enduring great torment within Katorga even as we speak. The danger to their lives grows every second that passes.
I know you have your concerns about my unrealistic ideas.

Which is why I dare not expect Pavlovich to face immediate punishment. But at the very least, we should strive for better treatment of the students, as well as for the removal of heavy weaponry from the area.
...I regret to say that the sitting council is most likely unable to grant your requests.
Mr. Pavlovich mentioned to me that he has the support of many noble friends on the State Council.
I believe you've left out the word 'old'. Or perhaps the military nobility.
To be quite frank with you, the rifts between Ursine noble factions can hardly be called a secret, even to the Bolívarians. You do not need to tiptoe around the subject.
Due to the recent unrest, every resolution, every regulation, who has a sharp tongue in the legislature today, who is praised by the tsar tomorrow... Everything leads to divisions by rank.
If we look at only the State Council, it boasts four hundred or so councilors, most of them from illustrious families, with outstanding achievements of their own.
The hereditary nobles living in the capital, whose family names are recorded in the Almanac of Nobility, number nearly eight hundred.
As for the reputable burghers of influence, they are innumerable. Everyone brings their own complicated stances to the table.
If things were as easy as splitting a blini in two... I do not think Ursus would find herself in this present position.
You mean to tell me...
That even some new nobles back Pavlovich. And the reason why we cannot stop him is that he has many powerful supporters.
This is why I cannot step over everyone's heads to offer you any material assistance on this matter. Not even the Chairman himself could.
To be fortunate enough to speak with you is already the greatest of assistance.
My objective will not change. If I want to actually save Sonya and all the others in the quarantine zone, I must impede Pavlovich's efforts to the fullest extent of my power.
An astute assessment, but an assessment is not enough.
When you are young, it is easy to know what you should oppose, but hard to know how to go about doing it.
What will you do, Baryshnya Rostova?
If I can find out why different people are supporting him, and get in touch with a few hidden 'friends'...

You reminded me that everyone brings their own complicated stances to the table. If you look at it from another point of view, even the old nobility, even the ones who once called him friend, can shift their stances under the right conditions.
Treating these words as a 'reminder' is rather...
Once this is all over, we must get together again. Once Elotta is done with her things, maybe...
I beg your pardon?
Nothing.
I have here a piece of information that has spread amongst a portion of the nobility, despite Chairman Witte's attempts to silence it.
His Imperial Majesty has not returned to the palace since the Winter Ball, for some reason.
The Chairman has been quietly dispatching investigators, but none have found any trace of him. After a process of elimination, there is only one place left he could be.
A place that is rather difficult to investigate, at the moment.
Difficult to investigate? Surely you don't mean—
His Imperial Majesty might be in the quarantine zone... somewhere even the Chairman cannot search?
Considering the current state of things, we hope to handle this as quietly as possible, lest greater chaos develop.
As for the nobles who somehow managed to hear of this news, they appear to hope this state of affairs continues. This fits with what you have told me.
...Some silent stance shifting for an exchange of benefits, or perhaps a wish to relieve the greatest source of pressure from above once and for all.
Not to mention how those who should have been deploying special measures to protect the tsar were slow to react, for some reason, at just the right time.
Which means the precise timeframe of this information is unclear, even though it would not be hard to investigate.
The important thing is, before these special measures take effect, you can continue resolving the problems your friends face, your way. But if they do take effect...
All your friends can do at that point is pray.
...What exactly are these spe—
All you need to know is that, once they are in effect, His Imperial Majesty will return to the palace safely.
However, I do know one more thing that might bring you comfort. Chairman Witte has already suppressed the resolution to abandon the quarantine zone. This should not change for at least a week.
Everything you have said is crucial information for us. On behalf of myself and my friends, we thank you wholeheartedly.
...In other words, a councilor divulged to Baryshnya Rostova that some of the new nobility hope His Imperial Majesty will be tortured in the quarantine zone, perhaps even murdered?
Though this hearing has approved the omission of names so as to protect the dignity of the nobility, rest assured that we will perform a thorough investigation once it is over.
No! Who is it?! Who was it who said such a deranged accusation?! I demand the witness tell us the names of these beasts IMMEDIATELY!
Drag them out of their lairs! Let us see if their gold-greedy hearts are still made of Ursine flesh!
I'm sorry, but I'm not Natalya. I have no idea who the persons mentioned in this letter might be.
But based on the following pages, she then called upon many time-honored noble mansions, but their masters were similarly unenthusiastic... You could say that they were unmoved by money.

Th-This is ridiculous! I don't care who they are, just say their names, otherwise—
Why are you stopping me?

He subconsciously swings his arm, the crisp slap breaking the rare dignity of the hearing once again. All present look his way out of curiosity, as his comrade who stopped him earlier covers the welt with his hand.
Said comrade can only force out a stiff smile in response to everyone's 'concern', but his eyes glare daggers at the impatient, rash noble, who angrily shuts his mouth.
Should I continue? Because someone gave Natalya a list of military nobles, and it's attached to the back of this letter.

The letter says that these nobles insist the tsar's disappearance is simply a rumor without even bothering to check, and that some of them wanted to use Natalya to extort the parents of the captured children...
Especially on the afternoon of December 29th, when one gentleman who wished not to be named blackmailed her—
Wait. You cannot divulge any details about these nobles.
I will conceal their names as asked, and will not pass judgment on their actions.
You cannot mention specific times or places either. Do not feign ignorance of the actual substance of my request. Tell us about this matter, and this matter only, am I clear?!
I understand, Your Honor.
After that, Natalya did manage to win the support of some parents, but most importantly, she visited the home of an important noble one day.
He is a long-time supporter of Pavlovich, and has advocated for using severe punishment to deal with law-breaking students. As long as—
...If you agree with our views, we can reduce the intensity of the fighting in the quarantine zone to a minimum.
Daughter of the House of Rostov... Please leave. If you had not described the situation as critical, I would never have anything to do with a noble of Chernobog.
This matter pertains to the tsar's safety, Your Grace. Nobody can bear the guilt of letting Ursus face a national crisis.

'National crisis'? You might not know this, girl, but there has been no shortage of madmen shouting these words on the streets of Deity Grypherburg these past few years—I am not referring to you, of course.

As for that piece of shocking news you just told me, forgive me, but I must feign ignorance. My mind is incessantly waving a red flag at me, telling me this is simply another piece of theater by those new money upstarts, orchestrated and starring themselves.
Perhaps I have misunderstood, but it seems as if you are accusing us of using His Imperial Majesty's safety as a prop piece, uncaring of the consequences if the tsar truly is in danger.
No, I simply refuse to be coerced by you, even if you are dressed as grandly as your average Grypherburg noble.
There is nothing more important these days than giving those youths with poisoned minds a proper education.
If, say, at Tsarskoye Selo—at Tsarevgrad, that rabble was not punished severely, what will become of the empire's reputation?
Your concern for your peers is understandable, and I will not pry too deeply into what guilt led you to defend that mob. Treat today's meeting as having never happened.
...I understand, Your Grace.
But believe me when I say that there will come a day that you, too, will defend that 'mob'.
Come again?
The reason why I was able to find you was because I heard from a few nobles that you and your heir have been secretly inciting the students to unrest this whole time.
Some have already obtained evidence, evidence that proves Your Grace's cellar is a base for student activities. They even managed to film them rehearsing in your garden.
Hah. A meaningless attempt. No matter how much you bluff and bluster, girl, I will not be fooled.
He slowly rises from his seat, no longer looking Natalya in the eye.
I did warn you, if you try and coerce me—
Listen to me! Everyone turn about! Retreat!
From what I understand, people guessed the relationship between your heir and the student organization very early on, which even led you to threaten her teachers into quashing these 'rumors'.
As it so happens, your heir has not made a public appearance since the students who protested at the Winter Ball were arrested.
Because she is busy studying in the Central Governorate—
You are free to continue believing your own lies. Perhaps I read too much into things and assumed you and I are in similar positions, able to save her from a doomed future...
Alas, poor Olga.
Wh-What have you done?!
Nothing. Maybe I chanced upon one of their rehearsals here, that's all.
Or perhaps I should say that even unexpected guests such as me can inadvertently stumble onto them in the act. This explains the level of activity within your home, does it not?
You—
The sunlight is dazzling as it streams in through the window. Rosa lowers her eyes, giving an imperceptible nod before returning to a polite smile befitting a noblewoman.
As I said, I simply heard a few rumors. It is Your Grace's good fortune that they have not spread.
What do you want?
It is not about what I want. It is Your Grace who must protect yourself, and the future of your house.
It is now just past noon. I hope you will permit me to rest here a while, as I await your answer—
No, it was nothing like that!
This is all a lie... Your Honor!
Duke Treplev?
I confess, the one Natalya Rostova found was me, and I agreed to reduce arms shipments to Pavlovich.
But my daughter is innocent! She was coerced by th-those lunatics in the student organizations!
She will testify today, to bravely prove her own innocence, and expose Natalya's lies. She is the next witness.
Natalya's letter here is a confession of the dishonesty shown to Your Grace and to others.
Ursus has never afforded us opportunity, and yet, not once has Natalya betrayed anyone. She has simply made the right choices, to protect the friends she should protect.
No matter who may step up and lie at the witness stand, she is worthy of Ursus, worthy of us.
You—
Order!
We shall adjourn for a ten-minute recess.
Have the next witness make ready, parliamentarian.
Countess Vorontsova... I don't understand. This is very much not your style.
You clearly have Natalya's true testimony. If you had presented it against Zoya's, the nobles here would not have embarrassed themselves like this, at the very least.
You never spoke up once she started narrating her experience in the quarantine zone. Many of our superiors are watching you, and they are angry.
What are you waiting for?
As you wish.
Good, good. This way, I will have time to explain things to your mother and father. There is still time enough for everything.
Oh, such beautiful penmanship, Natashenka. Let me see if you have overlooked anything—
Natashenka, you...
What is this you've written? Isn't this supposed to be a confession?
It is.
I confess to all those I once cheated and deceived, and to all the suffering students who were, in turn, exploited and abandoned by them.
They were once my fellow students, even though we did not attend the same school.
We are all Ursine. We were supposed to all share the same fate.
No, no!
Oh, my child! Who made you bear such suffering? Who branded you a cheat? This was not what I wanted you to do, certainly not!
O, bozhe moi, Marsha, what... what must I do to comfort your poor daughter? No more talk of such fearful words, Natashenka! This is not your fault!
But there is always someone who must pay the price, or bear the guilt, Countess.
I have written of these people's participation, describing it as you asked me to, as well as... what stories I know. But you said this is not what I should do.
Have I laid my heart bare incorrectly? Or should I forever keep my distance from responsibility, like a child who never grows up?
You shall always be a child to us! I merely wanted to help you, like I would help any friend's family... or my own daughter.
But who needs to write such a dour confession for these ridiculous, forgivable mistakes? I do not wish to see you torment yourself so, my... Natashenka...
I understand, Countess. I really do.
Your passion and sincerity burn so bright that it often pains me when we are together. But this is not your fault.
It's just that, after meeting with far too many of noble bearing who were once out of reach, after understanding how they think and how they feel about this country, I can't help but wonder—
Before the Hippogryph Kingdom had been toppled, when the ancestors of today's Ursine nobility were still common folk, when even Igor Velikiy was just another soldier in the army.
As the Hippogryphs cracked their whips, they fearlessly threw themselves forward to shield the enslaved. This made everyone believe what flowed in their veins was the blood of honor and courage.
But if there comes a day the inheritors of such brave blood choose to trample over the oppressed and humiliated, even pick up the whips of the Hippogryphs themselves...
Will there still be people who believe in them, who want to keep their company?
And will I actually take part, and become one of them?
This is... our inherent rights—
Don't, Natashenka...
No, Countess. Please allow me to refuse, just this once.
If you were to ask me which right I wish everyone would be born with, it would certainly be...
'The right to choose'.
And right now, it is just like you said... 'There is still time enough for everything'.
Time enough for me to make my choice, time enough for me to decide what to bear.
There is no need.
'Even the most well-crafted of lies cannot withstand the truth you have lived'. Natashenka... has made her choice, nothing more.
But she deceived you. At least make her pay the price—
I thank your lordship for your enthusiasm. It is just that...
I am somewhat tired.
...Anna! The street lamps ahead are out! Chyort... why is this happening?
Don't worry about that for now.
Take this torch, Leto, and call out to the students who have fallen behind. Have them follow the light towards me, slowly, and watch out for anyone who might've collapsed.
Gotcha.
What are you doing here... get up! We need to go!
Olga!
A-Anna... where are we?
Out of Tsarevgrad, on the streets. The rest of them are behind us.
Enough talk, are you hurt? Can you stand?
M-My left foot!
...I need a hand! Anyone?
Istina tries to swallow, but she feels only piercing pain in her parched throat. She does not know how long she has walked in the cold wind.
For the first time, Grypherburg's dark night seems so unfamiliar. Aside from a few lights on isolated castles and towers, everything else is swallowed by darkness, from street lamps to houses...
But now is not the time to ponder the reason. She raises the torch and looks left and right with ragged breath, attempting to recognize familiar faces in this abnormal darkness.
Over here, Sergo.
I... I, she—
Grab Olga's arm for me. We'll talk after we get out of here.
Then... where are we going?
The theater.
...Therefore, I didn't go home that night, but instead went to an abandoned theater with the rest of the students.
Baryshnya Olga Trepleva, as the three previous witnesses all strayed from the subject one way or another—
I need your statement to be strictly based on facts, so that we might avoid wasting our time.
During the committee's preliminary investigation, you clearly stated that you chose to part ways with them as their actions went beyond the pale.
However, Anna Morozova and the students kidnapped you, and used your disappearance to deceive Duke Treplev. Is that correct?
...Yes.
And so, I witnessed Anna Morozova's group planning, and how they participated in Sonya Mikhailivna's violent actions.
Finally, a sensible witness. I knew we could count on the House of Treplev.
Very good.
Please continue. The committee needs to hear more truthful details—how did Anna Morozova help Sonya Mikhailivna sabotage the order of the quarantine zone?
Olga nods nervously, rubbing her palms on the edge of the witness stand. She hears a familiar cough—her father is, apparently, even more nervous.
Those of us in the theater were terribly frightened. We had lost our reason, and everyone was either crying, or accusing one another...
...Damn, what happened to the communications gear? I'm not getting anything.
Quit fiddling with that trash, Vanguards. What do you have to say for yourself, instigator of 'great action'?
Nonsense! We were going to—
Raid the prison? See what they did to us, even though we were unarmed. We would all be dead, if we believed your crap!
You were the ones who were calling for violence first! Don't try to hide!
