The problem isn't with this action. It's with your lack of faith in the nation, blindly expanding conflict and slandering His Imperial Majesty in Tsarevgrad.
We were going there to petition. His Imperial Majesty would have appointed an inspector if word reached him.
Now, there's no way back...
This has nothing to do with us! It's the Vanguards who forced it through! Faddey must be held responsible!
I didn't see you vote against it.
Everyone knows I've always been a supporter of Sonya and the Self-Government Group. It was because you people were threatening to expel and punish anyone who didn't cooperate—
You didn't say anything at the meeting, didn't say anything today at the scene, and now you want to act superior after things went wrong?
You're one to talk, Vanguard! I was looking for an excuse to teach you a lesson!
Stop. Now is not the time to argue.
We need to figure out how many were arrested, then discuss how to rescue them. At the very least, we need to learn what happened to them.
What are our options? These Vanguards got Leonid arrested. None of this would have happened if we'd listened to him!
So you want to keep yelling? We have to do something!
We must go home, apologize to our parents and teachers, and hope that we're not expelled...
No, I'm gonna help them! We need to help Sonya!
Quit dreaming, Lada.
I know, Sonya saved you, but how are we supposed to save Sonya when not even she could get herself out of there?
She didn't just help me, she helped everyone! People like her were standing in front of us, and now they're hurting for our sakes!
I... we can't give up.
That's right. How do we know it wouldn't work? We'll find a way, we'll keep fighting!
Fight? Easy for you to say. What are you going to fight with? Those books Anna carries with her, and your spirit?
Yeah, what about my spirit? I'll bring Sonya and the others back, as long as I can still move my arms and legs!
You don't have the guts, you can shut up and watch from the sidelines, but stuff your jokes up your ass!
Those that want to go can go. It's none of my business.
Sonya was reckless, just like you, which is why she got herself arrested. She's probably locked up somewhere, regretting that she ever tried to—
Leto grabs the big-mouthed student by the collar and almost lifts him into the air with one hand. Even Istina and Gummy have rarely seen her so angry.
Calm down, Rosalind. We don't need a fight.
Maybe YOU can tolerate these cowards, Anna, but I've had enough. Even the air here makes me want to puke.
I'm gonna find General Zima. Come find me when you and Lada have had enough of this trash, and the SSG will go together!
...Then Rosalind left, and neither Anna nor Lada could catch her. They called out to her from the door, but she never turned back.
This corroborates Ukusik's testimony that Rosalind entered the quarantine zone of her own accord, and not as part of the Student Assembly's plan.
Yes. She and Sonya Mikhailivna were both members of the Ursus Student Self-Government Group, a testament to their internal unity. This has nothing to do with the Student Assembly.
It seems we are now able to further narrow the responsibility for the Katorga Incident. Let us go to how you were kidnapped.
...Many people were asking me what the students should do.
...You were the one who led us, led the Assembly to protest.
I, I don't know.
You said your father would smooth things over, just like the Petrachevsky Group at first.
What do we do, Olga...?
I... I'll go and ask him. I'll try my best to find out about the other students.
We'll be alright, won't we? We'll go to bed, and things will get better when we wake up in the morning, won't they?
If you're going to ask your father, should we all go back to our homes right now?
It's been a long and hard day for everyone. Better to dismiss everyone early.
You're right... let's call it a day? Let's all go home and get some rest, and we'll figure things out tomorrow.
Go home? The words are like a pardon, or an ironic spell.
The students look at each other, frozen hesitation turning to relief. The tightly wound crowd begins to loosen and disperse, and the theater becomes filled with scattered footsteps.
Olga stands lonely on stage, watching the silhouettes that cannot wait to get away.
Someone quips, 'If there's a tomorrow.' She bites her pale-white lower lip.
Where are you going?
Didn't you hear Olga's instructions, Anna? We're going home.
The Assembly hasn't determined a plan to find and help the captive students. Many in the theater are still too weak to move.
We should not disperse before these issues are resolved.
Someone takes a step forward. Gummy spreads her arms wide to stop them.
Lada?
Please stop! We have something to say!
A lot of you said the Self-Government Group was right when we were talking. Why not hear us out?
But it wasn't just you; most of us were opposed to violence. Olga only proposed the compromise because Faddey's group was insistent.
This is not our responsibility. Let Olga take care of it. I'm not going to have all of us pick up the bill for the Vanguards' recklessness!
Let's not waste any more time here. We're all—
Enough!
Gummy. A honey drop, please.
Huh? Istina...
Istina pushes past the student in her way. Normally gentle and rational, she walks straight through the crowd, glaring at everyone left and right as she heads towards the center of the theater.
You, every single one of you, voted to do this, chose to wave the banners, and chose to shout those slogans. No one made you do anything.

You argued over whose slogan was the most powerful, who cared the most for Rania, who could come up with the most creative insults about the aristocracy, and who was the most fit to guide the future direction of the student movement.

And the result? You caused a commotion, threw your friends under the bus, and ran away satisfied with a good night's work, hoping for mercy from the nobles you just insulted, so that you can pretend nothing happened?
Is this 'great work' that you advocate nothing more than a farce?
You misunderstand, Anna. The Symposium is very serious about this. This is why we study the theories—
So the result of your studies is to convince yourself that you're doing great things when things go smoothly, and pretend none of it has anything to do with it when things don't go smoothly?
You shout about 'new Ursines', yet you run off and hide when the smallest thing happens. Why would any Ursine with the slightest bit of spirit want to associate themselves with you?
Anna's right. You people are always undermining things when unity is needed. You're a bunch of cowardly—
And you, Vanguards! How do you manage to sound like you just downed a whole cask of mead whenever you open your mouth to speak?
Get your hands on a few old weapons, draw a few lines and put a few wargame pieces on some old maps of Bresk, and suddenly you think you're ready to fight the gendarmes?

You spend less than a minute deciding, and get thrown into jail in less than an hour. The assembly meetings would have more substance if we replaced your vandalized civilian maps with cheap detective novels!
But we all want to go home—
I haven't gotten to you yet! 'We were going there to petition'! How did you manage to say that with a straight face?

The more students like us shout our slogans, the more we become 'seditious elements' that the nobles look to hand over to the tsar in chains. Why would they want to sit down at a table and talk to us?
Now you sneer and scoff and talk about surrender, after your fellow students have been arrested. Do you dare say those same words to their faces?
And you!
Huh? I didn't say anything, Anna, I've always been on the side of the SSG—
...Check the theater for functioning lights.
Spotlights shine through the dust. The crowd narrow their eyes at the light, as they watch in awe the tiny figure walk towards the edge of the light.
For the first time, their gazes are no longer weak and scattered; they are focused tightly on Istina.
...Olga?
Go, if you can help them. I-I'm—
Fellow students, all you who know where your consciences lie—
We are back. We have returned, tired and lost, to this tiny theater that is safe for now, where we found light and warmth.
But our friends, the ones whom we see every day, the finest amongst us, continue to endure cold and darkness out there.
Some say that we have failed, that it is all over. To them I ask: What is failure?
Should we pack up, pretend nothing ever happened, let others pay the price for us, and continue to live without hope? Is this your idea of victory?

True failure is not being struck down. It is choosing to extinguish the flame in your heart, lowering your head in fear that you aren't kneeling submissively enough, even when you still have a choice, a choice to fight against injustice.
True failure is not being locked away behind bars, but being stripped of even the courage to imagine a land that is more just, more free.

Look at your hands. Remember how they made your hearts tremble when you voted with them. You know that you were not born with them to applaud and offer gifts to the rich and powerful, but to topple the high walls!
Anna... we understand what you're saying. But they were taken away, and we don't even know where they are. We—
Just shouting slogans won't do anything, Anna. Do you have a way to find them?
They took my roommate too! I have no clue if he is even alive anymore...
...Yeah, we do not know exactly where they are, but we know who took them.
Please answer a question first—what is your deepest desire? Answer me, not for my sake, but for your own.
A brief silence. Some look down at their hands, while others exchange glances.
Sonya taught me that if you are being pushed around, you have to fight back. I am going to... I am going to fight to the end!
At the very least, we need to know what happened to them! We need them to know that we haven't given up!
I've had enough of hiding in the back! Every time I look down, I feel like I've failed them... that I've failed myself.
Yes! We must fight, until we free everyone!
Then we have the answer—we fight! Only by fighting can we break our shackles. Surrender, and we will forever lose the strength to ever break free again.
Tell Ursus that we are fighting for our fellow students, our friends, our families! We are fighting for ourselves!
Tell us! What is to be done?
First, everyone needs to stay here and do a head count, so that we know who's missing.
If anyone is injured, inform Lada so she can provide medical treatment. Anyone who has medical experience is invited to volunteer as well.
Next, everyone needs to understand that we are facing a daunting mission. I hope everyone can be aware of their own responsibilities.
Understood? Then—
Let's move!
Anna... I've signed in.
I understand. You are free to leave.
I couldn't be like you. I joined the group for credits. Maybe I believed in it at one point—but you got to understand, I'm looking for a peaceful life.
You don't need to justify your choice. I hope you get back to school, and get to enjoy the life you want.
If you care about any of the missing persons, please pray for their safety, and for our success.
...I want to apologize to you and Lada. It was not my place to judge Sonya or the Self-Government Group.
If I ever get a chance... no, when you see Rosalind, please tell her I'm sorry.
Anna... do you have a moment?
Olga, you should get Lada to look at your injuries, or do you want to—
No... I just want to ask, what is your plan?
Honestly, I'm not totally sure it's going to work.
The resources available to the students are mostly associated with school or family, varying considerably from one individual to another.
This also means, however, that they have access to information from all strata of society.
You want to... leverage our families?
Anna, if you're trying to steal information from the nobility, you need to think about the consequences.
...I won't come to any conclusions until sign-ins are done.
But I know that an inexorable tide has crashed over Ursus.
We could go home, avoid making a choice, and avoid the potential responsibility and scorn that comes with it.
But there is something else that we can do—take each other's hands in this tide.
I will give everything to protect those close to me.
This path can be yours too, if you wish it... Chairman Trepleva.
Baryshnya Trepleva, it is quite clear to all present that Anna Morozova usurped your authority that night.
I am curious, however, as to why you did not choose to leave the Assembly, like other students did.
That's because—
Your Honor, I believe the hearing should focus on specific events.
...The atmosphere at the time had compromised my reason.
In that case, you must explain why you split from Anna's group, and how they kidnapped and coerced you.
...Yes, Your Honor.
Virtually everyone stayed at the theater that night, helping those who were injured, and thinking of ways to find out about those who were arrested.
But the situation changed the following day—
...Alright, Olga, I applied what medicine I could find.
It may not look good, but bear with me, it'll help you heal.
You're on duty today? Where's Lada?
You went to bed early last night. Natalya showed up later, along with a Vulpo I didn't know. They took Lada away after talking to Anna's group for a while.
Where's everyone else? The theater's all empty.
I'm not sure, but I think Anna assigned missions.
...Our priority is to figure out where the students are being held captive.
Start with this list and talk to their parents, it may help us find a way.
I'll talk to my family contacts. Let me know if you have a lead; I'll verify it.
Take care, Anna.
Hm? What are you two doing here?
Olga was sleeping by the stage last night. I saw her wake up when I came to the theater in the morning, so I reapplied her medicine.
...Very good.
Sergo, help me move Olga to the rehearsal studio on the third floor. She needs rest.
Perhaps I should go home, Anna.
I'm good enough to walk now. I can't promise my father can help get people off, but at least I can ask where they're being held.
Don't worry, I already have a lead on where they're held.
As for you, you should stay put and focus on recuperating. People will talk if you go home like this.
There are other injured students staying behind to receive treatment. I'm having someone deliver their letters to their families.
I'll get the stretcher, Olga.
They moved me into a room, claiming to be protecting me.
But I soon realized that their 'protection' involved students standing at my door around the clock in shifts with fireman's axes in hand.
When I tried to talk to them, I was told that they were under orders not to interact with me... so I gave up on writing to my father, because there was no way they would help me send it.
So you realized you were being held captive by Anna Morozova?
Yes.
Do you know her motivation to do such a thing?
My guess is that I expressed reluctance when she hinted at exploiting the nobility the previous night.
Do you think it explains the Ursus Student Self-Government Group's hostility towards the aristocracy? It would be consistent with Sonya Mykhailivna colluding with the Unbound.
...Yes.
I wasn't the only one she imprisoned. Anyone who wasn't sufficiently firm in resolve, whom she deemed an information risk as well as... nobles who had value to her, were all treated the same way.
Did you have any opportunity to communicate with the outside or leave the room?
Very little, except for Sergo, who quietly told me what the students were doing when he was on duty, even telling me—
...Are you sure about this?
Absolutely! My mother has been running a garment factory in Grypherburg for more than a decade. You can trust us on this.

But she said that approximately nine hundred winter army uniforms were being transported to the quarantine zone, while Natalya's observations yesterday indicates that there are no more than five hundred combatants there.
If both of you are right, then there can only be one explanation—someone is sending reinforcements into the quarantine zone.
Sonya just said they couldn't deal with heavy weapons, and now reinforcements are being sent? What do we do, Anna?
Will your mother be at the factory these couple of days?
Yes, why?
I will speak to my police contacts, get a few uniforms, put some tall boys in them, and go to your mother's factory disguised as the gendarmes auditing the books.

Tell your mother that you don't have class for a few days, so you're helping out at the factory. Put in a word for us if your mother gets suspicious, tell her letting the cops see the books won't do any harm.
Uh...
No hesitation. Our friends are in graver danger with every passing second. Trust my judgment, if you want to save them.
The source of this order is the breakthrough that we've been waiting for.
But impersonating the cops... that's way too hard.
We haven't been in contact with our comms girl Botani since the ball, but the equipment that she left behind still works.
Bring the equipment and follow my orders. My friend who has police connections will be there to help...
Sergo, are you there?
You're the tallest, you'll be the first to try the uniforms.
Me? But I get all red in the face whenever I go onstage in drama club. No way I could—
...Play a cop.
Wow, my whole face is covered up...
Stop talking to yourself, Sergo. Watch the office door and don't let anyone come in.
Gotcha, Anna.
Do not respond verbally.
He nods reflexively, his throat moving up and down underneath his mask. He has had to swallow three times in the span of a single minute.
Anna's friend still has her head buried in the pile of documents on the office desk. Everything is going smoother than he expected, except for the part where he actually finds the answer.
Why is it taking so long—
What do you mean, taking so long...?
Wait, who are you? I thought we were supposed to be checking the books today—Unit 2.
Sergo turns around to find an authentic, non-impostor Ursine policeman staring at him perplexedly, or so he infers through the policeman's goggles.
He covers his mouth by reflex, although his counterpart would never have detected his anxiety if he did not do so.
What's your district and unit? Did the new superintendent mix up the orders again?
Uh, uh, uh—
Are you not feeling well? There's no fireplace or heating here. Why are you sweating like that...?
Slap him, Sergo.
...Huh?
Do it. My friend's coming your way.
Slap him, then yell at the top of your lungs, 'Do not delay the daughter of Lord Yaroslav!'
...Do not delay the daughter of Lord Yaroslav!
He slaps the man with all his strength, and has to stop himself from crying out at the pain of his stinging palm.
The man stands where he is, reaching up to touch where he was slapped.
I apologize. The superintendent made a last-minute change, and the news apparently didn't reach you.
This man is my bodyguard, whom my family arranged to go into the service with me, for father was uneasy about me being alone.
...So it's like that again?
Yes, like that.
Command knew this factory's books were off, so they left it to some noble kid to reap the fruits.
I've been in the force for three years, and it's the same every year. Every time there's a new superintendent, a bunch of people come in you don't dare to touch.
This is Grypherburg, after all.
Wait!
...Give your father my regards. I'd appreciate it even more if you gave him my name and number.
The cop just walked away without saying another thing! I should've slapped him harder.
That's incredible, Sergo.
But you were telling me that the books revealed that it was the House of Treplev that was supporting the magistrate behind the scenes, and planning to send reinforcements?
Yes. Anna and Natalya talked for a long time last night about your family and friends, especially your father.
How do they know my associates?
Anna arranged for a few students to return home and go back to school like nothing happened.

You know the Assembly has students from practically every school. We talked to friends and teachers of those who were arrested. There are many people who care about them, and so we got a lot of information.
Someone said she's already located the Treplev estate and is planning to lay an ambush for the duke. All hearsay and rumors amongst the students, of course—
Olga... I know this isn't fair to you.
I see no option other than to accept.
I'm trapped here with no way to stop whatever they're trying to do. I can only hope for the best.
Mm...
I'm glad you see things that way. I'll let you get your rest.
Say, you said you were going to sew a flag for the Assembly and wanted me to collect various kinds of fabric. Have you finished it?
I'm sure Anna would want to come and talk to you, if I showed her the flag you made.
I'll tell you when I'm done.
Sure! Good night, Olga.
Olga exhales as the door closes silently.

She takes out a long rope tied together from fabric of many different colors, and ties one end to the heavy bed frame made of solid wood. She tugs on it a few times, making sure that it can bear her weight.
Then she goes over to the window and throws the other end out. The rope is immediately swallowed up by the night, as though it has fallen into a bottomless abyss.
I'm sorry, Sergo. I hope Anna won't be too hard on you.
...I won't be making your flag.

lines.st: I didn't dare to go home after escaping the theater. I didn't dare to face my father, though he was sure to forgive everything, and I was afraid of the rumored ambush.
I went back to school, looking for someone I could rely on. Professor Valeriya took me in—out of respect for the House of Treplev.
I spent the longest winter night in the professor's dormitory.

lines.x: ...You must be mistaken.
I understand your wish to protect your students, Professor Valeriya.
However, Olga is not the only student at this school. We need her to help the students who are being held captive.
Please—
The faint silhouette outside the winter suddenly turns its head. Its gaze seems to pierce the thick frosted glass, immediately driving the sleepiness from Olga's head.

She leaps from the bed, not even having the time to put on her shoes, and runs through the back door up the stairs. In her terror, she dares not turn around, even as the footsteps and shouting behind her grow louder.
*Pant*—*Pant*—
S-Stay away!
I should have known. Sergo is gentle-hearted, but prone to naivete. He was always likely to make a mistake.
There is still time to rectify the mistake, however.
How did you find me? Do you even have spies in our school?
These past few days, I combed every school in Grypherburg for potential allies, following the list of missing students.
You sought sanctuary at your school as soon as you escaped the theater... you're exactly who I think you are.
Where else could I go? Sergo told me you have assassins hiding around my home.
Is it true that you're trying to kill my father?
I have neither the intention nor the ability to deal with the Ursine aristocracy that way. We have always operated by negotiation.
I believed you when you promised to rescue the students that night, because I felt guilty about what happened to them.
But what did you do to me? Tricked me and locked me up in a room! Did you think I'd still trust you?
I don't know where you heard these rumors—
Stay away from me!
Olga stumbles back a few steps, leaning against the windowsill at the end of the stairway, her hands pressed against the window frame.
I've had enough, Anna!
I-I don't want my father to be purged because of me, but I can't just watch my fellow students die either.
I just want all this to end! If you'll only be satisfied by making me—
Calm down! Think this through. If anything happens to you, it would be a catastrophe for both your father and the students!
The duke would lose his daughter and heir. He would stop at nothing for revenge, to crush us, and everyone in the quarantine zone.
No, no, I just—
I don't know what to do!
Oh—
The cold wind tears at Olga's shawl, threatening to devour her. Suddenly, her arms lose their strength, and she loses her balance, falling backwards out of the window.
Olga—
...I was lucky to fall right into the middle of the pile. I escaped from Morozova with only minor injuries.
I hid in the city for a day, until my father's men found me and took me home.
That is the extent of my account.
The chamber is once again filled with chatter, though a single sigh stands out, as though a tremendous weight has been lifted off one pair of shoulders.
Baryshnya Trepleva, from your point of view, how did the students enter the Treplev estate?
I don't know how they did it, but given that Anna already knew where it was, they would have had their pick of options.
Well... I'm sure the entire committee has arrived at an answer.
Still, I must follow protocol and confirm this—
Baryshnya Trepleva, do you accuse Anna Morozova, leader of the Student Assembly, of colluding with Sonya Mykhailivna, and committing various crimes, including treason?
I accuse the leader of the Student Assembly...
Olga Danilovna Trepleva, of responsibility for all acts involving the students in the Katorga Incident.
Wait—
Anna Morozova should be penalized for blackmailing the nobility, but she only did what she did out of urgent necessity—
Do you know what you are saying, Baryshnya Trepleva?
I am stating the truth, Your Honor.
Ever since Zoya took the stand, everyone in the room knew the source of the storm, yet no one was willing to say her name.
Who was the leader and organizer of the Student Assembly, who pushed it down this path, who is responsible for this broken order...
I declare that I shall willingly don the shackles I deserve—
Recess! Recess!
Stop writing, parliamentarian! Escort Baryshnya Trepleva out for fresh air, now!
The testimony once again sets the hearing on fire. The roaring of the duke and the animated discussions quickly drown out the feeble hammering of the gavel.
Olga lowers her gaze as she is escorted out by the parliamentarian, past Absinthe on the witness stand.
Absinthe nods slightly.
Hah—hah——
Get, up, here!
...What?
I'm not letting go! Stay put!
Istina is leaning out the window, both hands locked around Olga's arms, hanging on with all her might.
The others rush forward to pull Istina and Olga back into the hallway in a chorus of heave-hos and panting.
Hah—
You can't die here, Olga. Didn't you hear what I said?
But, I could never be, as ruthless as you are—
Ruthless?
Tell me, were you really planning to jump when you were sitting on that windowsill?
Your problem was never that you couldn't be ruthless. You were simply running away.
When you decided to hold the protest, and now... you were fearless in opposing everything, simply because you knew—
No matter what you did, all you needed to do was to turn around, and you would find yourself in your father's embrace.
You never knew what it felt like to struggle to survive, you never even imagined it. You simply dreamed one day after another, in the cradle that your family has woven for you...
Do you think all the other people in the land of Ursus get to dream the same dream?
Let me tell you this, Olga.
You have never truly seen your country, seen Ursus for what it is. Innocence is a sin in this land, and indecision its greatest accomplice, but you have continued to avoid choosing your path.
I—
If you wanted to continue to dream, you should have gone back to your father a long time ago, and sat by the warm fireside watching the executioner's axe fall on our futures.
If you want to rescue the students, you need to put all your chips on the table, even your own family.
I have already made my choice... stand up, Olga.
I'm taking you back, whether you like it or not. I will show you how we get the others out of the quarantine zone.
We have to go, Anna. We've already caused quite the commotion on campus. The students helping us can only delay them for so long.
...Let's go back to the theater.
Students can't remain students forever, Olga. Everyone has something that they must do... and what I must do now is make you disappear for a while.
You will be freed once the situation has been resolved.
...One moment, Anna.
You know where the Treplev estate is...
Yes, but I have no intention of killing your father. I only want to convince him.
To save the students?
Yes.
...I have an idea.
There is a secret passage that leads to the manor's wine cellar, accessible through the warehouse of a vineyard on the western outskirts of Grypherburg.

It is my father's escape route in the event of an assassination attempt... not even the guards know about it. You can enter the manor through there, and he will know at once that it was I who told you about it.
Olga...
You understand that this will ruin your relationship with your family beyond repair.
No, Anna.
I will defend my honor and that of my house, in my own way.
...What are you doing, Mykola?
Someone was falling behind—
So you decided to break formation on the left flank? Do it over!
Good. Advance with your spears and force me into a corner.
You're too strong, Sonya. We can't budge you.
It's not that I'm too strong, it's that you are not pushing together.
You have to remember, we're not guerillas. The empire will not protect us, so we must form a fortress together.
Do you understand?
Yes, ma'am!
Hey, General! Still training?
You just got back?
What's the sitch?
Good news, the cannons and heavy weapons they were showing off yesterday are gone.
Nika saw the thugs moving a bunch of stuff out. Looked like weapons.
Natalya got it done, Sonya.
...I knew we could count on them.
Also, like we were talking about, Gromov sleeps in a camp inside the quarantine zone each night. Only Pavlovich lives on top of the walls.
We can smash the thugs' main force before we assault the wall.
We need more food and other supplies. Did you see their warehouse?
No... How much longer can we stretch these rations?
Three days, max. The Unbound are running short also. We owe Antosha too much already.
I got a bad history with food supplies... I can't—
Hold my hand! It'll be okay, General. We'll get through this.
We need to keep training. I got a feeling the next few days are gonna decide our fate.
Just how many are willing to fight...?
Surprisingly many. They've seen our training these last few days pay off. And the rest are willing to do first aid and logistics.
There's nothing young people hate more than injustice, is there?
You've done a good job, that's all.
What about that Fedya? He's not a student. Is he willing to join?
Hm... I'm still not sure if we can trust him.
We really don't know anything about him. But he is determined.
Fedya! I found a can of meat. Want some?
...No, thank you.
Don't push it. You haven't known him that long, you don't know he likes to be alone.
Come on, it's been a few days, we're not exactly strangers anymore.
Say, Fedya, you don't look like a student, but you don't look like a worker either.
How did you ever end up in this hellhole?
...I'm sorry, but I can't divulge that, under any circumstances.
Whuh?
Just who the hell...?

lines.loc: December 24th, 110130 minutes before the Winter Ball

lines.x: Time is short, Your Imperial Majesty. I beg you to consider it one last time.
Consider, yes—I'm considering feeding all these obese geriatrics to flesh buthidas.
That way, we'd get a windfall for the treasury by confiscating their assets, and a bunch of well-fed, succulent flesh buthidas.
Your Majesty... I completely understand your fury.
But you must understand that these old nobles are more willing to stand with you than the industrial nobles, who put clear price tags on their loyalty.
You need as many voices on your side as you can at a time like this, when you need to impress the Armies that continue to encroach upon the far shores of Lake Neva.
And that's their leverage to bargain with me?
Even my palace can barely afford heating this winter, and they want me to give them Originium to supply that unproductive Katorga Raion?
Is it those morsels of profit that they're after? No! They simply seek to emphasize their presence to me and make me bow to them. They will not get their wish!
The Grand Duchess of Far North, the Armies, and these old nobles...
When did we allow these leeches to our empire? They suck the blood of Ursus, and all it takes is the slightest opportunity for them to proclaim our weakness and claim Grypherburg for themselves!
Tell me, Witte... tell me that we can still demand their respect, that my assent to their ridiculous demands will not be seen as weakness.
Tell me you can make those old aristocrats go to war, risk life and limb in battle, and chase the Fourth Army back to where they belong—otherwise, do NOT trouble me with this matter again!
Your Imperial Majesty...
You know, Witte, sometimes, I can't help but think that there is too much rot growing on Ursus, like that Katorga they're so obsessed with protecting, and those people themselves.
Your Majesty is certainly correct. The Empire of Ursus is sick. But any doctor can tell you that one must be careful about what medicine to give the very ill.
Our Originium reserves are on the brink. You must do everything in your power to stop the forces of sedition from growing within Ursus, until we can come up with a material solution.
Otherwise, our internal conflicts will destroy us before any external foe or force of nature.
Fantastic. Great Ursus is as fragile as a Gaulish omelette, falling apart at the slightest touch.
You need not do much.
Simply placate them as usual, tell them that Ursus needs their loyalty, and that you intend to protect their interests.
I will handle the rest.
Do whatever you want, Witte.
I'm used to it. Those bemedaled skeletons and perfumed parasites stand in the way of everything I try to do... they don't care about Ursus, and they certainly don't care about me.
You can explain it to them when you attend tonight's ball.
Can't you and the Vice Chairman go for me? I'm tired.
It would be improper, Majesty.
You cannot refuse to attend the Winter Ball two years in a row. At a time like this, when people's hearts are unsettled, your subjects look to you to offer some degree of comfort—
Alright, alright, I'll go, just give me some time, please! That's enough talk. We've had too many vexations this winter already.
Leave me, Witte... please. And, I'm sorry.
Blyat! Blyat! Blyat...
Fyodor looks out the window. The streets of Grypherburg are nowhere near as bright as they were years past.
Such a cold winter... it could really use a fire.
What's this...? A power outage?
Death to the mudak tsar! Death to the mudak tsar! Death to the mudak tsar!
Bring out the bloodsucker Witte! Bring out the imbecile Fyodor!
You're looking for me? Here I am.
My, what a commotion.
Please! Stop! No more!
Shut up! How dare you insult His Imperial Majesty! Traitor!
He strikes the student's back with such force that his stick flies from his hand, falling by the wayside. Then it is fists and kicks that find their mark...
Enough, enough! He's not resisting. No need to beat him so hard.
Another traitor to the empire!
Traitor to the empire? Hah! Whose empire?
Insolent mudak! You need a beating too!
Such impudence!
How dare you hit me!
Indeed, I hit you. You may boast to your children that the tsar—
A heavy fist finds Fyodor's face before he can finish.
*Bzz*... target... escape... capture, complete! Over!
In the name of... *bzz*... His Imperial Majesty! Over!
The concealed communications device that Fyodor carries has fallen on the ground by the time he gets up. With no time to examine it, he quickly grabs it and puts it back in his ear.
...Blyat.
Mayday! Mayday! Anyone hear me?
All Student Assembly members, evacuate immediately! The lead vehicle is driving towards the outskirts!
If you can hear me, answer ASAP! Botani out!
Wait—
Several policemen grab and push him into the crowd that is being packed up into the cramped trucks.
The trucks drive to Katorga Raion, to the sound of frightened crying.
And so... we were all captured.
No explanations, no promises, no food, no tents.
We were tossed into Katorga like garbage.
Don't worry! I'll help you!
The diminutive student keeps Fyodor behind him, wildly swinging the tibia of some unidentified beast at the surrounding tuskbeasts.
Stay behind me! I've hunted in the Far North with my father! I can handle these beasts! Trust me!
Look out!
Phew... they're gone. That was close.
He drops to the ground in a pile of snow, panting.
Your arm. It's hurt.
Huh? Argh... you wouldn't happen to have alcohol and bandages on you, would you?
No. But I'll find you the finest doctors in Grypherburg once we are free of this place.
Don't worry about it. It's cold here, maybe it won't get infected.
What's your name?
...Fyodor.
Let me call you Fedya, since I've helped you. You can call me Shorty. That's what my friends call me.
You don't mind?
Minding doesn't change anything... If you're not hurt, I'll go on ahead.
Wait, you're going to the wall?
Yes, my friend told me that the one in charge here lets you go if you pay up.
I put together some money. Not sure if it's enough, but I figured I might as well take the chance.
Here, you can have this ration bar. If you need a place to start a fire, the students have a camp down on the south side.
Bye, Fedya—
...Wait.
Take these chervontsy. This should be enough to bribe the guards.
Emotions flash rapidly across Shorty's face. He bows solemnly to Fyodor and walks to the walls.
Please, hear me out—!
*Bzz*... this is Botani calling anyone who can hear me. Anyone?
Please, do you copy...?
The Council of Sixteen thugs are killing students! We need help!
Can anyone hear me? Come in, please?
Have we been abandoned? Are our cries and screams soundless?
It's a wall, not the great tundra! Why...?
(Sobs) Why doesn't anyone hear us...?
What should I...?
...Botani out.
(Rasping call) Attempt No. 373. Calling anyone who can hear me...
We are trapped in Grypherburg's Katorga Raion, unable to contact anyone on the outside...
Yesterday alone, five students died from blunt force trauma and hypothermia... there may have been more. We find ourselves on the brink of death, here in the glorious capital of Ursus.
The people who murdered my friends now sit in a room above me...
Attempt No. 374. Come in, come in...
...Maybe you'll never be like that voice from the Far North, Botani. You'll never change anything.
How could I make people hear my voice, so that all these lives can be saved?
(Sound of pained vomiting)
(Sobs)
Three hundred and seventy-four... you have shown more spirit than any bureaucrat in the palaces of Deity Grypherburg.
Maybe you don't realize it, but you are doing great deeds.
...Huh?
Y-You can hear me? Who is this...?
I... I'm Fedya. I'm from Sonya's camp.
Sonya's camp... I know of it, but I couldn't go, no, I didn't dare...
I sneaked into the last truck that came here... I wanted to tell the people of Grypherburg the truth of what I saw, the cruelty and brutality that's being inflicted upon the young people here.
But nobody answered, nobody heard me... this room I'm hiding in is right in the middle of the thugs' camp...
They came in today, and they stabbed the wardrobe that I'm hiding in with a freshly-honed knife... I think I can still hear its blade trembling...
I can't come out. They'll get me for sure.
(Sobs) I can't do anything—
In that case...
Why do you keep talking?
...Why?
There are thugs all around you. The wise would remain silent and cover their eyes and ears, the wise would ignore everything going on around them...
What is happening in Katorga had nothing to do with you... you could have remained silent. You live in danger and in pain. No one would blame you.
Yet you entered the quarantine zone and risked exposure to publicize the tragedies, even though no one is listening. You believe every call you make offers hope to the students.
I can... offer hope... the students need...
Unless you have a better explanation... I've really had quite enough, listening to a brave soul lament her cowardice. I come out here just once and I seem to keep running into this sort of thing.
How many hostiles on your end?
Two.
Good. Just the two of them won't catch you. Can you hear their movements from your location? Like what they're saying, what shape they're in?
...I can hear, if I listen carefully. They keep complaining about work and yawning. They seem tired.
Excellent. The tired are less alert. They are people too; they can grow weak or careless. Even you should be able to kill someone who is badly fatigued.
That's too—
Well, it's up to you whether you do it or not. But you can run, can't you?
Tonight, once they're asleep and you can hear them snoring, run, and don't look back.
If you don't know the way, I'll guide you. I walked all the way from the wall to the camp. I remember the buildings you'll pass.
If you try, you'll find that it's not so hard after all.
...Will I continue to hear your voice?
If it gives you the courage to move...
She recalls the day she decided what she wanted to do with her life.
The smell of dust and dirt, and overheated electronics... she curled up on a chair, searching for news of Bresk—of home, amidst the haphazard and scattered frequencies.
'Next, an excerpt from the opera—'
'Hiss—'
She fiddles with the knob. She needs to hear the sound of hope, a power that brings comfort, to keep the weightless panic in her chess, even for just a moment...
—What?
'Bzz, bzzt...'
'Comrades in the mines and cities.'
'We come from the Far North.'
...I'll try.
Can I ask who you are? You're not a student, are you?
...That is correct, but Sonya permits my presence.
I see... I've been providing communications support for the Student Assembly. Any student who hears my voice recognizes me and the code name 'Botani'.
Take a break, Pavalo. Even I'm tired after hauling all those crates today, you must be exhausted.
It-It's an honor to carry Master Gromov's burdens.
Come on, you got a barony from your dad, you could grovel a little bit less.
He's long gone, and our family is...
Can you tell Gromov, I just want to leave, you guys kidnapped me—
Shut it. Yeah, I kidnapped you, big deal. Boss needed someone who was good with numbers. It's not like you've been treated badly.
You want to get out, talk less and work harder.
What is it, Botani?
No, it's nothing.
It's just that when I get a chance to actually listen to them talk... they don't seem so scary anymore.
Hmph. I know exactly how many good-for-nothings there are in Ursus.
Hehe...
Thank you, Fedya.
Thank you for hearing my voice.
A cold draft keeps blowing in from the window that will not shut, causing the rickety house to hum quietly in the night.
Sitting in front of a dirty table, Pavalo flips through the ledger to the deafening snores of his colleague in the next room, his brow furrowed.
How come I haven't seen a shadow of any of the supplies that Gromov requested...?
No, the purchase price is much higher than the market price, and the Sixteen Warriors' nominal wages are far higher than what they actually are.
Hmph. A tale as old as Grypherburg itself.
He sneers. At almost the same moment, the roaring snore is interrupted, replaced by a wet, bubbling sound, as though someone is gargling.
Dreaming about meat again? Mudak sounds like he fell into a soup pot.
The gurgling ceases, replaced by the sound of liquid dripping on the floor.
...A leak?
He rubs his dry eyes and gets up to head over to the next room.
Pavalo opens the door. His pupils contract in shock, and he drops the ledger to the floor. Deep crimson liquid is seeping from his colleague's neck.
Ahh—
Hush... your life is in my hands, Baron.
Wh-Who are you?
Th-That's not important. What's important is that I need your help.
...Your voice is trembling, and your hand's trembling even worse. Are you nervous?
Put down the knife, devushka, and we can talk about this—
No...
I-If you shout, or try to stall for time, I'll have to kill you.
Like you said, my hand's trembling. I can't promise you it won't accidentally slip...
P-Please, I have a family back home. Spare me, and I'll do anything—
...Put on this headset.
What...?
I won't keep holding you up with a knife, but if you make one wrong move... this headset represents the latest research from the Third Bureau. It can blow your head off your shoulders at any time.
The Third Bureau?! N-No, how did I get on their bad side—
Quiet... someone will tell you where to go through the headset. You will lead me there, avoiding all Sixteen Warriors positions along the way. Do you understand?
Y-Yes...
Tell me where your camp is, I'll head there...
Ha, haha—
...What's so funny?
No, it's nothing. First, tell me the buildings you see around your position—
I'm getting my very own 'mission'... this is certainly unexpected, but not entirely unwelcome.
Let me think... how do those Third Bureau freaks talk?
Yeremey! You're still drinking? I had to turn the chemical factory upside down to find that single crate of beer!
Get lost—
Heh, let him drink, he's had plenty of scares these past few days.
Well *hic*... I pulled through *hic*... lousy beer *hic*... totally beneath me *hic*...
O noble lord, what has brought you down so low, that you must beg a humble 'peasant' like me for drink?
No, you're a decent fellow *hic*... the best *hic*...
I'm a 'peasant' too, Yeremey, compliment me!
Forget it—*hic*!
How did we get onto this topic? It's kind of embarrassing, really.
Listen, friends, I'll buy you a crate of beer for every cup I drink here.
Sonya, Mykola, Fedya, there'll be plenty for everyone!
You alright, Yeremey?
Judging from the way he's chugging one beer after another, I'd say he's perfectly alright.
How about you save the rest of the beer for us right now, because Fedya is sitting right behind you!
Not *hic* Not tonight... after tonight, whatever you want *hic*—
Why don't you sit with the others?
What about you, the conquering hero who captured the enemy?
Sonya and Antosha have been interrogating him all day. We should know more soon.
Let's hope it'll bring about the end of Gromov's tyranny...
You don't sound happy.
I've been thinking about what caused the radio blackout in the quarantine zone.
The Third Bureau has its ways.
But your equipment still caught my signal. How...?
You ask too many questions, 'Botani'... 'bookworm', indeed.
There aren't many earnest folk in Ursus these days... I can't believe I've become so nostalgic.
...I know you're hiding something from us, Fedya.
If you don't want to talk about it, I'll just pretend not to notice.
But I couldn't have brought Baron Pavalo back without you... you're the true hero on that front.
Maybe one day, you'll be a hero to even more people...
Fedya! Botani! Want a drink?
Yeremey sure is strong when he's drunk. He won't let me near the booze.
Well, he's finally out cold now, and I punched him a couple of times for good measure. He's not waking up for a while.
Huh?
Anyway, we've got enough for four cups. Want to sit down and chat a little? I'd love to make friends...
Sure, Pencil Stub. I think this is the first time you've seen my face?
Hah, you scared people when you showed up covered in blood, but we all relaxed when we heard your voice.
Anyway, I've got your cups. This one's for you, Fedya.
...Spasibo.
To tomorrow!
To victory!
To...
To souls happy and free.
...I cannot accept this compromise.
Unless you got a better idea. You can torture him if you want, but the only thing he cares about is his own hide.
I warned you, Pavalo is the prototypical Ursine noble.
Short-sighted, cowardly, ever dreaming of kindness and 'guidance' from above, acting harmless while pocketing all the gold and silver.
Give them a chance to catch their breath, and they will not hesitate to draw their swords against the people, and offer bloodshed to their liege lords as a gift.
Walking corpses whose expertise is self-preservation... can you not smell their stench?
We can keep arguing, or we can spend our time making more urgent plans. The intel I extracted from him includes a map of the Sixteen Warriors headquarters.
They've got lots of supplies there, and he says Gromov has been gone a lot lately. This is the perfect opportunity.
He will sell you out, if he gets out alive... you'll have every policeman in Ursus on your tail, even if you manage to get out of Katorga. Do we really want to meet again in court?
At least we share the common goal of liberating this raion right now. We can argue about the rest later.
Assaulting their headquarters is no easy task. We are willing to work with you, but we'll need to rest and regroup. Perhaps—
Understood. Once we are all set, we will move out and have Pavlo lead the way.
What do you think, Antosha?
Bring plenty of guys, Sonya. Do not underestimate him.
...Sonya?
Shh. I don't want to wake them up.
I just wanted to... get some rest by the fire.
You've done a huge service for the people here. But I'm still not sure if I'm a leader worthy of any of that.
When I got back to Ursus, I thought about living a normal life back home, but all of us are still struggling in the mud, me and all the girls who follow me...
I've let a lot of people down, watched my friends die... soon, I'll be leading them on another journey.
Can we go back to our old lives? Or am I just gonna fail at everything...?
You've already achieved a lot, haven't you?
...Huh?
You can have half my beer. I haven't touched it yet.
Zima reflexively takes the cup and inhales the faint scent of wheat, while faint snoring rings in her ears.
She scans the peaceful sleeping faces, red and puffy, smacking their lips in their dreams... it is the most peaceful night they have had since they came to the quarantine zone.
Hm...
Half a cup, even if it's just half a cup...
Boss, take it easy.
Where is Pavlovich? Spit it out!
Why did those mudaki take my cannons? Why did they cut the supplies? I want an explanation!
The magistrate will be back soon. I'm sure it'll all sort itself out.
He gave us money, and those bodyguards he has—
Blyat! I don't need you to tell me that! Pizdets!
He picks up a chair and throws it into a corner, then hears a frail, frightened chirping.
...What's that?
Gromov lifts the velvet covering the box, revealing an elaborate cage and its resident, a brown beckbeast trembling in a corner.
Pavlovich's? He didn't take his stupid pet with him today...
You, wait outside.
Yes sir!
After his subordinate has left, Gromov grins, He will bring his arrogant employer down a peg.
Rough hands reach into the cage, put themselves around the poor little creature's neck, and twist...
Gromov! I didn't expect to see you here. I heard you were looking for me?
...Why are you staring at my beckbeast like that?
What is it doing here...?
We don't see each other for a few days, and you've already forgotten? How could I go without its companionship?
Uh...
Feeling jealous? Hah, I knew you loved small animals too.
There's another one in my office that's going to breed with this one. You can have one of the babies.
Where's your gratitude?
Don't worry about it.
I don't suppose you came for this. What has you in such a hurry?
Gromov takes one look at the bodyguards, all of them bigger than him, and swallows the profanities that he had intended to say.
Why did you cut our supplies, sir? We're having enough trouble handling those kids as it is.
Do you remember why I hired you to manage Katorga Raion, Gromov? You were the lowest bidder.
I hope you have not forgotten this excellent quality.
Then my cannons—
Do not mention them again. I wouldn't tell you, even if I knew.
This is noble business. Do your job!
Boss! We've got a problem!
What?
Th-The students found the 'Honor Room'!
Blyat! How's that possible?!
I just came from there! Sonya is gonna get in, if we don't send help!
Magistrate!
Assign half our security team to him.
Yes sir!
If anything goes wrong, I will feed your pieces to my beckbeast. You understand?
Now get lost!
...Exterior is clear. Cleaning up.
These guys can fight, but they have absolutely no discipline.
Are things going well on the General's side? She should be inside their HQ by now.
The Sixteen Warriors will fight tooth and nail to protect it. We need to get over there and back them up, fast.
Let's hope Gromov has some real food here. I've had enough of cans—
His smile freezes on his face. He sways and falls by the feet of his friends. There is a crossbow bolt straight through his chest.
Yeremey's eyes widen. He sees Gromov approach with a dozen massive brutes in tow.
Hurry! Stop them!
Blyat!
Die, mudak!
No!
Yeremey's steel pipe meets Yeremey's hamaxe, and he is sent flying like a balloon.
Yeremey! No!
Your turn, cherv.
Gromov...!
You will pay for your crimes, murderer!
I'll kill you or die trying!
Blood rushes up her throat, and she can speak no more.
With great effort, Nika turns her neck to look in Yeremey's direction. She sees her friends scrambling to form a line, while Gromov has already charged inside like a monster.
I knew it was a trap the moment you said you were going to bribe Gromov and get him to let us out.
But why did I go with you... Yeremey?
Govno, govno, govno!
It's not over yet... We can cut through the back—it's faster. My men must still be fighting inside.
I'm the only one who knows the passphrase to the Honor Room. I'll hand out the weapons inside and turn this around...
The door's just ahead—
I got the last one, General!
...Gromov?!
A brief silence, then Gromov leaps towards a machine on the wall.
Please speak the passphrase.
*Expletives*!
Passphrase incorrect.
Watch out! That button must be hiding something!
Matvey!
The bolt hits Gromov's left arm. He roars and manages to fend off his attackers by swinging his hamaxe.
Please speak the passphrase.
*Expletives*!
Passphrase incorrect.
*Ursine roar*!
Passphrase correct.
Welcome, brave Gromov, descendant of Igor Velikiy's sixteen bravest companions...
He whose will is unbreakable, heir to the unstoppable legendary hamaxe...
Before the recording can finish, Gromov has already charged through the facade, using the momentum to roll inside.
Leto's strike misses, destroying the annoying box instead.
*Bzz*... the Sixteen Warriors... usher... next golden age of Ursus!
Who d'you think you are?!
Gromov tries to reach out, but a crossbow bolt hits the wall in front of him, just an inch from his finger.
I recognize you, and you... the Unbound.
He jumps back and punches a brick on the wall, causing two transparent 'walls' to drop down between Gromov and the others.
I originally designed this 'prison' for Pavlovich. I never thought I'd be its first prisoner.
Did you think a single pane of glass would—
Zima punches the glass, only to be knocked back several steps.
Something's funny about this glass!
The Third Bureau's shiny new toy, a new type of material that not even the tsar has seen... makes you wonder, doesn't it? Who did they make it for?
Better find yourself a landship if you want to break it... haha!
Gromov sits down on the floor, panting, but relaxed enough to begin tying his shoelaces.
We don't have much time... reinforcements will be here any moment. The guys outside can't hold for long.
There must be a way!
The Sixteen Warriors... wait a minute!
Why are there two of the same hamaxes here in this room?
The sixteen heroes who fought alongside Igor Velikiy were the bravest and strongest warriors of their time...
The street thugs who took their name forged a hamaxe in imitation of the legendary weapon, only to find themselves unworthy, lacking the strength to lift the glorious weapon.
Therefore, Gromov put the 'authentic' weapon on display, and carries a replica.
You're crazy! No one can swing that thing!
You'll only hurt yourself!
Sonya, do you need help—
Botani's jaw drops as she watches Sonya smash the display glass and raise the hamaxe into the air. She can almost hear Sonya's bones creak at the stress.
Zima slowly walks towards the impregnable glass wall, dragging the hamaxe behind her.
No... no, no, no, no, no!
Looks like I'm more worthy than you...
Right?!
No!
This is for all the people you murdered, all the evil you've allowed, the judgment and punishment that you've dodged all this time... this is for pissing me off.
Any last words, Gromov?
How—How could you possibly lift it—
The words have hardly left his mouth before Zima brings the hamaxe down. In the brief moment that it takes to find its mark, Zima seems to feel it grow lighter in her hand.
No longer the stuff of legend, nor an artifact that should sit in a museum collecting dust, and certainly not the plaything of a murderer—
It is power.
The power to resist, to sweep aside obstacles, to cut open the path of life.
It has no opinion, no position, no intention, no emotion.
It is life's primal roar, the first drop of blood that the heart pumps with each beat. It ignores all the complicated things in this world. All it does is—
Fight!!!
Sonya... we're saved.
The thugs ran for the upper walls once they saw Gromov's remains.
Good work... I know everyone fought bravely.
Do a head count, take as many supplies as you can, and the fallen—
Sonya! Sonya! Over here!
Keep your people in check!
She can't stop me. No one can.
Your Well Born death will make Ursus a better place, Baron.
What are you saying—help me!
Calm down, Antosha!
...We had a deal, Antosha.
He gives us the location, we spare his life.
I told you, Sonya, I will not suffer any of these leeches to live. Whatever value they might offer can only extend their lives for a few hours.
Allow them to live, and it will be our friends who die. It will be the workers in the mines, the farmers in the wilderness.
At the moment of death, his pathetic life will offer its last worth, and atone for his sins.
No. You're wrong.
He only has value if he gets out alive. That'll tell the other opportunists like him that we can be reasoned with, that they can negotiate.
The empire isn't one big thing, it never was. This is how we'll trip them up, exploit their differences, and get what we want as fast and easy as we can.
And my goal is to see all oppression gone from Ursus, from all of Terra.
I swore upon the future of this land that I will break its spine with my own hands and await a new dawn upon its ruins.
I do not kill these leeches for vengeance. I kill them so that this teetering house of cards will collapse more cleanly.
Killing a former noble who has already lost everything, begging for his life like a beckbeast...
You think a death like that means anything?
All I know is that this is a country where the freedom of the wealthy is built upon the corpses of the poor.
Every one of them we kill is a life saved.
You're out to smash things, but you don't get that breaking stuff is just a means, not an end.
Rubble's not enough. We need unity. We need people, people who will stand with us and fight injustice when we need them most.
Really? Allowing a man like this to live is the greatest injustice to those he has exploited.
Enough, Sonya. Botani caught this man. It is your right to do with him as you please.
But, if you are willing to work with them, then this is where we part ways. The Unbound will work with you no longer.
Don't be stupid, Antosha!
You're burning bridges, hurting your own cause, and putting the people who follow you in danger!
The Unbound don't follow me. I am simply their advisor.
All of us have gathered here of our own volition, to act in every corner in Ursus where oppression exists, to help those who suffer fight back against the cruelty of the nobility.
Anyone is free to leave, if they don't agree with me. Anyone can remove me.
Antosha turns around to seek Matvey's gaze.
This is a habit that he developed when they left school together, whenever he says something, goes somewhere, or kills someone.
Matvey always casts a supporting gaze from behind, helping him affirm that he is sober, and walking the right path.
Even Ukusik knows that Matvey will tell Antosha when he goes wrong.
But now—
There is no one there.
There you are, Matvey.
Yes.
Matvey is standing in the snow. He takes a bloody cigarette and puts it in his mouth, only to cough violently at the acrid smoke.
...I never knew you smoked.
I never knew you killed for the sake of killing.
Some of them may be criminals who have yet to be judged. But they are not monsters doomed to be slain.
You unleashed violence upon them, but allowed them to escape judgment... law and order have no place in your heart.
...You've told me that dozens of times. But there's no better way to uphold justice for the ordinary man. Unless you—
No, Antosha.
You are an aristocrat, and an Ursine. Every time I saw you kill someone, I couldn't help but wonder if they were actually men, just like you.
But you never gave anyone else the same opportunity you had.
Matvey puts the burning cigarette in the snow, with the others that have fallen upon the white, soaked and crushed beneath the heels of passersby.
Then he turns around, walking the path from whence he came.
...I didn't kill Pavalo.
But Matvey is already far away.
Antosha... are you fighting with Matvey?
No. Don't ask questions like this.
Then... can I go and see Rosalind tonight? She told me she'd tell me stories about her time in Kjerag after we beat Gromov.
No, don't go there.
What about tomorrow?
Not tomorrow either, Ukusik. Don't go there anymore.
But aren't we gonna fight together to tear down that wall?
We will...
But Sonya has her path, and we have ours.
We will learn which is the right one.
At any price.
What are you doing, Fedya?
A head count, and preparing food for tomorrow.
Head count... how many did we lose?
At least several. Possibly dozens. Some are still being treated.
I was happy that I finally did something that was absolutely right... but in the end—
Things didn't seem to get better. We lost so many friends... and split with Antosha's group...
Did I really make things better for people, Fedya, like that voice from the Far North? Even just a little bit?
You mean that criminal wanted for illegal broadcasting?
...Yes. You did the right thing.
But I don't think you need me to judge what you've done.
Fyodor lights the campfire that has been out for a while.
He digs out a lonely potato lying in an ash heap, puts a wooden skewer through it, and begins to roast it.
Because what really matters isn't what I say... but how you view yourself.
Should I consider that a lecture?
I don't know... maybe you're right. No. Maybe I'm right.
That night, we sat together by the fireside and roasted potatoes just like this.
That was the first time you joined the circle of students, chatting with them, talking politics, discussing literature...
That was the first time I saw with my own eyes the people I only knew by voice.
It was wonderful...
...Your efforts were never futile.
Yes.
I was the voice on the headset. I think I'll continue to be that.
Thanks, Fedya!
Huh?
'That night, we sat together by the fireside and roasted potatoes just like this...'
Pencil Stub...
Yeremey...
Nika...
Shorty...
This is for you.
Fyodor's hands cannot stop trembling. The hands that gave the chervontsy to Shorty...
The hands that saved lives...
The hands that wrought countless deaths...
Fyodor cannot describe his feelings in words. He can feel his excitement, and genuine fear...
By the time Fyodor wakes from his reverie, the campfire has been reduced to a small lick of flame, trembling in the darkness.
One side of the potato is burnt, while the other side is still raw.
'Tomorrow will come'...
Such a simple prayer.

eps.name: Two Ends of a Dead Knot

lines.loc: Rhodes Island Provisional Office, Deity GrypherburgOne week before the Winter Ball

lines.x: Dur-nar, I brought my report—
...Dur-nar?
There is no sign of any person, only a scene of utter chaos. Crownslayer forces her way through the multitude of cardboard boxes.
What a mess... I can hardly see the floor.
Dur-nar—
Is there somebody there?
Instructor Dur-nar's not here. You can give the report to me.
Oh, it's you.
Where's Dur-nar?
Not sure. I just got back a few days ago. Lada—I mean, Gummy and I are the only ones here.
We only just got approval to set up the new office, so the others are probably busy with red-tape and whatever. I'm heading out, too, in a bit; there's a Student Assembly letter that I need to send—
Here's my report. Please give it to her.
Okay.
Just a sec.
What is it?
Uh...
You're always on your own. I guess you're not really into talking to us, but we're all from Ursus, and now we're all Rhodes Island operators.
Everything's starting from scratch with this new office. I was thinking maybe we could get more done by helping each other out.
...What do you want?
That's not what I mean! What I'm trying to say is, if you need something, feel free to ask for help from the office, from any of us. You don't have to do everything yourself.
Of course, we'll ask if we need your help.

Instructor Dur-nar says the only contact you get with anybody is submitting your reports. Not that there's anything wrong with doing your own thing, but I thought I might check in with you, since you're here.
You wouldn't want me to show up here more.
Don't try to decide what I think. I know you had something to do with Chernobog and Reunion, but I don't know what you did, and I'm not about to find out.
It's a wound that keeps getting reopened, but trying to avoid it won't help it heal either.
The important thing is that you're on our side, and we can use as many people on our side as we can get.
So, yeah, if you ever find yourself in need of help, just give us a call.
Hey!
Thank you.
I will, if I need it.

lines.loc: Academy Riverside Police Station, Deity GrypherburgDec 24, 7:45 A.M.

lines.x: Lyudmila!
...I was just going to put in your bail.
Well, you can thank that kind soul for saving us the bail money!
How did you get out? And what was that explosion just now...?
—Run—
After them—!
Nothing to see here, just another ordinary afternoon in Grypherburg.
Never mind that for now, I better get out of here in case the cops show up, or I'll be back in that hole.
Don't go back yet. Come with me. I have questions.
How did you know the cops got me? I thought I was gonna rot in there for sure.
Someone saw the cops questioning you. You remember the kid who lives across the street?
Kid? The redhead? I remember I didn't like that brooding look of his—
Don't judge people by appearances. Have you sold all your goods?
There was one who didn't meet with me. I was waiting for him when I got arrested. Bloke from Odoyev... what's his name again?
Rus, occupation: barber. Lives on Fifth Avenue. Two infants at home, wife died of flu complications.
Yes... that's the one. I got everyone else.
How did they pay for the energy converters?
Huh? I thought they didn't have to pay? They get the energy converters for free as long as they keep buying the goods from us.
Correct.
You were testing me! You trust me that little?
People who are trustworthy don't usually end up in jail.
Come on, let's not talk about that!
Were you concerned that me or someone else might be selling the energy converters behind your back?
Not gonna happen. Everyone's in your debt. We'd all be frozen solid without you. We have nothing but gratitude towards you—

No, I understand some of you would like to make more money, but you should not do it by exploiting people who are in even more need than you are. That's not what I wanted to see when I chose to sell through you guys.
I have other channels, but I chose to work with you instead of working on my own. You should understand that all it does is add extra risk.
Honestly, I don't understand why you're doing this... you're just doing good by people with nothing in it for you.
I've dealt with Rus's case, but we need to put the recruitment of new clients on hold for now. I'll let you know when there are any updates.
Oh? Will our supplies be cut?
Our reserves can meet the needs of existing users for about two weeks. I'll try to get supply restored during this time.

If any new clients show up, use discretion and due diligence, and help out where you can with the money that I gave you, but don't tell them about the supply chain issues. We don't want to cause panic.
Of course, I trust you... anything I can help with?
No, this is my responsibility. I might be away for a few days. Find some excuse if anyone asks.
Thank you.
Sure, but how do I reach you if something happens?
Come here and leave a note, just like I taught you.
Lyudmila! Haven't seen you down here for a while. Are you going outside the city?
Yes, I have something to do. Is there an unguarded exit ahead?
No, but they won't give you any trouble if they see you.
Any suspicious intruders from the mobility layer recently?
No. Police patrols have dropped too. If you're asking which exit has no cops watching, it's the same answer as usual. They only come at fixed hours; we keep a watch the rest of the time.
Good, thank you.
Come back soon!
I think this is the place...
Crownslayer kneels and wipes away the dust, revealing an etched mark on the floor.
She looks up and sees identical emergency ladders neatly installed between the layers. She climbs one of them and goes deeper into the mobility layer.
Can you hear me?
Hello?
Is it safe on your side?
This is a new safehouse. It's been checked for mics and cameras.
Good. I don't have much time...
...Are you alright?
Not great, but that's not important. They may have found out about us transferring energy to Grypherburg. I haven't faced any consequences yet...
They've updated their base stations. It's likely that they'll be building new energy pipelines next, then abandon the old one. We need to make a couple of preparations before that.
You planning to tap the new pipeline?
We must.
The original pipeline was already basically a dedicated Tsarevgrad one. Now they're probably going to pave it straight to the palace. They don't even care about the other nobles anymore.
They say it's to 'conserve resources', but how is it not a waste to keep building pipelines that could be destroyed by Catastrophe any moment?
I heard workers are already being reassigned over here. Anything of the sort from Grypherburg?
No... Grypherburg is dealing with its own problems.
You mean the students—
Although news about the ore exhaustion got out, what you're researching has bought the council time. The Fourth Army also had to dealt with internal unrest of its own...
Nobles, soldiers, workers, no one is making any rash moves right now, except for these students who are completely ignorant of the currents under the surface.
Oh, I'm not accusing you. But if you could tell me more about what you're researching—
Let's talk about the topic at hand first. The old pipeline should remain in service until the new one is complete, but we'll need to find a different way to communicate.
If I recall correctly, your comms are using a foreign company's independent network?
Yes, a rental base station operated by a foreign-owned company in Ursus.
That's the problem. Even foreign-owned companies are potentially subject to intense surveillance, especially after the Far North Broadcast.
Not even if we use a new anonymous channel each time?

The base stations on my end have been updated. Hard to tell if someone might have added new 'features'. Can you find radio equipment with an independent network, one that doesn't use a commercial base station?
You're talking about high-level military equipment? That might take some time.
Try. If you succeed, you can continue to reach me on this channel.
If you don't... you may have to wait for me to find an opportunity to contact you from my end. If you don't hear from me in two weeks, destroy all evidence of ever having communicated with me.
...We'll all do our best.
Take care.
You too.

lines.loc: Rhodes Island Provisional Office, Deity GrypherburgDays after the Winter Ball

lines.x: I really can't go out to help?
Leto just went out after leaving a letter. Istina and the others don't come back to the office much either. Don't they need my help?
Zima was taken away because she tried to help me, but I couldn't do anything—
I know you're worried, Gummy, but someone needs to stay here to deal with the office's work until the next group of operators arrive in Grypherburg.
Building a new Oripathy treatment center, assisting the government with the registration and monitoring of Oripathy patients... there's a lot to do.
Besides, we're making sure that they can focus on whatever it is they have to do.
I know it's important, but I'm the only one who's not helping rescue Zima...
I don't want to be like that. They wouldn't have gotten Zima if I wasn't being dumb that night!
I know how you feel, Little Cub, but I promised Istina to protect—
Is Zima in?
Huh?
The cops took Zima—oh, Crownslayer!
...You can call me Lyudmila. What do you mean, the cops took Zima?
Govno, I should have come sooner. Do you know where she is? How can I help?
Zima is in the quarantine zone. We're making plans to rescue her.
The quarantine zone? Katorga Raion? That's basically Pavlovich's own little fiefdom. What can you—what can Rhodes do?
The Ursus Student Self-Government Group... the children are trying to rescue their own.
But I'm not helping! Zima's in there because of me, and there's nothing I can do...
You're sure Zima's being held in the quarantine zone?
Rosa has confirmed it through multiple sources, and she's apparently seen Pavlovich herself.
But she couldn't get Zima out... or rather, Zima doesn't want to leave.
Zima doesn't want to leave?
Why do you say that—
A hunch.

Do you have any advanced communicators here that run on their own network without using a commercial base station? I've asked all my contacts, but there's no one selling this stuff, even on the black market.
Sounds like something that only the military will have, or folks like Closure who like to fiddle with things on their own.
Most branch offices will not have something of that grade without making a special application. Why do you need it?
Saving lives.
Rosa said there's a radio blackout on the quarantine zone. Even those communicators won't work.
(Lowers voice) No, I need to contact the one who's helping me steal electricity.
My communications there may be compromised. I need a more secure method.
Steal—
Steal electricity?!
Not so loud.
So you're the one behind the cheap energy in the city these days.
I had a lot of help.
Well, I guess I shouldn't be so surprised. You came to Ursus before us, and you were the one who built our intelligence network in the Central Governorate.
I'll be going if there's no such communicator at the office. Take care of yourselves. I'll see what I can do about Zima.
You take care too. Stay hidden.
(Mutters) Communicator... communicator?
What?
I remember now!
The listening device that we used on the day of the ball was a student's handiwork. Zima said she built her very own set of radio equipment—
Where is this student now?
...I don't know. Zima got the stuff, I guess she's the only one who knows them.

eps.name: Two Ends of a Dead Knot

lines.x: If you want to come with me, you do exactly as I say throughout the whole thing.
Do you understand?
Yes! Hehe...
What are you laughing at?
It's just, you're so dependable, Lyudmila.
Don't say things you can't take back.
When did you two become such good friends? I guess I never should've worried that you wouldn't get along.
She's different. We met each other in the Rhodes Island canteen.
Oh, is that why? At the canteen—
Ah! So you're the red-haired lady who makes great Ursine and Siracusan food!
Back on topic. My Arts can conceal my movements. I'll go and find Zima first; it won't be hard if Rosa's coordinates are accurate.
Rosa reports that the situation in the quarantine zone is in flux. It's possible that Zima's base of operations may have moved. Go ahead and check it out, but come back if things don't work out.
Mm-hm.
Why can't we go together?
Pavlovich's people control the mobility layer passages since the lockdown. We'll alert them if we go on together. You have to wait here.
This area is outside Katorga Raion, and all the workers know me. If anyone comes over, just tell them you're with Lyudmila Ilyinichna.
Understood, but it's best not to be detected. We'll stay hidden and wait for your signal.
When you see Zima, see if she's hurt, if she's gotten thinner—
I'll do my best.
No patrols? That's different from the reports.
Sonya's camp should be just ahead.
...If you don't want me to talk to Matvey, I won't. You want to be by yourself, I won't bother you.
But holler if you need someone to talk to, okay?
I'm here for you. Don't put everything on your own shoulders.
What the...?
Rosalind—
Don't yell. It's me.
Huh?
You told me to find you if I ever needed help, didn't you?
So I came.
The comms equipment looks good.
So you've dealt with the thugs from within the wall, and you're preparing to leave.
No wonder I didn't see a soul on my way here.
The thugs on the ground might be done for, but the ones on the walls are still up there. We have a tough fight ahead of us.
Are you ready for it?
We have to think we are. I don't have time or energy to ask every one of them what they think, but the fact that they haven't stopped training is enough.
I'm not questioning any of you. Based on what I know from the outside, it's a miracle that you're alive at all, much less united and fighting.
What are they saying out there?
That it's His Majesty Pavlovich's little kingdom, and he alone decides what lives and what dies within.
The nobles don't care anymore. After all, this plate is going be discarded like cutting away a piece of rotten flesh, along with everyone on it.
Hmph.
That's how Ursus is, how it always has been... yet those who are abandoned end up struggling to survive.
Amiya didn't want us to have too much contact with you. I never knew you were so sentimental.
It's not about sentimentality...

Let me put it another way. On my way here, I saw someone huddled by a campfire crying, being comforted by someone who was smiling. Their arms were bandaged, and they were as dirty as the snow on the ground.
Some were chatting, some were holding steaming cups of water, some were roasting things over the fire.
They've been through so many things in a place like this, yet they didn't look like they're in pain. Really, they looked like they were looking forward to tomorrow.
They had nothing but the hope in their hearts. I've seen this scene before, the same expressions on faces before, in...
Thanks for sharing.
But we're really short on supplies. Every day might be our last. This cup of tea here could be too. If you don't want it, I do.
Crownslayer says nothing, but gestures for her counterpart to go ahead.
The plainly exhausted young woman does not demur. She lifts the steel cup and downs its contents, tea that has been brewed so many times it hardly has any color left.
...I've told you all the important parts. Anything you want to know before you leave?
Is there anything I can help with before I go?
Well... maybe it's a dumb question.
But do you think maybe you could use your Arts to get these students out the way you came in?
The mobility layer passage is very narrow. We could maybe get a few dozen out in a night, but you have hundreds... Besides, There is only one way to the passage.
They are bound to notice your move of this size. If the students get caught out in the open, even with my Arts, we won't stand a chance once those thugs start raining fire down on us—
Forget I said anything. Should've known it wasn't so simple.
Other than that, is there anything I can do?
I thought you were going to ask me if I wanted to escape with you.
Didn't bother. You're not leaving.
Damn straight.
Actually, there IS something you can do. You said you came in through the mobility layer. I take it you're familiar with what's down there...
Talk about bad luck?
