I guess you're in here by accident. You don't look like the kind of man who would associate with the elements here.
Ah... yes, you're right. This was quite an absurd accident.
What are you doing?
Just memorializing fallen friends.
I'm sorry. You look sad. I hope I'm not interrupting you.
Oh, it's perfectly alright. I'm used to being interrupted.
Be my guest, sit down by the fire and get some warmth. There are roasted potatoes, if you're hungry... what's your name?
My name is Lyudmila... but my friends call me Crownslayer.
...That's a cool nickname.
Have you... slain any particularly important crowns?
Sadly, not yet. But I've seen many tyrants, or should I say, leaders.
The first was in Ursus. She was a remarkable woman, one of the most remarkable I've ever met. She was powerful, and a charismatic leader.
But her ideals were too distant, and her methods too idealistic. That's why she failed. Maybe it's not quite fair to call her a tyrant. She was just one of the many who fell by the wayside.
The second was in Siracusa. She wasn't even a leader when I first met her. She was a good person, and an unlucky one.

She became a leader after a strange twist of fate, and tasted power before she realized the importance of responsibility. I was worried she would go astray, but we're destined to go our separate ways.
You've seen a lot. I envy you. I've never even left Grypherburg.
As for the third, I've only ever heard his name and deeds.
I've never seen him with my own eyes—until now.
Who sent you? You don't look like one of Witte's.
Don't bother guessing. I'm not after you.

What an experience it is, to come back to Ursus after all this while, only to experience something as crazy as this. I guess the State Council's freaking out right about now, trying to get you out without causing a scene.
Perhaps. Or perhaps someone wants me to die in here quietly.
I don't know. I don't think it really makes a difference whether I'm here or in the palace.
The commoners hate you, the nobility looks down on you. How do you even manage that?
When you try to change something, the people whose cake gets moved do all they can to oppose you. People take turns opposing all the different decisions you make.
Never mind... you wouldn't understand.
I wouldn't. You sound like you think you're doing your best to govern your country. How did Ursus end up like this, then?
You said you've never left Grypherburg? You should. Go out there, and see what this empire of yours really looks like under your rule.
That's enough!!!
I don't need your ridicule... don't think I don't know what's wrong with the empire. I want to change it too.
You don't know how hard I've tried. No one does. But what can I do, if no one ever truly supports me?
So what? Are you saying it's everybody else's fault, and you're just a sweet, innocent little tsar?
You want your suffering people to empathize with how hard things are for you, when you don't even understand your own responsibility?
Fine. You're right, I'm a terrible tsar. What are you waiting for, then?
Kill me already. Fulfill the wishes of the nobles who want me dead, and make the commoners who hate me happy.
Then you'll no longer be a little girl who gave herself a stupid khuyovy nickname, but a true crownslayer at last.
Snap out of it, svolotsch!
Killing you would be easy, but what would that achieve? You think Fyodor matters? Not even a little bit, I tell you.
Every kid in Ursus has heard the story of how the tsar put down the Great Rebellion at the age of ten. Do you think they know what kind of mudak sits on the throne?
Do you think your deeds bring glory to the name Fyodor? You don't understand your own responsibility, yet you're complaining as though everything under the sun is doing you an injustice.
You're simply a kid who never grew up, living a lie that all the people around you keep spinning for you.
Yebat—
Are you really mourning the people you saw die? Tragedies like these and much worse happen every day in Ursus. Do you really mourn them?
If you really want to save people, go back to where you should be, find a few decrees that do the right thing, and put your signature and stamp on them.
Is it so hard? The question is, do you really want to do it? Do you know what the right thing is?
I regret inviting you to my campfire.
I don't like to be vulgar, but there are always people who want to make me angry.
Thank you for the invitation, Your Imperial Majesty.
I pray your generosity will reach further.
Where are you going?
None of your business.
Don't worry, you want to keep indulging in your little game here, that's your choice. I won't tell anyone.
There's just one thing I'll say...

If you were really trying so hard to bring about change, then the palace wouldn't be the only place that's still lit at night, while the rest of Ursus put together doesn't have enough candles to illuminate Grypherburg.
As Crownslayer departs, a gust of wind extinguishes what is left of the campfire before Fyodor.
Darkness falls, leaving the silent tsar and the wanderer in the cold night.
I know you're there. Show yourself.
Your Imperial Majesty.
...Why am I not surprised that you followed me here?
Your will and that of Chairman Witte was to avoid any further disturbances arising from your disappearance.
We therefore had to remain hidden.
And? What's Witte planning to do with Katorga?
That is not for us to know.
If you wish to speak to him, you should return to the palace with us immediately.
You want to bring me back, quietly put me in a car, then put me back on that chair.
I'm telling you, no.
You should understand your own situation.
You are too young, and too willful, compared to the old tsar.
Idi na hui! Do not compare me with a man who's been dead for ages! Get out of my sight!
I'm not leaving. I have things to do. I am not a mannequin for Ursus to display in the shop window.
Tell Witte that if he wants me to leave here, he can come pick me up himself.
They're gone...
Over here!
You ran into workers on patrol?
If 'workers' are people dressed like policemen and carrying machetes and sticks, then yes.
You ran into Pavlovich's people? But this isn't Katorga, they shouldn't—
It was a few guys in worker garb that helped us hide. But they left in a hurry, and I didn't get any information from them.
What about Zima? Did you see her? Is she and Leto alright?
Zima, Leto and the students they gathered are planning to leave the quarantine zone, maybe in the next couple of days.
Leave? Did that Pavlovich let them go?
Not the kind of leaving where you just open the door and walk out.
What are they planning? Can we help?
I asked the same question. Anyway, I'll talk to the workers on duty in the mobility layer tonight.
First, I need to try the comms equipment that Zima gave me, or those unemployed workers will soon lose electricity and heat.
Where do we try?
I don't have a safehouse in this area. We need to find somewhere more remote.
This will do.
The gear's heavy. I'll hold it; you take the headset.
Thanks.
What about me? Is there anything I can do?
Keep watch. Tell us if there's any movement.
Alright!

We'll put out the fire first, then worry about the rest. Watch me—
...Sonya?
Hah.... hah....
Wh-Why don't you come in?

Can you put down the match? At least don't point it at the fuse—
Never!
...What about the people that Captain brought?

No! What do you know?! I... I can't end up like that. I'd rather—

Hrrah—
She raises her arm, for the voices trapped in her throat, and a gushing crack appears in the marble pedestal.
Follow Sonya!
Smash it, topple it! Grypherburg lies before us!
Here I come!

Don't just stand there, Fedya! Give us a hand!
He peers up at the statue, once awe-inspiring, now trembling and teetering, his heart trembling along with the sound of every hit.

Ura—
Magistrate!
Gosudar-batyushka—
Igor's pieces come thundering down on his head as he mutters his last words.

Someone's running! More Sixteen Warriors ahead!
Get them! Make them pay for their crimes!
For Ursus!
Igor's sword falls upon the wall, the authority wrought from stone shattered to pieces.

Zima's speech last night echoes in their minds.
...They told us to be ordinary.

For all the children of Ursus who will not kneel!

I, I was the only one who made it out alive. Everyone else—
(Sobs)

Keep your emotions in check, sir. The committee needs more details.

Yes.

Liar!

...Police, remove the child from the room.

...How many casualties this time?

Sonya. Rosalind.
Antosha?

Take this and press it against your chest. You'll be fine.

Yeah.

Almost—

Remember, Antosha?
I'm the nimblest amongst us.

Then, Matvey—
No... no...

No. Say no more.

You must defeat me.
What?!

Pave the path to your new order with my dead body.

Enough is enough.

Ukusik...

Your Imperial Majesty!
Witte?

Students... friends, comrades!
